title: Totally abolished discernment: judge first, or establish non-responsibility first?
description: World map in Mollweide projection classifying criminal-law systems by the procedural fate of an accused whose discernment was totally abolished by a mental disorder at the time of the act: the trial comes first (green), non-responsibility is established first without a real trial (yellow), non-responsibility is established first but a trial still takes place (purple), the accused chooses when the mental state is examined (blue), no non-responsibility is recognised (black), no data or outside the scope (white).
subtitle: Serious crime (e.g. homicide), discernment totally abolished at the time of the act · partial impairment and plea bargaining ignored · law in force on 28 October 2026
subtitle_2: OECD (excl. Turkey), Americas (excl. Cuba), Oceania, Africa (excl. Maghreb, Egypt, Eritrea, Sahel other than Senegal, Mauritania), Balkans (excl. Serbia), Ukraine, Moldova (controlled areas), Asia (selection, incl. UAE)
marker_note: Circle: state too small to be visible at this scale (same colour as on the map). Hover over a country: legal basis, nuances and confidence level.
footer: Method: legal research in each country's official language(s) (penal codes, codes of criminal procedure, case law) by 24 agents, a second verification pass on weak entries, then an independent check of high-stakes entries. Sources, excerpts and confidence of each entry: accompanying JSON file.

White: procedural text not found or unreadable (hypothesis in the tooltip), countries excluded from the scope, countries and territories not studied. Where two routes coexist, the ordinary route of the reference scenario is used; routes based on agreement of the parties are treated like a plea.
Line of control in Ukraine on 28/10/2026: DeepStateMap (daily data, cyterat/deepstate-map-data repository); Transnistria: Natural Earth administrative units; base map: Natural Earth (world-atlas).

green.label: Judge first
legend: No pretrial gate: the ordinary trial establishes the facts, then the trial court finds
the accused not responsible and itself orders the treatment or security measure.
green.definition: No prior gateway: the case goes to an ordinary trial; the trial court first establishes the facts, then rules on non-responsibility (acquittal, exemption, special verdict) and itself orders the measure. The psychiatric examination is ordered by the authorities or the court, not at the accused's choice.

yellow.label: Non-responsibility first, no real trial
legend: Mental state examined before any trial: dismissal (non-lieu), or a reduced procedure replacing the trial
(France since 2008: hearing before the investigating chamber). Trial only if the accused is found responsible.
yellow.definition: The mental state at the time of the act is examined during the pretrial phase; if discernment was abolished, the case ends without a real trial, either through a dismissal or a decision not to commit for trial, or through a reduced procedure that replaces the trial (hearing before an investigating court, in chambers, a non-public care tribunal, a written or simplified procedure, a lower standard of proof, absence of the accused as the rule). The person may nonetheless be committed. A trial only takes place if the person is found responsible.

purple.label: Non-responsibility first, but a trial
legend: Mental state examined first, routing the case to a special track, but a real trial (adversarial hearing
before the trial judge, same evidence) always precedes the measure, or takes place at the accused's request.
purple.definition: Non-responsibility is examined first and diverts the case into a special procedure, but the trial court holds a genuine hearing on the merits with the guarantees of an ordinary criminal trial (oral adversarial hearing, full taking of evidence on the facts, same standard of proof) before any measure, or the accused can obtain a full trial on request despite the abolition of discernment.

blue.label: The accused chooses the timing
legend: The defence decides whether and when mental state is examined (before, during or after the trial);
the prosecution or the judge cannot impose it on a fit accused (e.g. Canada, R. v. Swain).
blue.definition: The defence controls whether and when the mental state at the time of the act is examined: before trial, at its end (e.g. a mental-health phase that the defence chooses to open) or after the verdict. The prosecution or the court cannot impose the examination or the non-responsibility defence on a fit accused, or only after a guilty verdict.

black.label: No non-responsibility recognised
legend: Neither a special verdict nor committal in lieu of a sentence:
every convicted person goes to prison, even if their discernment was abolished.
black.definition: The law recognises no form of non-responsibility for mental disorder: no defence or special verdict, no acquittal or exemption with committal, no committal ordered in lieu of a sentence; every convicted person goes to prison (possibly with treatment in detention).

white.label: No data / outside the scope
legend: Insufficient data (procedural text not found or unreadable), countries and areas excluded from the scope (Maghreb, Egypt,
Sahel except Senegal and Mauritania, Eritrea, Cuba, Turkey, Serbia, occupied Ukraine, Transnistria: dashed), countries not studied.
white.definition: Insufficient reliable data to classify, countries excluded from the scope by choice (lack of rule of law: the law there is only a hint, not a requirement to follow), or countries and territories not studied.

methodology.question: When an accused whose discernment was totally abolished by a mental disorder at the time of the act is prosecuted for a serious crime, is non-responsibility established before a trial (which then does not take place, or not really), during the trial, at the accused's choice, or is it not recognised at all?
methodology.reference_scenario: An adult is prosecuted for a serious crime (for example a homicide). The psychiatric evidence indicates that at the time of the act a mental disorder (for example an acute psychosis) totally abolished their discernment or control over their acts; they need secure care.
method_exclusions: Partial impairment of discernment (diminished responsibility): ignored.
Guilty pleas and other plea bargaining: ignored (the accused is assumed to be always able to demand a trial).
Fitness to stand trial (state at the time of trial): distinct from non-responsibility (state at the time of the act); always described in the entry, never used for the colour.
The prosecution's mere power to drop a case (discretionary prosecution) is not enough for yellow.
A non-criminal care hearing (non-public care tribunal, administrative or civil commitment) is never “the trial”.
classification_order: 2. blue: the accused chooses whether and when the mental state is examined.
3. yellow: prior examination and end of the case without a real trial (dismissal, or a reduced procedure replacing the trial, e.g. France since the Act of 25 February 2008).
4. purple: prior examination but a real trial before any measure, or a full trial at the accused's request.
5. green: no prior gate; ordinary trial, then finding of non-responsibility.
6. white: insufficient data or outside the scope.
methodology.federalism: For federal states, one entry per federated unit when the rule is sub-national (United States, Australia, United Kingdom, Argentina, Kerala…), otherwise a single national entry.
methodology.languages: Each agent searched first in the country's official language(s), with the native legal terms; English or French were only used as complements. The research_languages field gives the languages actually used. The English edition is a translation of the French working edition; excerpts stay verbatim in their original language.
process: First pass: 24 research agents, one group of countries each, sources read in the official language(s) (penal codes, codes of procedure, case law).
Second pass: 26 verification groups targeting low-confidence entries, borderline cases and federated states (Argentine provinces, US states, Australia, United Kingdom, India).
Third, targeted look at procedure in francophone Africa: without a readable procedural text, the entry turns white (no classification by analogy with the French model).

Independent check of 38 high-stakes entries (28, then 10 after the extension) by agents who had not produced the entries: 37 confirmed, 1 found doubtful (Peru, security trial held in camera, kept purple).

Manual decisions by the coordinator (merge_decision field): Saint Pierre and Miquelon (legislative identity verified), Brazil (CPP art. 415), Peru (in camera), Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (ZKP FBiH arts. 231 and 410).

Extension of 28/10 in the evening: 12 agents (then a second, targeted look at Albania and North Macedonia) for 28 new jurisdictions, with the same requirement: a colour only if the decisive procedure was read.

Texts supplied by the user (28/10, 22:38): Macedonian Code of Criminal Procedure of 2010 (OSCE translation), Malagasy code (UNODC copy) and Act 2016-017, codes of Entre Ríos (consolidated Act 9754), La Pampa (Act 3192, STJ 2021 edition) and La Rioja (Act 1574); they made it possible to classify North Macedonia (purple), Madagascar, Entre Ríos, La Pampa and La Rioja (yellow).
methodology.white_criterion: A colour is only assigned if the decisive procedural mechanism (who decides, at what stage, in what kind of hearing) was read in a primary source (statute, decision) or in reliable scholarship quoting it; otherwise the entry stays white and the hypothesis is kept (hypothetical_colour field).
methodology.asia_scope: Asia (selection): India (and Kerala), Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, the Philippines, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macao, Mongolia, Kazakhstan, Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, as well as Japan, South Korea and Israel (OECD).
methodology.extension_28_10: Extension of 28/10/2026 (21:00): Egypt removed (criminal procedure deemed a hint rather than a requirement); 13 Asian countries or territories, Mauritania, the Balkans except Serbia and the remaining Pacific island territories added; Senegal re-checked.
methodology.extension_28_10_bis: Extension of 28/10/2026 (22:00): Sri Lanka, Madagascar (second attempt), Ukraine (government-controlled territory) and Moldova (except Transnistria), one agent per country; Albania and North Macedonia relaunched separately. Occupied Ukrainian territories (line of control on 28/10/2026 according to the daily DeepStateMap data, cyterat/deepstate-map-data repository) and Transnistria (Natural Earth administrative units) drawn white with dashes.
methodology.extension_28_10_ter: Additions of 28/10/2026 (23:00): texts supplied by the user (North Macedonia, Madagascar, Entre Ríos, La Pampa, La Rioja); 9 Legal Data Hunter queries run one at a time, without agents, on the jurisdictions still white (Albania and Mauritania classified; Guinea, Rwanda, Zanzibar and Brčko still white; daily quota reached); United Arab Emirates added through web research, without Legal Data Hunter (Federal Decree-Laws No. 31 of 2021 and No. 38 of 2022, official portal).
methodology.scope_criterion: An authoritarian regime is not excluded as such: some authoritarian countries keep, for ordinary criminal cases, a justice system in which the law on defence rights is still followed (corruption aside); they are included. Excluded are those where the lack of rule of law means that the law is only a hint, not a requirement to follow.
methodology.english_edition: English edition produced on 28/10/2026 from the French working edition: notes, outcomes, legal bases and source titles translated; statutory quotations and native legal terms kept in the original language. This English file is the dataset maintained in the repository; the French edition (data/fr/irresponsabilite_penale.json) is the original of 28/10/2026 and prevails for that date in case of a translation discrepancy.

contributing: See CONTRIBUTING.md. Pull requests may only modify the JSON data (data/insanity_procedure_map.json); maps are regenerated from it.

A colour other than white requires the decisive procedural mechanism (who decides, at what stage, in what kind of hearing) to be read in a primary source (statute, decision) or in scholarship quoting it; otherwise the entry stays white with a hypothetical_colour.
Give at least one source with a working URL, exact article numbers in legal_bases, and an excerpt of at most 25 words copied verbatim in the original language.

Describe the ordinary route for the reference scenario (adult, serious crime, discernment totally abolished at the time of the act); ignore diminished responsibility and plea bargaining; describe fitness to stand trial separately, it never decides the colour.

Scope: an authoritarian regime is not excluded as such if, in ordinary criminal cases, the law on defence rights is still followed (corruption aside); jurisdictions where the lack of rule of law makes the law only a hint, not a requirement, stay out of scope (white).

entities.name: France

facts.outcome: Declaration of criminal non-responsibility without trial, by order of the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) (706-120 para. 3) or by decision of the investigating chamber (chambre de l'instruction) (sufficient charges + disorder having abolished discernment, with a ruling on civil liability if the civil party so requests, 706-125); the investigating chamber (or the trial court) may order full-time hospitalisation (706-135) and security measures of 10 years, 20 years for a felony or a misdemeanour punishable by 10 years (706-136), without prejudice to the prefectoral route (CSP L. 3213-1 and L. 3213-7); committal for trial only if art. 122-1 para. 1 is ruled out (706-124).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The investigating judge (juge d'instruction) issues an order of criminal non-responsibility (706-120 para. 3) or, on request, the investigating chamber (chambre de l'instruction) rules at a public adversarial hearing on merely sufficient charges (706-122, 706-125), without trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Until 2026, stay of committal for trial as long as the person cannot defend themselves (Crim. 19 Sept. 2018, no. 18-83.868). Crim. 7 Oct. 2026 (no. 26-84.139, FS-BR, according to summaries) abandons this stay: committal ordered, then, if appearance is impossible on a lasting basis, public hearing limited to the civil action, with a lawyer representing the person (CPP 10 para. 4). Unfitness does not prevent the 706-119 et seq. procedure (appearance “si son état le permet” [if their condition so permits], 706-122).

entities.legal_bases: CP arts. 122-1 para. 1 (abolition of discernment), 122-1-1 and 122-1-2 (voluntary intoxication, Law 2022-52); CPP arts. 706-119 to 706-128 (investigating judge [juge d'instruction], investigating chamber [chambre de l'instruction]), 706-129 to 706-134 (assize court [cour d'assises], criminal court [tribunal correctionnel]), 706-135 to 706-139 (hospitalisation, security measures), 706-139-1 to 706-140; CPP art. 10 para. 4; Laws 2008-174, 2022-52, 2023-1059 (art. 13); Ordinance 2025-1091 (rewritten CPP, in force on 1.1.2029).
entities.excerpt: Elle déclare qu'il existe des charges suffisantes contre la personne d'avoir commis les faits qui lui sont reprochés
entities.note: Yellow confirmed. At the close of the investigation, the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) issues an order of criminal non-responsibility (706-120 para. 3) or, on request, the investigating chamber (chambre de l'instruction) rules at a public adversarial hearing (experts, civil party) on merely sufficient charges (706-122, 706-125), with treatment and security measures. Assize court (cour d'assises) only if 122-1 is ruled out. Amendments: Law 2022-52, 706-119 (2024); new CPP in 2029.

entities.name: Belgium

facts.outcome: Confinement (a security measure, not a penalty) ordered by the council chamber (chambre du conseil) at the settlement of the proceedings (or by the indictment chamber [chambre des mises en accusation] on appeal), in camera and without trial; enforcement (placement, arrangements) by the social protection chamber of the sentence enforcement court.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The council chamber (chambre du conseil) orders confinement in camera (public pronouncement), after hearing the charged person, assisted by a lawyer, and the civil party, on the basis of a forensic psychiatric expert examination, without committal for trial (2014 Law, arts. 9 and 13).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No inadmissibility of the prosecution: Cass., 23 Sept. 2020 holds that art. 6 ECHR does not require inadmissibility when the charged person can no longer follow the trial; the judge may establish the facts and order confinement (without penalty), the charged person being assisted or represented by a lawyer (art. 81, 2014 Law).

entities.legal_bases: Loi du 5 mai 2014 relative à l'internement: arts. 2 (security measure), 5 and 7 (forensic psychiatric expert examination), 9 §§ 1-2 (confinement by investigating and trial courts; mental disorder abolishing or seriously impairing discernment or control, risk of reoffending), 13-14 (council chamber [chambre du conseil], closed hearing, appeal to the indictment chamber [chambre des mises en accusation]), 15 (assize court [cour d'assises]), 19 et seq. (social protection chamber), 81 (lawyer); former CP art. 71, replaced by art. 25 of the new Code pénal (in force on 1.9.2026); C.i.cr. art. 127 et seq.
entities.excerpt: Les débats devant la chambre du conseil se déroulent à huis clos et le prononcé est public.
entities.note: Federal rule (single entry). At the settlement of the proceedings, the council chamber (chambre du conseil; appeal: indictment chamber [chambre des mises en accusation]) may order confinement in camera, after hearing the charged person and the civil party, without trial (≈68% of cases studied); no right to demand a trial found. Trial possible (assize court [cour d'assises], art. 15). New CP in force on 1.9.2026 (art. 25). Law read via preparatory works.

entities.name: Luxembourg

facts.outcome: Order of the council chamber (chambre du conseil) finding sufficient charges and criminal non-responsibility (art. 71 CP) and ordering judicial placement in an authorised establishment (socio-judicial psychiatry unit, Law of 10 December 2009), without trial; alternatively, acquittal with placement by the trial court.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The council chamber (chambre du conseil) of the district court (tribunal d'arrondissement) rules at the end of the investigation, in chambers, on the prosecution's submissions, the expert examination and the defence's written brief (CPP 127), and may order placement without committal to a trial court.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Not verified: no rule or decision on unfitness to stand trial found in the sources consulted; before the criminal court, the defendant may be represented by a lawyer (CPP 185(1), judgment of 15.1.2025), but the effect of lasting unfitness is not established.

entities.legal_bases: Code pénal art. 71 para. 1 (mental disorders having abolished discernment or control of one's actions) and para. 2 (placement if the danger persists), art. 71-1 (impairment, outside the scope); Code de procédure pénale (formerly Code d'instruction criminelle) art. 127 (settlement of the proceedings by the council chamber [chambre du conseil]) and art. 133 et seq. entities.note: Ordinary route for a clear case (abolition established by expert examination): the council chamber (chambre du conseil; appeal within 5 days) finds sufficient charges and non-responsibility, and orders placement, without trial (Diekirch order 26.9.2025; CA 2011). Parallel route: acquittal with placement at trial. No 2022-2026 reform found; unfitness not verified; text of art. 71 read via case law.

entities.name: Switzerland

facts.outcome: judgment finding that the act was committed in a state of non-responsibility (neither conviction nor acquittal) + institutional therapeutic measure (art. 59 CP) or confinement (art. 64 CP)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Independent procedure on the written application of the prosecution (ministère public) before the court of first instance, with a hearing governed by the ordinary first-instance rules (arts. 374-375 CPP).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Art. 114 CPP: temporary incapacity → urgent acts in the presence of the defence; lasting incapacity → suspension or discontinuance, subject to the procedure for a defendant not criminally responsible, whose hearing may be held in the defendant's absence (art. 374 para. 2 let. a CPP).

entities.legal_bases: Art. 19 paras. 1 and 3, arts. 20, 59, 64 CP/StGB; arts. 114, 319, 374-375 CPP/StPO; ATF/BGE 147 IV 93 (6B_360/2020). Unified federal law (CPP in force since 2011): a single national entry, no cantonal rule.

entities.note: Non-responsibility established from the investigation stage for all offences: the prosecution (MP) does not discontinue but applies in writing to the court of first instance for a measure (art. 374 CPP). Hearing under the ordinary rules (public, evidence on participation); judgment without a guilty verdict (ATF 147 IV 93). Absence of the defendant and closed hearing possible, not the rule. No measure sought: discontinuance.

entities.name: Germany

facts.outcome: judgment ordering committal to a psychiatric hospital (§ 63 StGB) at the end of the Sicherungsverfahren; in ordinary proceedings: acquittal (Freispruch, § 20 StGB) + § 63 StGB
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Sicherungsverfahren: Antragsschrift equivalent to an indictment, then Hauptverhandlung before the trial court under the rules of criminal trials (§§ 413-414 StPO).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Verhandlungsunfähigkeit: bar to criminal proceedings (provisional suspension, § 205 StPO; discontinuance if permanent, § 206a StPO); but the Sicherungsverfahren is also available in cases of unfitness (§ 413 StPO, § 71 StGB), with a hearing possible without the person concerned (§ 415) and transition to criminal proceedings if they become fit again (§ 416 Abs. 3).

entities.legal_bases: §§ 20, 63, 71 StGB; §§ 126a, 140 Abs. 1 Nr. 7, 170 Abs. 2, 205, 413-416 StPO; §§ 24 Abs. 1 Nr. 2, 74 Abs. 2, 171a GVG. Uniform federal law (Bundesrecht): a single national entry.
entities.excerpt: Für das Sicherungsverfahren gelten sinngemäß die Vorschriften über das Strafverfahren, soweit nichts anderes bestimmt ist. […] Der Antrag steht der öffentlichen Klage gleich.
entities.note: If the investigation establishes Schuldunfähigkeit, the prosecution files an Antragsschrift equivalent to an indictment (Sicherungsverfahren, §§ 413-414 StPO) before the Landgericht: public Hauptverhandlung under the rules of criminal trials, mandatory defence, judgment ordering the § 63 StGB measure. Absence possible if the person's condition or public order requires it (§ 415). Alternative: Anklage, Freispruch + § 63.

entities.name: Austria

facts.outcome: judgment ordering placement in a forensisch-therapeutisches Zentrum (§ 21 Abs. 1 StGB), without penalty
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Antrag auf Unterbringung subject to the rules governing indictments, decided after a public oral hearing before the Landesgericht (lay assessors or jury) under the ordinary rules (§§ 434-434a StPO).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Specific rule not found (RIS inaccessible): the StPO applies by analogy (§ 429); defence counsel and expert mandatory throughout the hearing, on pain of nullity (§ 434d); defence counsel and legal representative may act even against the will of the person concerned (§§ 430 Abs. 1 Z 1, 434c).

entities.legal_bases: §§ 11, 21 Abs. 1 StGB; §§ 429-431, 434-434f StPO, as amended by the Maßnahmenvollzugsanpassungsgesetz 2022 (in force since 1.3.2023, unchanged as at 28.10.2026). Uniform federal law (Bundesrecht): a single national entry.
entities.excerpt: Das Gericht entscheidet über die Unterbringung nach öffentlicher mündlicher Hauptverhandlung, die in sinngemäßer Anwendung der Bestimmungen des 14. und 15. Hauptstücks durchzuführen ist, durch Urteil.
entities.note: If the conditions of § 21 Abs. 1 StGB are met, the prosecution must file an Antrag auf Unterbringung subject to the rules governing indictments (§ 434 StPO). The Landesgericht (lay assessors, or jury with a question on Zurechnungsunfähigkeit, § 434e) decides after a public oral hearing under the ordinary rules (§ 434a) and may also convict (§ 434b). Defence counsel and expert mandatory.

entities.name: Netherlands

facts.outcome: ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging (act proven but offender not punishable) + tbs met dwangverpleging (arts. 37a-37b Sr) or zorgmachtiging issued by the criminal court (art. 2.3 Wfz)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: ordinary criminal trial before the rechtbank, non-responsibility being decided as a question of the offender's punishability after proof of the facts (art. 350 Sv).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Art. 16 Sv: if a mental disorder prevents the suspect from understanding the significance of the proceedings, the court suspends them at any stage until the suspect's recovery is established; no trial in the meantime (civil compulsory care possible).

entities.legal_bases: Arts. 39, 37a, 37b Sr; art. 2.3 Wet forensische zorg (art. 37 Sr repealed as of 1-1-2020); arts. 16, 167, 348, 350, 352 lid 2 Sv; arts. 196 and 317 Sv (clinical observation at the Pieter Baan Centrum).

entities.name: Italy

facts.outcome: judgment of acquittal “perché il reato è stato commesso da persona non imputabile” (art. 530 c.p.p.) + security measure in the event of social dangerousness: REMS as a last resort, otherwise supervised liberty
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: if a security measure other than confiscation is foreseeable, the public prosecutor (PM) must bring criminal proceedings and the GUP must commit for trial; the giudizio abbreviato exists only at the accused's request and is excluded for offences punishable by ergastolo.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Psychophysical incapacity to participate consciously (arts. 70-72-bis c.p.p.): expert examination, suspension with a special curator and a new expert examination every six months; if irreversible, dismissal (art. 72-bis) unless a security measure is required: the suspension then remains (Cass. 10516/2020), with possible provisional application of a measure (art. 206 c.p.).

entities.excerpt: non può pronunciare sentenza di non luogo a procedere se ritiene che dal proscioglimento dovrebbe conseguire l'applicazione di una misura di sicurezza diversa dalla confisca
entities.note: The public prosecutor (PM) cannot request discontinuance (art. 408), nor can the GUP pronounce a dismissal (art. 425 para. 4), if a security measure other than confiscation is foreseeable: trial (assize court), acquittal for non-imputability and measure ordered by the trial court (art. 530 para. 4). Absent dangerousness, discontinuance or dismissal possible. No reform of the REMS found after Corte cost. 22/2022.

entities.name: Spain

facts.outcome: Judgment of acquittal with exemption from criminal responsibility (eximente completa, art. 20.1 CP) at the end of the trial (jury for homicide) + committal for medical treatment in a suitable establishment (art. 101 CP), the maximum duration of which, capped at the prison sentence the offence carries, is set in the judgment
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: even if the prosecution and the private prosecution request dismissal on the ground of an exemption under art. 20 CP (nº 1, 2, 3, 5, 6), the judge returns the case to the prosecuting parties for qualification of the charges and the trial continues to judgment (art. 782.1 LECrim).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Signs of insanity: the judge has the charged person observed by forensic physicians (art. 381 LECrim). Insanity arising after the offence: at the close of the sumario, the case is archived until recovery, with application of the CP measures for the insane (art. 383); this provision does not cover a disorder already present at the time of the offence (art. 20.1), which is a matter for the trial (782.1); the case of a disorder present from the time of the offence and persisting is not verified (case law not read).

entities.legal_bases: CP arts. 20.1.º, 101 (and 3.1, not re-read); LECrim arts. 381, 383, 637.3.º, 782.1; LO 5/1995 del Tribunal del Jurado, arts. 1.2.a) (homicidio, arts. 138-140 CP), 4, 24.2, 25.3, 26, 32.1, 37.b)
entities.excerpt: devolverá las actuaciones a las acusaciones para calificación, continuando el juicio hasta sentencia, a los efectos de la imposición de medidas de seguridad
entities.note: 782.1: even if the prosecution and the private prosecution request dismissal on the ground of the art. 20.1 exemption, the trial continues to judgment for the measure (CP 101). In jury trials (homicide), the judge may order a 637.3 dismissal (LOTJ 26.1, 32.1) with no express exception, but the LECrim applies on a supplementary basis (24.2) and the verdict covers the exemption (37.b). Practice not verified: medium confidence.

entities.name: Portugal

facts.outcome: judgment declaring the arguido non-imputable (CP art. 20.º) and ordering their confinement in a care, treatment or security establishment (CP art. 91.º), for at least 3 years for a crime against persons punishable by more than 5 years
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the sufficient-evidence standard covers the prospect of a security measure, so the prosecution (MP) must indict (art. 283.º CPP) and the investigating judge must commit for trial (art. 308.º); only the trial court orders confinement.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No general rule on unfitness found in the texts consulted; preventive confinement in a psychiatric hospital instead of pre-trial detention (art. 202.º n.º 2 CPP); during the trial hearing, the expert examination of mental state may interrupt or postpone the hearing (art. 351.º n.º 4).

entities.excerpt: possibilidade razoável de ao arguido vir a ser aplicada, por força deles, em julgamento, uma pena ou uma medida de segurança
entities.note: Expert examination ordered during the inquérito directed by the prosecution (MP), which cannot impose any measure: if it foresees confinement, it must indict (art. 283.º n.º 2 CPP). Non-imputability, dangerousness and confinement are decided by the court after a hearing (CP 91; CRP 27.º n.º 2), which may order an expert examination (art. 351.º). Where no measure is foreseeable, discontinuance possible. CPP up to date with Lei 37/2026.

entities.name: Greece

facts.outcome: Judgment of the trial court: exemption from penalty / acquittal for ακαταλόγιστο (art. 34 ΠΚ) + compulsory therapeutic measure (art. 69Α ΠΚ: hospitalisation in a special unit or psychiatric department of a public hospital, or outpatient treatment) if, at the time of the decision, the person is at risk of committing further offences at least as serious; maximum duration set in the decision (2 years for a misdemeanour, 5 years for a felony), extendable up to the maximum penalty applicable and reviewed every year (art. 70 ΠΚ)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the judicial council must commit for trial (art. 313 §2 ΚΠΔ) and only the court orders the measure (art. 69Α ΠΚ); the council imposes only a provisional restrictive condition (art. 315 §6 ΚΠΔ).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Disorder of the accused's mental functions: after an expert examination (art. 200), the court suspends the proceedings, unless it is going to acquit, definitively terminate the prosecution or declare it inadmissible; if the accused is in pre-trial detention, placement in a forensic psychiatric unit (or another psychiatric unit) for 3 months at most; during the investigation, the investigating judge rules without blocking necessary investigative acts; resumption when the disorder ceases (art. 80 ΚΠΔ).

entities.legal_bases: ΠΚ (ν. 4619/2019) άρθρα 34, 69Α, 70; ΚΠΔ (ν. 4620/2019) άρθρα 80, 200, 310, 311 §1, 313 §2, 315 §6; ν. 5090/2024 άρθρο 9 (only adds expulsion to art. 69 §1 ΠΚ, without affecting 34, 69Α, 70)

The court grants the exemption and then orders the measure. Where no measure applies, a dismissal remains possible (311 §1). Green, not yellow.

entities.name: Sweden

facts.outcome: No acquittal: after an ordinary trial, the court finds the offence established and then, instead of prison, imposes as a sanction överlämnande to forensic psychiatric care (BrB 31:3), with, where necessary, special discharge review by the administrative court; prison is excluded if the disorder removed the capacity to understand the significance of the act (30:6, except for a self-induced disorder) and the accused may be declared fri från påföljd.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No prior filter: the court orders the psychiatric examination (lag 1991:1137, upon confession or convincing evidence) but the case is always tried; åtalsunderlåtelse (RB 20:7) is merely an option for the prosecution.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No formal unfitness procedure identified: an accused with a serious mental disorder may be tried in their absence if their presence is not necessary (RB 46:15 a, 1 st. 3°, text seen in SFS 2026:1657); adjournment rules not verified.

entities.legal_bases: BrB 30 kap. 6 § (text seen via Prop. 2007/08:97 and the reform), 31 kap. 3 § (överlämnande till rättspsykiatrisk vård), 1 kap. 3 §; lag (1991:1137) om rättspsykiatrisk undersökning 1-4 §§; lag (1991:1129) om rättspsykiatrisk vård 16-16 a §§; RB 46 kap. 15 a §, 20 kap. 7 §; reform Prop. 2025/26:297 (SFS 2026:1654, 1657, 1668; BrB 31 kap. 4-6 §§), not in force.
entities.excerpt: av en allvarlig psykisk störning, får rätten överlämna honom till rättspsykiatrisk vård
entities.note: Not “black”: forensic care (BrB 31:3) replaces prison, but there is neither acquittal nor tillräknelighet (nor in the reform). Ordinary trial; the court orders the RPU examination, then care or fri från påföljd (30:6). Reform Prop. 2025/26:297 (SFS 2026:1654) promulgated on 20.8.2026, not in force: same regime in 31 kap. 4-6 §§. Adjournment for unfitness not verified.

entities.name: Norway

facts.outcome: Ordinary trial: the utilregnelig accused (§ 20) is not punished; the court leaves them without penalty (frifinnelse where no measure is imposed, e.g. HR-2022-1110-A) or orders by judgment their transfer to compulsory psychiatric care (§ 62) or compulsory care (§ 63) if the protection of society so requires.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No prior filter: the measure can only be ordered by judgment, on a tiltale from the prosecution, henleggelse (code 065) being reserved for clear cases of non-responsibility (Rundskriv 2/2020).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Right and duty of the accused to be present until judgment (strpl. § 280): if they are in a condition that prevents them from appearing and defending their interests, the case is adjourned, unless the impediment is attributable to them (HR-2004-1477-A, on appeal); at the appeal hearing, an absent mentally ill accused is excused if the absence cannot be held against them (§ 336; HR-2019-556-U). Rule for lasting unfitness not verified.

entities.legal_bases: Straffeloven § 20 (utilregnelighet, in force since 1.10.2020), §§ 62-65 (tvungent psykisk helsevern / tvungen omsorg ved dom); straffeprosessloven §§ 147, 165, 165 a (rettspsykiatrisk undersøkelse, Den rettsmedisinske kommisjon), 280 (tiltaltes tilstedeværelse), 336; psykisk helsevernloven kap. 5; Riksadvokatens rundskriv 2/2020 and 4/2001.
entities.excerpt: En lovbryter som er utilregnelig etter § 20 annet til fjerde ledd kan ved dom overføres til tvungent psykisk helsevern
entities.note: The court alone decides on utilregnelighet (the experts inform without concluding) at an ordinary hearing; the measure (§ 62) can only be ordered by judgment, on a tiltale from the prosecution. Rettspsykiatrisk examination ordered by the court at the prosecution's request, reports sent to the DRK. Henleggelse (code 065) reserved for clear cases. Lasting unfitness not verified (Lovdata blocked).

entities.name: Denmark

facts.outcome: Ordinary trial (domsmænd; nævninger if forvaring): guilt is decided without regard to § 16, which comes into play at the sentencing stage; the person not criminally responsible is frifindes for straf (§ 16) and the court orders a measure (§ 68): anbringelse in psychiatric care or an institution, treatment or supervision; forvaring (§ 70) possible.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the anklagemyndighed requests the mentalundersøgelse (rpl. § 809; the court settles disputes) then prosecutes, seeking the measure; tiltalefrafald (rpl. § 722 stk. 2) remains discretionary and seriousness weighs against it.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Personal attendance required throughout the hearing (rpl. § 853); the presiding judge may excuse an accused who so requests, in particular on mental-health grounds. In very special circumstances, the hearing may be held without an accused who, because of their mental state, is unable to understand and follow the proceedings (Vidensbasen); no procedure for adjournment or termination identified.

entities.legal_bases: Straffeloven §§ 16, 68-70 (LBK nr. 1294 af 7.11.2025); retsplejeloven §§ 809 (mentalundersøgelse), 722 stk. 2 (tiltalefrafald), 853 (tiltaltes tilstedeværelse) (LBK nr. 1298 af 7.11.2025); Retslægerådet; Rigsadvokatmeddelelsen “Psykisk afvigende kriminelle”.
entities.excerpt: Hvis en tiltalt frifindes for straf i medfør af § 16, kan retten træffe bestemmelse om anvendelse af andre foranstaltninger
entities.note: No pretrial filter for serious offences: the prosecution has the accused examined (rpl. § 809, Retslægerådet consulted) and prosecutes, seeking the measure; the court decides guilt, then § 16 is dealt with at the sentencing stage (§ 68). Tiltalefrafald (rpl. § 722 stk. 2) discretionary, with seriousness weighing against it. No reform of this regime identified.

entities.name: Greenland

facts.outcome: The Greenlandic code recognises only “foranstaltninger”: after an ordinary criminal trial with domsmænd, the court imposes on the sindssyg offender (§ 156 stk. 1) a special measure under ch. 33 instead of the ordinary measures: treatment in hospital or under its control, anbringelse, supervision (§ 157), where appropriate with no maximum duration (§ 158 stk. 2).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the prosecution requests the mentalundersøgelse (rpl. § 436 stk. 2; court decision in case of refusal or detention) and, if the examination becomes necessary during the hearing, as a rule asks that guilt be ruled on first (§ 473 stk. 1, 2. pkt.).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Attendance mandatory (rpl. §§ 451, 453): absence due to a psychiatric illness counts as a lawful excuse and the case is as a rule adjourned; hearing without the accused only in “ganske særlige omstændigheder”, depending on their ability to understand and follow the proceedings and on the prospects of improvement (U 2021.1771 H, Rigsadvokat pkt. 3.8).

entities.legal_bases: Kriminallov for Grønland (lov nr. 306 af 30.4.2008, as amended) kap. 33 §§ 156 stk. 1, 157 stk. 2, 158 stk. 2; retsplejelov for Grønland (lov nr. 305 af 30.4.2008, as amended) §§ 341, 436 stk. 2, 451, 453, 473 stk. 1; Rigsadvokatmeddelelsen “Psykisk afvigende kriminelle - Grønland” (CIR1H nr. 9873 af 13.10.2023) pkt. 3.1, 3.8; U 2021.1771 H; Grønlands Landsrets dom af 17.9.2025 (K 166/25).
entities.excerpt: var sindssyg eller i en tilstand, der ganske må ligestilles hermed, eller var mentalt retarderet, kan der idømmes foranstaltninger efter dette kapitel
entities.note: Special measures (ch. 33) imposed by the criminal court after an ordinary trial with domsmænd: in 2025 the Landsret found T sindssyg (§ 156 stk. 1) and sentenced him to treatment (§ 157 stk. 2). Examination requested by the prosecution (rpl. § 436 stk. 2), guilt as a rule decided first (§ 473). Incapacitated accused: adjournment in principle. Extract of § 156 taken from the 2008 text.

history.note: Own code based on “measures”: the sindssyg offender is subject to special measures (ch. 33) ordered by the court after an ordinary trial, guilt first in principle (rpl. § 473). Examination requested by the prosecution (§ 436 stk. 2), Retslægerådet consulted; no closed psychiatric ward in Greenland. Unfitness not verified; research in Danish only.

entities.name: Faroe Islands

facts.outcome: Ordinary trial before Retten på Færøerne (with nævninger for serious crimes): an accused falling under § 16 stk. 1 of the Faroese Criminal Code is declared “straffri” and the court orders a § 68 measure (placement in a psychiatric unit, treatment, supervision), with no maximum duration for serious violent crimes (§ 68 a stk. 2).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the Landfoged prosecutes, the mentalundersøgelse falls under rpl. § 859 stk. 2 (= Danish § 809 stk. 2) and only the courts order § 68 measures; påtaleopgivelse (§ 724) and tiltalefrafald (§ 725) remain discretionary.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Not verified: the Rigsadvokat's table of equivalences (2026) does not cover the rules on the accused's presence; in Greenland, a psychiatric impediment counts as a lawful excuse and the case is as a rule adjourned (U 2021.1771 H, cited by the Rigsadvokat), but Faroese equivalence is not established.

entities.legal_bases: Straffelov for Færøerne (“den færøske straffelov”) § 16 stk. 1, §§ 68, 68 a stk. 2, 69-70; retsplejelov for Færøerne §§ 724 stk. 1, 725, 859 stk. 2 (equivalent to Danish §§ 721, 722, 809 according to Rigsadvokatmeddelelsen CIR1H nr. 10105 af 22.9.2026, Bilag 3); Højesterets dom af 9.12.2020 (sag 63/2020); Revsilógin (Llk. nr. 8 frá 20.2.2024): not read.
entities.excerpt: Tiltalte er således omfattet af straffelovens § 16, stk. 1, og dermed straffri. […] Det er domstolene, der træffer afgørelse om eventuelle foranstaltninger
entities.note: Without analogy: Højesteret (9.12.2020, appeal from a trial with nævninger at Retten på Færøerne) applies the Faroese § 16 stk. 1 (“straffri”) and upholds the placement under § 68; medical opinions “alene vejledende”. The Rigsadvokat (22.9.2026) regards §§ 68-70 and rpl. § 859 as equivalent to Danish law. Extract taken from the judgment; text of § 16, status of the 2024 Revsilógin and unfitness not verified.

Extract taken from the Rigsadvokat's directive, not from the statute. Unfitness not verified.

entities.name: Finland

facts.outcome: Ordinary trial at the käräjäoikeus: the court, not bound by the psychiatric opinions (KKO:2025:43), leaves the syyntakeeton accused without a penalty (rangaistukseen tuomitsematta) and refers the question of their need for treatment to the THL (MTL 21 §), and may have them held in prison in the meantime; the THL orders compulsory treatment if the conditions are met (MTL 22 §), with appeal to the hallinto-oikeus (24 §).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the court orders the mielentilatutkimus (OK 17:45), the THL sends it its opinion, then the court rules on the facts and on syyntakeisuus; no ground for non-prosecution specific to syyntakeettomuus (ROL 1:7-8).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No unfitness procedure identified. General rules verified (KKO:2025:53): save for exceptions, the accused may not be sentenced to a penalty without having been heard in person (ROL 8:3) and judgment in their absence is limited to penalties of at most 3 months (8:11); the position of an accused unable to follow the proceedings (adjournment, representation) has not been verified.

entities.legal_bases: Rikoslaki 3 luku 4 § 2 mom. (syyntakeettomuus); oikeudenkäymiskaari 17 luku 45 § (mielentilatutkimus); mielenterveyslaki (1116/1990) 21, 22, 24 § (amended by 752/2015 and 15/2024, in force 1.4.2024, leaving 21-22 § untouched); laki oikeudenkäynnistä rikosasioissa (689/1997) 1 luku 7-8 §, 8 luku 3 ja 11 §; HE 92/2015 vp; KKO:2025:43; KKO:2025:53.
entities.excerpt: Rikoksesta syytetyn mielentila tutkitaan tuomioistuimen oikeudenkäymiskaaren 17 luvun 45 §:n nojalla antamasta määräyksestä.
entities.note: The court orders the examination (OK 17:45, HE 92/2015), is not bound by the opinion (KKO:2025:43), leaves the syyntakeeton accused without a penalty and refers the matter to the THL, which decides on treatment (MTL 21-22 §, unchanged in 2024). No ground for non-prosecution specific to syyntakeettomuus; prosecutorial discretion (ROL 1:8) yields to the public interest. Statutes unreadable on Finlex: extract from HE 92/2015; unfitness not verified.

entities.name: Iceland

facts.outcome: The court acquits the ósakhæfur accused (sýkna, hgl. 15. gr.) at the end of the criminal trial and may order security measures (62. gr.) in the same judgment, in practice öryggisgæsla, mainly in the réttargeðdeild; subsequent review by the court. Law of 19.6.2026 (in force on 1.4.2027): measures still “í dómi”, max. duration 5 years, renewable, recent and independent expert examination, tilsjónarmaður appointed by the judge.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route identified: the measures under 62. gr. are decided only “í dómi”; in practice the police ask the court to appoint a psychiatrist for the geðrannsókn (Hæstiréttur 91/2007, former law); law 88/2008 could not be read.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Law in force not verified (law 88/2008 unreadable). The law of 19.6.2026 (in force 1.4.2027, new 63. gr.) provides that if the person concerned falls into the condition referred to in 15./16. gr. on a lasting basis after the offence and before final judgment, the court decides in the judgment whether the penalty is imposed or dropped and may order the measures under 62. gr. in its place: the case is still tried.

entities.legal_bases: Almenn hegningarlög nr. 19/1940, 15., 16., 62. gr. (ráðstafanir eftir sýknu); lög um meðferð sakamála nr. 88/2008 (not read); lög um breytingu á almennum hegningarlögum, nr. 19/1940 (öryggisráðstafanir), samþykkt á Alþingi 19.6.2026, gildistaka 1.4.2027 (new 62.-63. gr., 65.-66. gr. repealed).

entities.note: The court acquits the ósakhæfur accused (15. gr.) and orders the measures under 62. gr. “í dómi” (öryggisgæsla, mainly in the réttargeðdeild): no pretrial route. The law of 19.6.2026 (in force 1.4.2027) keeps the decision in the judgment. entities.name: Poland

facts.outcome: Discontinuance (umorzenie postępowania) for niepoczytalność ordered by the trial court on the prosecutor's application + security measure of placement in a psychiatric institution (KK art. 93g); decision as a rule given after a rozprawa, exceptionally at a sitting.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Instead of an indictment, the prosecutor files with the trial court an application for discontinuance and a measure (art. 324 § 1); it goes to a rozprawa, unless the facts and non-responsibility are beyond doubt and the president of the court considers a sitting appropriate (art. 354 pkt 2).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Suspension of the proceedings for the duration of the obstacle if the accused cannot take part because of a mental illness or other serious illness (art. 22 § 1 KPK, read; zażalenie possible, evidence to be secured during the suspension); in the art. 354 procedure the suspect does not take part in the sitting if the experts consider it inadvisable, unless the court finds it necessary; mandatory defence in case of doubt about mental health (art. 79 KPK, not re-read).

entities.legal_bases: KPK art. 324 §§ 1, 1a, 2, 3 (wniosek o umorzenie i środki zabezpieczające), art. 354 pkt 1-3 (rozprawa or posiedzenie), art. 22 §§ 1-3 (zawieszenie); KK art. 31 § 1, arts. 93a-93g; KPK art. 79, art. 202, art. 414 (first pass, not re-read)
entities.excerpt: wniosek kieruje się na rozprawę, chyba że w świetle materiałów postępowania przygotowawczego popełnienie czynu zabronionego przez podejrzanego i jego niepoczytalność […] nie budzą wątpliwości
entities.note: The prosecutor does not indict: instead, they apply to the trial court (art. 324). Rule: rozprawa; exception: sitting (prosecutor, defence counsel, suspect) if the facts and niepoczytalność are beyond doubt and the court president considers it appropriate (art. 354 pkt 2). Actual frequency of the sitting not established. Consolidated text Dz.U. 2026 poz. 490 (as at 18-19.08.2026).

LexLege – Kodeks postępowania karnego, art. 324 (wniosek o umorzenie postępowania i zastosowanie środków zabezpieczających), as at 2.8.2026
LexLege – Kodeks postępowania karnego, art. 22 (zawieszenie postępowania), as at 19.8.2026
Standardy prawa – Umorzenie postępowania z powodu niepoczytalności sprawcy (art. 324 i art. 354 k.p.k.), thesis headings

history.note: Expert examination by at least two psychiatrists (art. 202 KPK). If committal is required, no indictment: the prosecutor files with the trial court an application for discontinuance and a measure (art. 324). It is decided in principle at a public, adversarial rozprawa (art. 354), exceptionally at a sitting if the facts and non-responsibility are beyond doubt. If it is rejected, the case is referred back to the prosecution.

independent_check.reasoning: Read: art. 354 pkt 2 KPK (stan 18.08.2026): the art. 324 wniosek goes to a rozprawa, unless the act and niepoczytalność are beyond doubt and the court president considers a sitting (posiedzenie) appropriate. RPO 2021: “zasadą ... rozprawa, tylko wyjątkowo posiedzenie”. Purple; actual frequency of the posiedzenie not established.

entities.name: Czechia

facts.outcome: discontinuance of the prosecution by the prosecutor + ochranné léčení (§ 99 TZ) or zabezpečovací detence (§ 100 TZ) ordered by the court at a veřejné zasedání
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The prosecutor must discontinue the prosecution (§ 172 odst. 1 písm. e) TŘ) and the court rules only on the measure, on the prosecutor's motion, at a veřejné zasedání (§ 239 TŘ), without hlavní líčení.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: If a mental illness arising after the act prevents understanding of the meaning of the prosecution, the prosecutor and then the court suspend it (přerušení, § 173 odst. 1 písm. c) and § 224 TŘ) until recovery; if the disorder existed at the time of the act, discontinuance + measure route; mandatory defence (§ 36 TŘ).

entities.excerpt: Státní zástupce zastaví trestní stíhání, […] nebyl-li obviněný v době činu pro nepříčetnost trestně odpovědný
entities.note: Mandatory psychiatric expert examination (§ 116 TŘ). Non-responsibility established before trial: the prosecutor must discontinue the prosecution (§ 172/1 e); the court orders ochranné léčení or zabezpečovací detence at a veřejné zasedání only on the prosecutor's motion (§ 239), without hlavní líčení; stížnost has suspensive effect. If the case goes to trial: acquittal (§ 226 d) + measure. Text seen: version of 1.4.2024.

Sitting on the measure alone, without hlavní líčení: yellow.

entities.name: Slovakia

facts.outcome: Discontinuance of the prosecution by the prosecutor for nepríčetnosť (TP § 215 ods. 1 písm. e), without conviction, then a court decision (uznesenie), on the prosecutor's motion and at a verejné zasadnutie, imposing ochranné liečenie ústavné (TZ § 73 ods. 1).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The prosecutor discontinues the prosecution (TP § 215 ods. 1 písm. e), then the court rules on the measure alone, at the prosecutor's request, at a public verejné zasadnutie, the accused present in principle, evidence possible under the trial rules applied primerane (TP § 299, § 293 ods. 3, § 295 ods. 2), without hlavné pojednávanie.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Prerušenie (suspension) of the prosecution if a mental illness arising after the act prevents the accused from understanding the meaning of the prosecution (TP § 228); resumption by uznesenie when the cause ceases. If non-responsibility already existed at the time of the act, the discontinuance + measure route applies; a sitting without the accused is allowed only under the conditions of § 293 ods. 4-5 (NS SR 1Tdo/62/2023). Mandatory defence: not re-verified.

entities.name: Hungary

facts.outcome: Acquittal (felmentés) for kóros elmeállapot (Btk. 17. § (1)) and kényszergyógykezelés ordered by the court in the same judgment (Be. 566. § (1) and (3); Btk. 78. §); an előzetes kényszergyógykezelés (Be. 301. §) may be ordered by the judge before judgment.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No replacement procedure found: the ügyészség indicts, the court tries the case at an ordinary hearing, then acquits and orders the measure in the same judgment (Be. 566. §, according to legal scholarship).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Suspension (felfüggesztés) of the proceedings if, after indictment, the accused's mental state prevents them from exercising their procedural rights; előzetes kényszergyógykezelés (Be. 301. §) may be ordered during the proceedings; mandatory defence in case of mental disorder (Be. 44. §, according to legal scholarship).

entities.name: Slovenia

facts.outcome: Court decision given after a glavna obravnava, without conviction, imposing a security measure: obvezno psihiatrično zdravljenje in varstvo v zdravstvenem zavodu (maximum duration of five years for a person not criminally responsible, KZ-1 70.a) or obvezno psihiatrično zdravljenje na prostosti (70.b).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The prosecutor proposes the measure to the court (ZKP 491); after any objection, the court rules after an adversarial glavna obravnava, with mandatory defence counsel, the accused being summoned if their condition allows (ZKP 492).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Psychiatric expert examination in case of serious doubt as to fitness to take part (ZKP 265/1); suspension of the proceedings during the investigation (ZKP 179) or at the hearing (ZKP 310/1); if the accused was not criminally responsible at the time of the act, the security-measure route applies and they are summoned only if their condition allows (ZKP 492).

entities.name: Estonia

facts.outcome: The prosecution declares the investigation complete and submits to the court a proposal to apply sundravi (KrMS § 397 lg 2, § 398). The court establishes the unlawful act and non-responsibility (§ 394, KarS § 34), terminates the criminal proceedings (§ 199 lg 1 p 1) and by määrus orders compulsory psychiatric treatment (KarS § 86), in hospital (20 cases in 2017) or on an outpatient basis (5), if the person is dangerous and needs it; otherwise no measure. No conviction (1 acquittal in 2017).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: After the investigation is closed, the court rules on the measure alone (neither indictment nor verdict), by default in abbreviated procedure on the file (lühimenetlus, KrMS § 400 lg 1; 34 cases out of 38 in 2017); general procedure possible (4 cases), chosen in practice by the prosecution, the accused's right to demand it not verified.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Incurable illness preventing participation in the proceedings or serving of the sentence: termination of the criminal proceedings at any stage (KrMS § 199 lg 1 p 6; Juridica 2025, pp. 102 and 107). Disorder established during the proceedings or after conviction: same chapter 16, sundravi (KrMS § 393, KarS § 86). Presence at the hearing: the rule, except where there is a risk to health (prosecution 2018, p. 4).

entities.legal_bases: KarS § 34 (süüdimatus), § 86 (psühhiaatriline sundravi); KrMS 16. peatükk §§ 393-403 (in particular §§ 393, 394, 395¹, 397 lg 2, 398 lg 4, 400 lg 1, 401-402); KrMS § 237 lg 4 and § 238 lg 1 p 2 (lühimenetlus); KrMS § 199 lg 1 p 1 and p 6

entities.name: Latvia

facts.outcome: The court, on referral from the prosecutor, releases the person from criminal liability and applies a compulsory measure of a medical nature (outpatient care, general psychiatric hospital or specialised secure hospital; KL 68) by decision (lēmums) at a closed hearing; if there are no grounds for a measure, the case is returned to the prosecutor (KPL 605(3)); if participation in the acts is not proved, termination (605(4)).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The prosecutor refers the case to the court (chapter 55 KPL), which rules by lēmums at a closed hearing (KPL 603), the person concerned being absent in about 70% of cases, with mandatory defence counsel and a representative, without a verdict of guilt.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: If the expert examination finds the person unfit to take part, the proceedings continue with mandatory defence counsel and a legal representative (KPL 75, 91-92, 594), with the possibility of excluding the person from the hearing on medical advice (KPL 602), and lead to the medical measure without a finding of guilt; illness arising after the acts or the conviction follows the same route (KPL 592 para. 1).

entities.name: Lithuania

facts.outcome: After the investigation, the prosecutor transmits the file to the court by nutarimas (BPK 398); the court holds a hearing (teisiamasis posėdis) under the general procedure (BPK 400), at which victims, witnesses and other evidence establish that the person committed the act, then rules by nutartis (BPK 403): compulsory medical measure (BK 98: outpatient monitoring or hospitalisation under general, enhanced or strict supervision), discontinuance without a measure if the person is not dangerous, or discontinuance if the act is not proved.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The special procedure of chapter XXIX BPK replaces the indictment with a nutarimas of the prosecutor, but the hearing follows the general procedure: victims, witnesses, evidence on the facts, expert (BPK 400).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Mental disorder arising after the acts or the conviction: the court suspends consideration of the case or execution of the sentence and applies a medical measure (BPK 403 p. 1 pt 3; BPK 393-394, 402); if the disorder is only temporary, mere postponement of the hearing; mandatory defence from the order for a psychiatric expert examination (BPK 396); the person may be brought to the hearing unless the expert advises otherwise (BPK 399).

entities.name: Israel

facts.outcome: Ordinary criminal trial: the court first establishes that the accused committed the act, then, if the accused lacked capacity at the time of the offence (Penal Law 34H), exempts them from responsibility (acquittal for lack of criminal responsibility) and, if they are still ill, orders hospitalisation or compulsory outpatient treatment (TMIL s. 15), capped at the maximum penalty for the offence (25 years for life imprisonment), subject to review by the district psychiatric committee.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial track (only a psychiatric examination before indictment is possible): the court first establishes the facts, then rules on responsibility (34H) and on the measure, at the ordinary trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Accused unfit to stand trial: proceedings stopped (CPL 170(a)), without acquittal or decision on responsibility, with possible hospitalisation (TMIL 15) on prima facie evidence, unless the defence requests an examination of guilt (בירור אשמה); the court may order it of its own motion for special reasons. Unfitness alone is rare (almost all forensic patients are NCR-MD) and no unfit accused has ever subsequently been tried (Argo 2023).

entities.legal_bases: Penal Law 5737-1977 s. 34H (34ח, insanity: חסר יכולת של ממש), s. 34E (34ה, presumption of absence of סייג according to Elron; 34B not confirmed), s. 34KB(b) (34כב(ב), reasonable doubt); Treatment of the Mentally Ill Law 5751-1991 (TMIL) s. 15 (s. 19 not verified); Criminal Procedure Law [Consolidated Version] 5742-1982 (CPL) s. 170(a)
entities.excerpt: יופסקו ההליכים נגדו, אלא אם כן, ביקש סנגורו לברר את אשמתו.
entities.note: No pretrial track: indictment, then ordinary trial in which the court establishes the act and then decides responsibility (34H); if the accused is still ill, hospitalisation (TMIL 15). Unfit: CPL 170, proceedings stopped save at the defence's request. Examination raised by the defence, the prosecution or the court. entities.name: United Kingdom

facts.outcome: special verdict “not guilty by reason of insanity” (England and Wales, Northern Ireland) or acquittal on the special defence of mental disorder (Scotland), delivered at trial, then a hospital disposal ordered by the trial court
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter in any of the three systems: non-responsibility is decided by the jury (or the judge in summary proceedings) at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: In all three systems, unfitness is decided by the judge alone and leads to a hearing on the facts (trial of the facts before a jury in England and Wales and Northern Ireland, examination of facts before the judge in Scotland) and then, if the act is established, to a hospital or other disposal.

entities.legal_bases: England and Wales: Trial of Lunatics Act 1883 s. 2, Criminal Procedure (Insanity) Act 1964 ss. 1, 4, 4A, 5, 6; Scotland: Criminal Procedure (Scotland) Act 1995 ss. 51A, 53F, 54, 55, 57; Northern Ireland: Criminal Justice Act (Northern Ireland) 1966 ss. 1-3, Mental Health (Northern Ireland) Order 1986 arts. 49, 49A, 50A
entities.excerpt: the jury shall return a special verdict that the accused is not guilty by reason of insanity.
entities.note: Synthesis of three systems: England and Wales and Northern Ireland in green (special verdict of the jury at the ordinary trial; the prosecution or the judge may also raise insanity); Scotland in blue (special defence reserved to the accused, s. 51A CP(S)A 1995). No pretrial filter; unfitness leads to a hearing on the facts and then to a hospital disposal.

entities.name: England

facts.outcome: special verdict “not guilty by reason of insanity” returned by the jury after trial + hospital order (with a mandatory restriction order in murder cases), supervision order or absolute discharge (s. 5 CP(I)A 1964)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the prosecution cannot accept a plea of insanity; only the Crown Court jury returns the special verdict at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Unfitness decided by the judge alone on the evidence of two doctors (s. 4); then a “trial of the facts” before a jury, limited to the physical act (s. 4A, which is not a trial): acquittal or finding that the accused did the act, followed by a hospital order (restriction mandatory for murder), supervision order or absolute discharge (s. 5); remittal for trial possible if the accused becomes fit again (s. 5A(4)). No planned amendments to ss. 4-5A according to legislation.gov.uk (2016 Law Com report not implemented).

entities.legal_bases: Trial of Lunatics Act 1883 s. 2; Criminal Procedure (Insanity) Act 1964 ss. 1, 4, 4A, 5, 5A, 6 (as amended by Criminal Procedure (Insanity and Unfitness to Plead) Act 1991 and Domestic Violence, Crime and Victims Act 2004 ss. 22, 24); Mental Health Act 1983 ss. 35-38, 41, 48; M'Naghten Rules (1843); R v Dickie [1984] 3 All ER 173; Bratty v AG for Northern Ireland [1963] AC 386; R v Antoine [2001] 1 AC 340

entities.note: No pretrial filter: at trial in the Crown Court, the jury returns the special verdict on the evidence of two doctors, then the judge chooses the disposal (s. 5). Insanity raised mainly by the defence, but also by the prosecution if the accused puts their mental state in issue (s. 6; Bratty) or by the judge on medical evidence (Dickie): green, not blue. Accused still ill: often unfitness (s. 4/4A).

facts.outcome: special verdict “not guilty by reason of insanity” returned by the jury after trial + hospital order (with a mandatory restriction order in murder cases), supervision order or absolute discharge (s. 5 CP(I)A 1964)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the prosecution cannot accept a plea of insanity; only the Crown Court jury returns the special verdict at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Unfitness decided by the judge alone on the evidence of two doctors (s. 4); then a “trial of the facts” before a jury, limited to the physical act (s. 4A, which is not a trial): acquittal or finding that the accused did the act, followed by a hospital order (restriction mandatory for murder), supervision order or absolute discharge (s. 5); remittal for trial possible if the accused becomes fit again (s. 5A(4)). No planned amendments to ss. 4-5A according to legislation.gov.uk (2016 Law Com report not implemented).

entities.legal_bases: Trial of Lunatics Act 1883 s. 2; Criminal Procedure (Insanity) Act 1964 ss. 1, 4, 4A, 5, 5A, 6 (as amended by Criminal Procedure (Insanity and Unfitness to Plead) Act 1991 and Domestic Violence, Crime and Victims Act 2004 ss. 22, 24); Mental Health Act 1983 ss. 35-38, 41, 48; M'Naghten Rules (1843); R v Dickie [1984] 3 All ER 173; Bratty v AG for Northern Ireland [1963] AC 386; R v Antoine [2001] 1 AC 340
entities.excerpt: the jury shall return a special verdict that the accused is not guilty by reason of insanity.
entities.note: No pretrial filter: at trial in the Crown Court, the jury returns the special verdict on the evidence of two doctors, then the judge chooses the disposal (s. 5). Insanity raised mainly by the defence, but also by the prosecution if the accused puts their mental state in issue (s. 6; Bratty) or by the judge on medical evidence (Dickie): green, not blue. Accused still ill: often unfitness (s. 4/4A).

entities.name: Scotland

facts.outcome: acquittal “by reason of the special defence” of mental disorder (s. 51A) delivered at trial + compulsion order with or without a restriction order, or other disposal (s. 57 CP(S)A 1995)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the special defence, notified by the accused before trial, is decided by the jury (or the sheriff in summary proceedings) at the ordinary trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Unfitness (inability to participate effectively in the trial, s. 53F) found by the court (s. 54), which orders an “examination of facts” before the judge (s. 55): proof of the act beyond reasonable doubt, acquittal possible including on the special defence (s. 55(4)), then s. 57 disposals; hearing possible in the accused's absence if the defence does not object (s. 55(5)).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Procedure (Scotland) Act 1995 ss. 51A (inserted by the Criminal Justice and Licensing (Scotland) Act 2010), 52B-52J, 53F, 54, 55, 57; Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003
entities.excerpt: The special defence may be stated only by the person charged with the offence
entities.note: Since 2012, only the accused may raise the special defence of mental disorder (s. 51A), which they prove on the balance of probabilities; neither the prosecution nor the judge can impose it. The jury decides it at the ordinary trial, then the court orders the disposal (s. 57). The accused chooses whether, rather than when, the issue is examined (advance notice): blue, close to green.

entities.name: Northern Ireland

facts.outcome: special verdict “not guilty by reason of insanity” returned by the jury + hospital admission with or without restriction (mandatory for murder), guardianship, supervision and treatment order or absolute discharge (art. 50A MHO 1986)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: insanity is decided by the jury at trial, then the court orders the disposal (art. 50A MHO 1986).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Unfitness decided by the judge alone on the oral evidence of an approved doctor (RQIA) and the opinion of a second doctor (art. 49 MHO 1986); the jury then determines whether the accused did the act, failing which acquittal (art. 49A); art. 50A disposals (hospital with restriction mandatory for murder). Part 10 of the MCA (NI) 2016 (ch. 6, ss. 204-210) contains provisions that are still prospective.

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Justice Act (Northern Ireland) 1966 ss. 1-3; Mental Health (Northern Ireland) Order 1986 arts. 49, 49A, 50A (as amended by 1996 NI 24); Mental Capacity Act (Northern Ireland) 2016 Part 10 ch. 6 (ss. 204-210, prospective provisions); Bratty v AG for Northern Ireland [1963] AC 386
entities.excerpt: the prosecution, with the leave of the court, may assume the burden of proving that the person charged was an insane person
entities.note: No pretrial filter: jury trial. The accused, presumed sane, proves insanity on the balance of probabilities, but the prosecution may, with the judge's leave, prove it itself (s. 2(3)): the defence does not control the issue. Definition includes inability to control one's own conduct (s. 1); no conviction (s. 3); disposal ordered by the court (art. 50A).

entities.name: Ireland

facts.outcome: special verdict “not guilty by reason of insanity” (jury or judge) + committal to a designated centre (Central Mental Hospital) if in-patient care is needed, under the oversight of the Mental Health (Criminal Law) Review Board
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the jury (Central Criminal Court) or the judge (District Court, Special Criminal Court) finds that the act was committed, then returns the special verdict at trial, on the evidence of a consultant psychiatrist.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Raised by the defence, the prosecution or the court, decided by the judge alone (s. 4); if unfit, proceedings adjourned and committal to a designated centre or out-patient treatment, with no examination of the facts unless requested (s. 4(8): discharge if there is a reasonable doubt as to the act); review by the Review Board at least every 6 months; return before the court if the accused becomes fit again (s. 13).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Law (Insanity) Act 2006 ss. 4, 5, 6, 11-13, 13A-13C, 19 (as amended by Criminal Law (Insanity) Act 2010; Criminal Justice (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2023 s. 72)
entities.excerpt: shall return a special verdict to the effect that the accused person is not guilty by reason of insanity
entities.note: No pretrial filter: the jury (or the judge) finds that the act was committed, then returns the special verdict at trial (s. 5); the court orders committal, reviewed by the Review Board. The defence gives notice of its expert evidence (s. 19); in murder cases the prosecution may prove insanity if the accused raises diminished responsibility; no Swain-type rule. Unfitness: committal without a trial of the facts.

entities.name: Canada

facts.outcome: verdict of not criminally responsible on account of mental disorder (art. 672.34) + disposition by the court or the Review Board: detention in hospital, conditional or absolute discharge (art. 672.54)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the trier of fact (jury or judge) returns the NRCTM (NCRMD) verdict at trial; the Crown may raise mental disorder before a finding of guilt only if the accused puts their capacity in issue (Swain).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Fitness presumed (art. 672.22); issue raised by the court of its own motion, by the accused or by the prosecutor (art. 672.23), decided by the jury where applicable (art. 672.26); if unfit, disposition by the Review Board (detention or conditional discharge), possible treatment to make the accused fit (art. 672.58), trial resumed if the accused becomes fit again; inquiry into the prima facie case every two years, acquittal if the evidence is insufficient (art. 672.33); stay of proceedings if permanently unfit and not posing a significant danger (art. 672.851).

entities.legal_bases: Code criminel / Criminal Code (L.R.C. 1985, ch. C-46) arts. 2 (“inapte à subir son procès” [unfit to stand trial]), 16, Part XX.1 (arts. 672.1-672.95), in particular 672.11-672.12, 672.22-672.33, 672.34, 672.45-672.54, 672.58, 672.851; R. v. Swain, [1991] 1 R.C.S. 933; R. v. Demers, 2004 CSC 46
entities.excerpt: verdict that the accused committed the act or made the omission but is not criminally responsible on account of mental disorder
entities.note: NRCTM (NCRMD) verdict returned at the ordinary trial by the trier of fact, followed by a disposition by the court or the Review Board. Under Swain (1991), the Crown may raise mental disorder only after a finding of guilt, unless the accused puts their capacity in issue: the defence controls the timing (assessment available to the Crown, art. 672.12(3)). Federal rule, Quebec included.

Blue, in line with the grid (the Swain example); caveat: the examination can still be imposed.

entities.name: Australia

facts.outcome: Special verdict “not guilty because of mental impairment” returned by the jury at trial (Criminal Code s. 7.3); the court then orders detention in prison or in hospital for a period not exceeding the maximum penalty for the offence, or release with or without conditions (Crimes Act 1914 s. 20BJ), detention being reviewed by the Attorney-General (ss. 20BK-20BL).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: a serious federal offence is tried by a jury (Constitution s. 80), which returns the special verdict at trial; only the summary procedure (s. 20BQ) allows a discontinuance.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: State or Territory law sets the test and the deciding body (jury or judge alone); federal law governs the consequences (Crimes Act 1914 s. 20B et seq.). If the accused is unfit, the court determines whether there is a prima facie case (failing which, the charge is dismissed and the accused released); otherwise it assesses whether the accused will become fit within 12 months (detention in hospital if treatable) or orders detention (up to the maximum penalty) or release for up to 3 years (ss. 20BA-20BC). No hearing on the facts.

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Code Act 1995 (Cth), Schedule, s. 7.3 (mental impairment); Crimes Act 1914 (Cth) Part IB: Div. 6 (s. 20B et seq., in particular ss. 20BA-20BC, unfitness to be tried), Div. 7 (s. 20BJ et seq., orders following acquittal because of mental illness; ss. 20BK-20BL, review by the Attorney-General), Div. 8 (s. 20BQ, summary proceedings); Constitution s. 80; Judiciary Act 1903 (Cth) ss. 68, 79
entities.excerpt: The prosecution can only rely on this section if the court gives leave.
entities.note: Federal offences tried by State courts under federal law: single national entry. No pretrial filter: the jury returns the special verdict at trial (s. 7.3); the prosecution may raise it only with the judge's leave. The court then orders detention (up to the maximum penalty) or release (s. 20BJ). State schemes do not apply.

entities.name: New South Wales

facts.outcome: Special verdict “act proven but not criminally responsible” returned at trial by the jury (or the judge alone), or entered by the court if prosecution and defence agree (s. 31); the court orders detention (“until released by due process of law”), conditional or unconditional release (s. 33), then refers the person to the Mental Health Review Tribunal, which oversees the forensic patient (s. 34, Part 5).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter for a serious offence tried in the Supreme Court: non-responsibility is decided at trial; the consensual route under s. 31 is akin to a guilty plea and diversion before a magistrate (ss. 12 et seq.) concerns summary proceedings.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Fitness decided by the judge alone, on the balance of probabilities (ss. 38, 44), in the absence of the jury (s. 41). If the accused is unfit and will not become fit within 12 months: special hearing (ss. 47-48, 54-62); if they can become fit, referral to the Mental Health Review Tribunal (ss. 49-51); advice from the DPP before any special hearing, release if the proceedings are abandoned (s. 53). The special hearing is conducted “as nearly as possible” like a trial, by the judge alone unless a jury is requested (s. 56), and results in acquittal, the special verdict (s. 61) or a finding that the offence was committed on the limited evidence available (s. 62), with a limiting term (s. 63).

entities.legal_bases: Mental Health and Cognitive Impairment Forensic Provisions Act 2020 (NSW): s. 28 (defence of mental health impairment or cognitive impairment), s. 29 (jury directions), s. 30 (special verdict), s. 31 (special verdict by agreement of the parties), s. 33 (orders), s. 34 (referral to the Tribunal), ss. 35-53 (fitness to be tried), ss. 54-68 (special hearings, limiting terms), Part 5 (forensic patients), ss. 12 et seq. (diversion before a magistrate)
entities.excerpt: On the return of a special verdict of act proven but not criminally responsible
entities.note: Since the 2020 Act, “act proven but not criminally responsible” replaces “not guilty by reason of mental illness”. No pretrial filter: the jury (or the judge alone) decides at trial, and the Crown may also raise the issue (Jawid); agreement between the parties possible at any time (s. 31). The court orders detention or release (s. 33); the Tribunal then reviews.

entities.name: Victoria

facts.outcome: Verdict “not guilty because of mental impairment” (CMIA s. 20) returned at trial by the jury, or by the judge alone hearing the evidence if prosecution and defence agree (s. 21(4)); the court then declares the person “liable to supervision” (custodial supervision order in detention or non-custodial supervision order in the community, of indefinite duration with a nominal term) or orders their unconditional release (s. 23).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the defence may be raised at any point in the trial; the finding by the judge alone (s. 21(4)) requires the prosecution's agreement and is akin to a guilty plea.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Presumption of fitness (s. 7). Investigation presided over by a judge and decided by a jury (Div. 1, ss. 5C-14A); the Act also contains a judge-alone regime (Div. 2, ss. 14B-14K, s. 14K providing for its repeal). If the accused cannot become fit within 12 months: special hearing with a jury, with the three findings available under s. 17(1) (not guilty; not guilty because of mental impairment; offence committed, without conviction), then supervision order or release.

entities.legal_bases: Crimes (Mental Impairment and Unfitness to be Tried) Act 1997 (Vic), version 085 in force as at 30 September 2026: ss. 5C-14K (fitness to stand trial), s. 17 (special hearing), s. 20 (defence of mental impairment), s. 21 (presumptions, burden of proof; s. 21(4) agreement of the parties), s. 22 (when the question may be raised), s. 23 (effect of the verdict); supervision orders and nominal term
entities.note: No pretrial filter: the jury in the County or Supreme Court decides the mental impairment defence (s. 20) at trial, raised by the accused or, with leave, by the prosecution. If the parties agree, the judge alone may hear the evidence and enter the verdict (s. 21(4)); the VLRC (2014) proposed abolishing this route. The verdict leads to an indefinite supervision order.
