entities.name: Queensland

facts.outcome: Before any trial, the Mental Health Court decides whether the person was of “unsound mind” (Criminal Code s. 27; MHA 2016 s. 109): the proceedings are then discontinued and cannot be resumed (s. 119(1)), and the Court makes a forensic order (hospitalisation) or a treatment support order (ss. 131-145). The person may nevertheless elect to be tried, by written notice to the DPP within 28 days (s. 119(2)-(3)); if the facts are substantially disputed (unless the dispute concerns the mental state), the Court does not decide (s. 117) and the trial proceeds.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The Mental Health Court (a Supreme Court judge assisted by clinicians, without a jury, on the papers and expert reports, not bound by strict rules of evidence) decides before trial and ends the proceedings, but the person concerned may demand to be tried (s. 119(2)).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Decided by the Mental Health Court on a reference (s. 118): permanent unfitness → proceedings discontinued (s. 122) and forensic or treatment support order (s. 131); temporary unfitness → proceedings suspended (s. 121) and order (s. 132), trial resumed if the person becomes fit again (s. 123). No hearing on the facts (no special hearing).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Code 1899 (Qld) s. 27; Mental Health Act 2016 (Qld): ch. 4 (ss. 86-104; s. 90 psychiatrist report on request, s. 101 reference by the chief psychiatrist), ch. 5 (s. 109 unsound mind; s. 110 when reference may be made: the person, their lawyer or the DPP, for a serious offence other than a federal offence; s. 116 decision; s. 117 substantial dispute about whether the person committed the offence (exception where the dispute concerns only the mental condition); s. 117A substantial dispute about a fact material to an expert report; s. 118 fitness; s. 119 discontinuance and election to be tried; ss. 121-123; ss. 125-128 withdrawal; ss. 131-145 forensic and treatment support orders; s. 159; ss. 175 and 183 references by courts; s. 693 hearing generally open to the public). Reform under way: Health Legislation Amendment Bill 2026 (IAS of May 2026; passage not verified) transfers to the Mental Health Court the review of forensic orders made by criminal courts; mentions neither s. 119 nor the election to be tried.
entities.excerpt: the proceeding against the person for the offence is discontinued [...] Despite the court’s decision, the person may elect to be tried for the offence.
entities.note: Ordinary route: reference to the Mental Health Court (accused, lawyer, DPP, chief psychiatrist or court, s. 110), which decides before trial; if unsound mind, end of proceedings and forensic order. But the person concerned may demand, within 28 days, to be tried (s. 119(2)), and the Court does not decide if the facts are substantially disputed (s. 117): trial. Yellow by default, purple at the person's option.

MHC route weakened, but a full trial obtainable on request: purple.

entities.name: Western Australia

facts.outcome: Acquittal “not guilty on account of mental impairment” (Criminal Code s. 27) delivered at trial, followed by a mandatory Part 5 order: custody order (the default for a serious offence, unless the risk can be managed in the community), community supervision order (5 years at most), unconditional release being in principle excluded for a serious offence (s. 46); the custody order is capped by a limiting term (estimate of the sentence that would have been imposed), under the oversight of the Mental Impairment Review Tribunal.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the art. 27 defence is decided at the ordinary trial; the Part 3 “special proceeding” concerns only the unfit accused.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Presumption of fitness (s. 27), test in s. 26; issue raised by the defence, the prosecution or the court before or during trial (s. 28), decided by a magistrate or a judge alone on the balance of probabilities (s. 29). If the accused is unfit and unlikely to become fit within 6 months (12 months exceptionally), special proceeding (ss. 35-37, 41-43): the judge rules on the available evidence (not guilty; not guilty on account of mental impairment; offence committed, beyond reasonable doubt, without conviction), then a Part 5 order.

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Code (WA) s. 27; Criminal Law (Mental Impairment) Act 2023 (WA), in force since 1 September 2024 (replaces the Criminal Law (Mentally Impaired Accused) Act 1996): s. 9 (mental impairment), ss. 26-29 (fitness), ss. 35-37 and 41-43 (special proceeding), ss. 43-46 and 50-53 (orders, limiting term, community supervision), Part 10 (Mental Impairment Review Tribunal)
entities.excerpt: not guilty on account of mental impairment under The Criminal Code section 27
entities.note: The 2023 Act, in force since 1 Sept. 2024, replaces the 1996 Act (indefinite confinement) with limiting terms. No pretrial filter: the defence under art. 27 of the Code is decided at the ordinary trial, then the court imposes a Part 5 order (custody order, community supervision ≤ 5 years or release). An unfit accused is dealt with in a special proceeding, without conviction.

entities.name: South Australia

facts.outcome: If “mental incompetence” (s. 269C) is established on the balance of probabilities and the objective elements of the offence are proved beyond reasonable doubt: finding of not guilty with a declaration of “liability to supervision” (ss. 269F-269G); the court orders release, detention or release on licence (supervision order) for a limiting term. 2025 Act: the wording becomes “conduct proved but not criminally responsible due to mental incompetence”.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the trial judge splits the trial and chooses the sequence (mental competence first, or objective elements first, s. 269E(2)); agreement between the parties can dispense with the inquiry (s. 269F).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: The court assesses unfitness (mental unfitness to stand trial) on the balance of probabilities, after hearing the parties and, if necessary, expert evidence; in the sequence chosen by the judge (ss. 269M-269N), it also decides on the objective elements of the offence beyond reasonable doubt. If the accused is unfit and those elements are established: declaration of liability to supervision (supervision order, limiting term); otherwise a finding of not guilty and release. The parties may agree to dispense with the fitness inquiry (s. 269M(5)).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Law Consolidation Act 1935 (SA) Part 8A: s. 269C (mental competence), s. 269E (reservation of the question), s. 269F (mental competence first), s. 269G (objective elements first), ss. 269M-269N (mental unfitness to stand trial), Div. 4 (supervision). Criminal Law Consolidation (Mental Competence) Amendment Bill 2025, passed by Parliament in March 2025 (change in the wording of the verdict without change of substance; commencement date not verified)
entities.excerpt: the question of the defendant's mental competence to commit the offence must be separated from the remainder of the trial.
entities.note: No pretrial filter: if the accused raises mental incompetence (or if the court so orders, on the prosecution's application or of its own motion), the question is separated from the trial and the judge chooses the sequence (s. 269E). The objective elements must be proved beyond reasonable doubt; finding of not guilty + liability to supervision (ss. 269F-G). 2025 reform: change of wording only.

entities.name: Tasmania

facts.outcome: Verdict “not guilty on the ground of insanity” (Criminal Code s. 16) returned by the Supreme Court jury at trial, then a Supreme Court order (CJMIA s. 21): restriction order (committal to a secure psychiatric unit until discharged by the Supreme Court), supervision order, treatment order or release with or without conditions; review by the Tribunal at least every 12 months (s. 37).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter identified: insanity is decided by the jury at trial; agreement between the parties is provided for only in relation to fitness (s. 19).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Presumption of fitness, proof on the balance of probabilities (ss. 8-9); in the Supreme Court the question is decided by a jury (s. 12), or found by agreement of the parties (s. 19). If the accused may become fit within 12 months, the proceedings are adjourned (s. 14); otherwise a special hearing before a jury “on the limited evidence available” (s. 15): not guilty, not guilty on the ground of insanity, or a finding that an acquittal is not possible (s. 17), then s. 21 orders.

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Code Act 1924 (Tas), Schedule 1, s. 16 (insanity); Criminal Justice (Mental Impairment) Act 1999 (Tas): ss. 5, 8-9, 12, 14-19 (fitness, special hearing), s. 21 (orders), ss. 24-26 (restriction order), s. 29A (supervision order), s. 37 (review by the Tribunal); Mental Health Act 2013 (Tas). Authorised version of 2 July 2025; 2019 TLRI report proposing reforms, no comprehensive reform identified.
entities.excerpt: A person is not criminally responsible for an act done or an omission made by him – (a) when afflicted with mental disease
entities.note: No pretrial filter: insanity (s. 16, including irresistible impulse caused by mental disease) is decided by the Supreme Court jury at trial; only that court can make a restriction order (confinement until the order is discharged) or a supervision order (CJMIA s. 21). Review by the Tribunal at least every 12 months (s. 37). An unfit accused comes under a special hearing (ss. 14-17).

entities.name: Australian Capital Territory

facts.outcome: Special verdict “not guilty because of mental impairment” (Criminal Code 2002 s. 28) returned at trial, by the jury or by the judge alone on the accused's election, then Supreme Court orders (Crimes Act 1900 ss. 323-324, depending on seriousness): detention for immediate review by the ACAT, submission to the ACAT's jurisdiction (mental health order or forensic mental health order, Mental Health Act 2015) or other orders.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the special verdict is returned at trial (a plea of not guilty because of mental impairment is provided for in s. 321); the Magistrates Court has its own powers (Div. 13.4 and 13.6).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Presumption of fitness (s. 312); question raised by the parties or the court (s. 313), inquiry (ss. 314-315A). If the accused is unfit and unlikely to become fit (s. 315C): special hearing (s. 316) with the verdicts of s. 317 (acquittal, not guilty because of mental impairment or “non-acquittal”, ss. 318-319), then Supreme Court orders; temporary unfitness: s. 315D; resumption possible if the accused becomes fit again (s. 319A).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Code 2002 (ACT) s. 28 (mental impairment); Crimes Act 1900 (ACT) Part 13: Div. 13.2 (unfitness to plead, ss. 310-319A, special hearing s. 316), Div. 13.3 (Supreme Court – plea and special verdict, ss. 321-324), Div. 13.4 (Magistrates Court), Div. 13.6 (summary proceedings); Supreme Court Act 1933 (ACT) ss. 68B-68C (trial without jury); Mental Health Act 2015 (ACT) (ACAT). Republication R155 of the Crimes Act as at 23 February 2026.
entities.excerpt: a special verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment is returned or entered
entities.note: The mental impairment defence (Criminal Code 2002 s. 28, test modelled on the Model Criminal Code) is decided at trial, by the jury or by the judge alone if the accused has so elected (Barker case, 2013); the prosecution may also raise it. After the special verdict, the Supreme Court refers the matter to the ACAT, a civil and administrative tribunal, for care or detention measures. No pretrial filter.

entities.name: Northern Territory

facts.outcome: Finding “not guilty because of mental impairment” (Criminal Code s. 43C) made by the jury on the balance of probabilities (s. 43E), or recorded by the court if the parties agree (ss. 43H, 43XA); the court must then declare the person “liable to supervision” or release them unconditionally (s. 43X), then makes a supervision order, custodial (including in prison where there is no practicable alternative) or non-custodial (ss. 43Z-43ZA), of indefinite duration with a fixed term (s. 43ZG) and periodic reviews (ss. 43ZH, 43ZK).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial filter: the jury decides the defence at trial; recording the finding without a trial (ss. 43H, 43XA) requires the prosecution's agreement and is akin to a guilty plea.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Presumption of fitness (s. 43K); the jury decides fitness (the parties may agree, s. 43T). If there is no reasonable prospect of the accused becoming fit within 12 months (s. 43R), the Supreme Court holds a special hearing before judge and jury (Div. 4) “on the evidence available”: not guilty, not guilty because of mental impairment, or offence committed (“qualified finding of guilt”, without conviction); then declaration of liability to supervision or release (s. 43X).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Code Act 1983 (NT), Part IIA (ss. 43A-43ZN, inserted in 2002, amended in 2016): s. 43C (defence of mental impairment), s. 43D (presumption), s. 43E (question of fact for the jury), ss. 43H and 43XA (plea accepted by the court), ss. 43J-43K and 43R (fitness), Div. 4 (special hearing), s. 43X (orders), Div. 5 (supervision orders, ss. 43Z-43ZN); KMD v CEO (Department of Health NT) [2025] HCA 4
entities.excerpt: a question of fact to be determined by a jury on the balance of probabilities
entities.note: Part IIA (2002): the mental impairment defence is a question of fact decided by the jury on the balance of probabilities (s. 43E); with the agreement of the parties, the court may record the finding without a trial (ss. 43H, 43XA, 2016). No pretrial filter. Indefinite supervision order, sometimes served in prison for lack of an alternative (s. 43ZA(2)); fixed term equal to the hypothetical sentence (s. 43ZG).

entities.name: New Zealand

facts.outcome: Finding “act proven but not criminally responsible on account of insanity” made by the jury (or judge alone) at trial, then acquittal entered by the judge (CP(MIP)A s. 20(1)); the court orders inquiries (s. 23, 30 days) then a measure: special patient (hospital) or special care recipient if the public interest requires it (s. 24), patient or care recipient, or release (s. 25).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Default route: the jury decides at trial; before or during the trial, the judge must find non-responsibility if the accused raises it, the prosecution accepts it as the only reasonable verdict and the expert evidence establishes it (s. 20(2)), a consensual route comparable to a guilty plea.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Found by the judge on the evidence of two health assessors, on the balance of probabilities (s. 8A); then involvement hearing: the evidence must be sufficient to establish that the accused caused the act, otherwise the charge is dismissed (ss. 10-13), and the hearing may be held in the accused's absence (s. 15). Then an order (special patient, special care recipient, etc., ss. 24-25); proceedings stayed, fresh prosecution barred (s. 27), resumption possible if the accused becomes fit again (s. 31), detention capped (s. 30).

entities.legal_bases: Crimes Act 1961 s. 23 (insanity); Criminal Procedure (Mentally Impaired Persons) Act 2003: s. 4 (unfit to stand trial), ss. 7-8A and 10-13, 15 (unfitness, involvement hearing), s. 20 (replaced on 13 December 2022 by the Rights for Victims of Insane Offenders Act 2021), s. 38 (assessment reports), ss. 23-25 (orders), ss. 27, 30-32 (stay, detention cap, resumption). Consolidated version of 17 June 2025: s. 20 unchanged since 2022. Review of the 2003 Act on the Law Commission's work programme (project page accessed; status “not yet commenced” according to the indexed title, unconfirmed): no adopted reform found.
entities.excerpt: the jury or (if there is no jury) the Judge makes a finding of act proven but not criminally responsible on account of insanity
entities.note: Default route: the jury (or judge alone) decides insanity at trial, even if the accused has not raised it (s. 20(5)); the court may order an expert examination (s. 38). Consensual route (s. 20(2)): before or during the trial, the judge finds non-responsibility if the accused raises it, the prosecution accepts it and the expert evidence confirms it; it does not displace the trial.

entities.name: United States (federal courts)

facts.outcome: Special verdict “not guilty only by reason of insanity” + automatic committal (18 U.S.C. § 4243), release if the person concerned proves the absence of substantial risk
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: insanity is decided only at trial, by the jury or the judge, in a special verdict.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: 18 U.S.C. § 4241: hospitalisation for restoration (4 months, extendable if there is a substantial probability); failing that, federal civil committal if dangerous (§ 4246, clear and convincing evidence) or release; no examination of the facts.

entities.legal_bases: 18 U.S.C. § 17 (Insanity Defense Reform Act 1984); 18 U.S.C. §§ 4241, 4242, 4243, 4246, 4247; Fed. R. Crim. P. 12.2; United States v. Read, 918 F.3d 712 (9th Cir. 2019)
entities.excerpt: as a result of a severe mental disease or defect, was unable to appreciate the nature and quality or the wrongfulness of his acts
entities.note: Affirmative defence (clear and convincing evidence) that only the accused can raise, by prior notice (R. 12.2); the government's expert examination is ordered only after that notice (§ 4242(a)). Special verdict at trial; automatic committal then a hearing within 40 days at which the person must prove the absence of risk. Imposing the defence on a fit accused is an error (Read, 2019).

independent_check.reasoning: Read 18 U.S.C. § 4242: the government's expert examination is ordered only after the accused's notice (R. 12.2) announcing the insanity defence; special verdict “not guilty only by reason of insanity” at trial (§ 4242(b)). Read (9th Cir. 2019, via JAAPL): imposing this defence on a fit accused is reversible error. Blue.

entities.name: District of Columbia

facts.outcome: Acquittal by reason of insanity (NGRI, ALI/Brawner test) followed by automatic committal to a psychiatric hospital (§ 24-501(d)(1)), with a hearing within 50 days at which the committed person bears the burden of proof (preponderance)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: ordinary trial (often bifurcated), insanity being established by a preponderance regardless of who raises the issue (§ 24-501(j)).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: D.C. Code §§ 24-531.01 et seq.: restoration treatment in periods, with hearings; absent a substantial probability of regaining fitness in the foreseeable future, the court orders release or, if necessary, treatment for the duration of civil committal proceedings (titles 21 or 7) (§ 24-531.06); trial resumes if fit; no examination of the facts.

entities.legal_bases: D.C. Code § 24-501(c), (d), (j), (k); D.C. Code §§ 24-531.01 to 24-531.09; Super. Ct. Crim. R. 12.2; Frendak v. United States, 408 A.2d 364 (D.C. 1979); Phenis v. United States, 909 A.2d 138 (D.C. 2006); Maziarz v. United States, No. 22-CM-898 (D.C. 2024)
entities.excerpt: the court cannot raise the defense over the defendant's voluntary and intelligent rejection
entities.note: ALI/Brawner test. The court cannot raise insanity against the accused's voluntary and informed rejection of it (Frendak; Maziarz 2024, p. 12); it can if the accused is incapable of a valid waiver, after a Frendak inquiry and expert examination (Phenis). Expert examination on the prosecution's motion or of the court's own motion “in an appropriate case” (R. 12.2(c)). Role of the prosecution not decided by Maziarz.

history.note: ALI/Brawner test; insanity is established by a preponderance “regardless of who raises the issue”. The judge may raise it of their own motion and must inquire if mental health is seriously in question (Frendak; Maziarz 2024), but cannot impose it on an accused who waives it in an informed and voluntary manner; imposition takes place in an insanity phase after the guilt phase.

entities.name: Puerto Rico

facts.outcome: Acquittal for mental incapacity (non-imputability, art. 40 CP 2012) at trial, or “determinación de no causa” at the vista preliminar for the same reason; then, if the person's dangerousness makes them a risk to society, a security measure of committal ordered by the court (Regla 241), for as long as the safety of society requires, with quarterly reports
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Pretrial route possible: a “determinación de no causa” at the vista preliminar for mental incapacity opens the way, without trial, to the Regla 241 security measure; otherwise the defence notified by the accused (Regla 74) is decided at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Regla 239 (no one may be tried, convicted or sentenced while mentally incapacitated); Regla 240: on reasonable grounds, the court suspends the proceedings and appoints experts, then institutional treatment with periodic re-evaluations. Permanent unfitness: Regla 241 as in force (Ley 281-2011) allows a security measure without trial (left in place in 2024 TSPR 55, certiorari denied), whereas Pueblo v. Santiago Torres and the Court of Appeals (Nieves Linares, 2023) require dismissal followed by release or civil committal (Ley 408-2000); P. del S. 669 (2025), pending, would abolish this route.

entities.legal_bases: Código Penal de Puerto Rico de 2012 (Ley 146-2012), art. 40; Reglas de Procedimiento Criminal 74, 239, 240 y 241 (as amended by Ley 317-2004 and Ley 281-2011); Ley 408-2000 (Ley de Salud Mental); Pueblo v. Pérez Velázquez, 99 TSPR 25; Pueblo v. Encarnación Santos, 2000 TSPR 37
entities.excerpt: Cuando el imputado fuere absuelto o hubiere una determinación de no causa en vista preliminar por razón de incapacidad mental
entities.note: Defence notified by the accused (Regla 74); the court appoints a neutral expert, the prosecution cannot impose its own (Pérez Velázquez 1999; Encarnación Santos 2000). Acquittal at trial or “no causa” at the vista preliminar, then security measure (Regla 241). Initiative for and use of the preliminary route not verified; current Regla 74 not read. No reform adopted (P. del S. 669 pending).

entities.name: Connecticut

facts.outcome: Verdict “not guilty by reason of mental disease or defect” + 60-day examination, then release or placement under the jurisdiction of the Psychiatric Security Review Board for a period ≤ the maximum sentence that could have been imposed
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: the affirmative defence is decided at an ordinary trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: C.G.S. § 54-56d: examination at the request of the defence, the State or the judge, subject to probable cause; restoration ≤ 18 months or the maximum sentence; if not restorable, release or DMHAS custody with possible civil committal, then nolle or dismissal of the charges on expiry of the limitation period for prosecution; no hearing on the merits.

entities.legal_bases: C.G.S. § 53a-13; C.G.S. §§ 17a-580 to 17a-603 (PSRB), in particular § 17a-582; C.G.S. § 54-56d; Practice Book § 40-17
entities.excerpt: lacked substantial capacity, as a result of mental disease or defect, either to appreciate the wrongfulness of his conduct or to control his conduct
entities.note: Affirmative defence proved by the accused (preponderance), with the State still required to prove the act beyond reasonable doubt; decided at an ordinary trial, with no pretrial route. After acquittal, the “acquittee” is evaluated for 60 days and then, unless released (very rare), placed under the jurisdiction of the PSRB, which decides on hospitalisation and conditional releases.

entities.name: Delaware

facts.outcome: Verdict “not guilty by reason of insanity” + committal to the Delaware Psychiatric Center on the Attorney General's motion, until the Superior Court finds that public safety is not threatened
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: the affirmative defence is decided at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: 11 Del. C. § 404: committal and treatment at the Delaware Psychiatric Center until fit; at the defence's request, a hearing at which the State must establish a prima facie case, failing which the charges are dismissed with the effect of an acquittal.

entities.legal_bases: 11 Del. C. §§ 401, 402, 403, 404; Super. Ct. Crim. R. 12.2; cf. Cooke v. State, 977 A.2d 803 (Del. 2009)
entities.excerpt: lacked substantial capacity to appreciate the wrongfulness of the accused's conduct
entities.note: Cognitive test (substantial inability to appreciate the wrongfulness of the act); affirmative defence with the burden on the accused, decided at trial, with no pretrial route. After NGRI, committal to a secure building on the AG's motion; the Superior Court reviews of its own motion the need for detention after one year. For an unfit accused, a prima facie hearing at their request may amount to an acquittal.

entities.name: Maine

facts.outcome: Verdict, finding or negotiated plea “not criminally responsible by reason of insanity” + committal to the custody of the Commissioner of Health and Human Services (15 M.R.S. § 103)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Optional: the court may accept a negotiated NCR plea (agreement of the accused and the State), without trial; otherwise decided at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: 15 M.R.S. § 101-D(5): case continued until fit, placement with the DHHS or release on conditions, reports at 30, 60 and 180 days; absent a substantial probability of recovery, dismissal of all charges and possible civil committal proceedings.

entities.excerpt: as a result of mental disease or defect, the defendant lacked substantial capacity to appreciate the wrongfulness of the criminal conduct
entities.note: Affirmative defence of the accused (NCR plea, which triggers a mandatory expert examination). The State may also request an evaluation of responsibility and the judge may order it despite the accused's objection, but the report is then sealed. Outcome: accepted negotiated plea or verdict at trial; committal to the DHHS, release decided by the court (§ 104-A).

entities.name: Maryland

facts.outcome: Verdict “not criminally responsible” (NCR) + committal to the facility designated by the Maryland Department of Health, unless released on a favourable report with the agreement of the accused and the prosecutor
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: written NCR plea by the defence, then a two-stage decision at trial (the act, then responsibility).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Crim. Proc. §§ 3-104 to 3-108: committal or treatment for restoration; mandatory dismissal of the charges after the lesser of 5 years (serious or violent crime; 3 years otherwise) and the maximum sentence, unless extended for extraordinary cause; discretionary dismissal if resuming would be unjust.

entities.excerpt: the defendant or defense counsel shall file a written plea
entities.note: Only the accused or their counsel may plead NCR, and no NCR verdict is possible without that written plea (§ 3-110(d)); a fit accused may refuse this defence (Treece). The trier of fact first decides whether the State has proved the act, then separately whether the accused has proved NCR (preponderance). Automatic committal to the MDH, subsequent release by court decision.

entities.name: Massachusetts

facts.outcome: Verdict “not guilty by reason of mental illness or defect” + observation (≤ 40 days, Bridgewater if necessary), then civil committal for 6 months, renewable, on petition of the prosecutor or the facility
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: the issue is decided at an ordinary trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: G.L. c. 123 §§ 15-17: trial suspended, observation then civil committal; the unfit accused may request a non-jury hearing on a defence on the merits (other than insanity), with dismissal of the charges if the evidence is insufficient (§ 17(b)); mandatory dismissal on the notional parole date calculated on the maximum sentence (§ 16(f)).

entities.legal_bases: Commonwealth v. McHoul, 352 Mass. 544 (1967); G.L. c. 123, §§ 15, 16, 17, 18; Mass. R. Crim. P. 14(b)(2)
entities.excerpt: notify the prosecutor in writing of such intention
entities.note: ALI test (McHoul); once the issue is raised, the prosecution must prove responsibility beyond reasonable doubt. The judge may order a responsibility examination at any stage (c. 123 § 15(a)), but the defence depends on the accused's notice (R. 14(b)(2)) and the prosecution's expert examination remains sealed unless and until the accused maintains this defence.

entities.name: New Hampshire

facts.outcome: NGRI verdict (or NGRI plea accepted by the prosecutor) + automatic committal to a secure psychiatric unit, hearing within 40 days, then committal for 5 years, renewable, if dangerousness is proved by clear and convincing evidence
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Optional: NGRI plea by the accused accepted by the prosecutor and certified to the court (RSA 651:8-a), without trial; otherwise decided at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: RSA 135:17-a: restoration treatment with a hearing within 12 months; if restoration is impossible within that period (clear and convincing evidence), dismissal of the charges without prejudice and continued custody for up to 90 days for evaluation with a view to civil committal (RSA 135-C, 171-B) if dangerous.

entities.excerpt: Any person prosecuted for an offense may plead that he is not guilty by reason of insanity or mental derangement.
entities.note: “Product” test (Pike/Jones): insanity is a question of fact left to the jury; clear and convincing evidence by the accused, who must give notice of the defence (RSA 628:2 III). Distinctive features: either party may raise a “sanity” issue with the judge and trigger an expert examination (135:17); an NGRI plea accepted by the prosecutor is certified to the court, without trial (651:8-a).

entities.name: New Jersey

facts.outcome: Acquittal by reason of insanity stated in the verdict + psychiatric examination, then release, conditional release or committal reviewed periodically (“Krol”), capped at the ordinary maximum sentence
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route provided for by the Code: the defence is decided at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: N.J.S.A. 2C:4-6: proceedings suspended, possible placement with the Commissioner of Human Services; after 3 months without restoration, hearing on dismissal with prejudice or continued suspension (presumed), according to the seriousness of the offence, the duration and the prospects of recovery; legal objections possible without the accused.

entities.excerpt: he shall serve notice of such intention upon the prosecuting attorney in accordance with the Rules of Court
entities.note: M'Naghten test; affirmative defence proved by the accused (preponderance) after notice to the prosecutor (2C:4-3). Decided at an ordinary trial, with no pretrial route. After acquittal, psychiatric examination and decision by the judge: release, conditions or committal treated as civil committal, with the prosecutor heard at reviews, capped at the ordinary maximum sentence (2C:4-8).

entities.name: New York State

facts.outcome: Verdict or plea “not responsible by reason of mental disease or defect” + examination order then initial hearing (CPL 330.20): dangerous mental disorder → secure facility; mental illness → committal; otherwise order of conditions
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Optional: plea of not responsible (CPL 220.15) with the consent of the court and the prosecution, the judge finding that the act would be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: CPL art. 730: observation orders then retention orders (1 year, then 2 years); total duration ≤ 2/3 of the maximum sentence for the most serious felony; on expiry, the criminal action ends and the indictment is dismissed; misdemeanours: final 90-day observation and dismissal.

entities.excerpt: lacked substantial capacity to know or appreciate either: 1. The nature and consequences of such conduct; or 2. That such conduct was wrong.
entities.note: Affirmative defence of the accused, who must give notice of intent to present psychiatric evidence (CPL 250.10). Two routes at the accused's choice: plea of not responsible accepted by the judge and the prosecutor, with detailed findings (220.15), or verdict at trial. Then CPL 330.20: examination, initial hearing, retention orders and orders of conditions under judicial supervision.

entities.name: Pennsylvania

facts.outcome: Verdict “not guilty by reason of insanity” (or acquittal entered at the fitness hearing) + petition for involuntary treatment (MHPA §§ 406 and 304), up to 1 year, renewable, for serious crimes
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Optional: at the fitness hearing, the judge may, at their discretion, rule on responsibility under the rules applicable at trial and acquit (MHPA § 404(a)).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: MHPA § 403: prosecution suspended for as long as the incapacity lasts, detention limited to a reasonable period for evaluation; suspension capped at the maximum sentence or 10 years, except for first- or second-degree murder (no limit); dismissal possible if resuming would be unjust; involuntary treatment via § 304.

entities.excerpt: the court may, in its discretion, also hear evidence on whether the person was criminally responsible for the commission of the crime charged
entities.note: M'Naghten test, proof by the accused (preponderance). Ordinary route: defence raised by the accused at trial, bifurcation possible in the interest of justice, where appropriate before a separate jury (§ 404(c)). Alternative route: acquittal entered at the fitness hearing (§ 404(a)); failing that, the defence remains open at trial. Committal on petition (§ 406).

entities.name: Rhode Island

facts.outcome: Acquittal by reason of insanity + committal for observation (report within 20 days), hearing, then committal if unsupervised presence creates a serious risk of harm, review every 6 months
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route identified: the defence is decided at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: R.I. Gen. Laws § 40.1-5.3-3: examination at the request of the parties or the judge; restoration committal with six-monthly review; absent a reasonable probability of recovery, civil committal possible; dismissal of the charges after 2/3 of the maximum sentence (30 years if life imprisonment); issues may be decided without the accused.

entities.excerpt: the person's unsupervised presence in the community will create a likelihood of serious harm
entities.note: Modified ALI test (State v. Johnson, 1979); defence raised by the accused and decided at an ordinary trial. After acquittal, the court orders observation, then holds an adversarial hearing; continued committal requires clear and convincing evidence of risk, with no maximum duration, with six-monthly review and petitions by the person concerned.

entities.name: Vermont

facts.outcome: Acquittal by reason of insanity (ground stated by the jury) + committal hearing; for offences punishable by life imprisonment, committal to a secure forensic facility (13 V.S.A. § 4819a)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No ordinary route: committal on a mere pretrial insanity report was repealed in 2023; there remains non-indictment by a grand jury on grounds of insanity (§ 4818), which is rare.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: 13 V.S.A. § 4817: no trial of an unfit accused; committal hearing (§ 4820(a)(2)) and supervised restoration (§ 4815a); misdemeanours: dismissal without prejudice after a period of inactivity equal to the maximum sentence; interim forensic programme (Act 147 of 2026) pending the secure facility planned for 2029.

entities.excerpt: The defendant shall have the burden of proof in establishing insanity as an affirmative defense
entities.note: 2023 reform (Act 28): the accused must obtain the responsibility expert examination themselves (paid for by the Defender General if indigent); the judge can no longer order it of their own motion, and the former pretrial committal hearing on an insanity report (§ 4820(a)(1)), which allowed committal without trial, has been repealed. Decided at trial, then forensic committal (§ 4819a).

entities.name: Virginia

facts.outcome: Acquittal by reason of insanity stated in the verdict + temporary custody of the DBHDS Commissioner for evaluation, then committal or release (with or without conditions) under the court's supervision
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: the defence is decided at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Va. Code §§ 19.2-169.1 to 169.3: restoration in 6-month periods; if the incompetence is lasting, release, civil committal or certification; dismissal of the charges on expiry of the sentence that could have been imposed or 5 years after arrest, except for aggravated murder (no dismissal, secure treatment, annual then biennial hearings).

entities.legal_bases: Case law (M'Naghten + irresistible impulse); Va. Code §§ 19.2-168, 19.2-168.1, 19.2-169.5, 19.2-182.2 to 19.2-182.16; §§ 19.2-169.1 to 19.2-169.3 (amended by 2026, c. 502, in force from 1 July 2027)
entities.excerpt: he, or his counsel, shall give notice in writing to the attorney for the Commonwealth, at least 60 days prior to his trial
entities.note: Defence raised by the accused, who must notify the prosecutor 60 days before trial (§ 19.2-168); the evaluation requested by the Commonwealth takes place only after that notice (§ 19.2-168.1). Decided at an ordinary trial. After acquittal, temporary DBHDS custody for evaluation, then a court decision on committal or conditional release.

entities.name: West Virginia

facts.outcome: Verdict “not guilty by reason of mental illness” + court jurisdiction until expiry of the maximum sentence, dangerousness evaluation, hospitalisation or conditional release
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: the issue is decided at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: W. Va. Code § 27-6A-3: restoration (90 days; 240 days max. in hospital); not restorable: non-violent charges dismissed without prejudice, violent charges held in abeyance for the maximum sentence under the court's supervision; § 27-6A-6: the unfit accused may request a non-jury hearing on the merits, with dismissal if the evidence is insufficient.

entities.legal_bases: State v. Milam, 163 W. Va. 752, 260 S.E.2d 295 (1979); W. Va. Code §§ 27-6A-1 to 27-6A-13 (in particular 27-6A-3, -4, -5, -6); W. Va. R. Crim. P. 12.2
entities.excerpt: The acquittee shall remain under the court's jurisdiction until the expiration of the maximum sentence
entities.note: ALI test (Milam); once the issue is raised, the State must prove responsibility. The evaluation of state of mind at the time of the offence is ordered when, in light of the evidence or the statements of defence counsel, responsibility will be a significant factor in the defence. Decided at trial; the acquittee remains under the court's jurisdiction until the maximum sentence expires.

entities.name: North Carolina

facts.outcome: NGRI verdict or pretrial finding on motion + automatic committal to a 24-hour facility (forensic unit if serious injury or death), then chapter 122C hearings
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Optional: pretrial hearing on insanity at the accused's request and with the State's consent, which may result in dismissal of the charges with prejudice (§ 15A-959(c)).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: N.C.G.S. §§ 15A-1001 to 1008: an unfit accused cannot be tried; examination, civil committal (ch. 122C); dismissal of the charges if recovery is unlikely, after a deprivation of liberty equal to the maximum sentence (final), or after 5 years (misdemeanours) / 10 years (felonies); no hearing on the merits.

entities.excerpt: it may dismiss that charge, with prejudice, upon making a finding to that effect
entities.note: M'Naghten test, proof by the accused, defence notified by the accused (§ 15A-959(a)). Distinctive feature: on the accused's motion and with the State's consent, the judge may hold a pretrial hearing on insanity and dismiss the charges with prejudice; if refused, the defence remains fully available at trial. The finding, pretrial or by verdict, entails automatic committal (§ 15A-1321).

entities.name: South Carolina

facts.outcome: NGRI verdict + committal to the State hospital for evaluation (≤ 120 days), hearing within 15 days before the chief administrative judge, committal or release on therapeutic conditions, capped at the maximum sentence
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: the affirmative defence is decided at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: S.C. Code §§ 44-23-410 to 460: examination ordered by the judge; unfit and not restorable: the solicitor initiates civil committal within 14 days; restoration up to 180 days; the unfit accused may present a defence on the merits (other than insanity), dismissal if a directed verdict of acquittal would be required; dismissal if hospitalisation exceeds the maximum sentence.

entities.excerpt: lacked the capacity to distinguish moral or legal right from moral or legal wrong
entities.note: M'Naghten-type test; affirmative defence proved by the accused (preponderance) and decided at trial, with no pretrial route. After NGRI, evaluation at the State hospital, then a hearing before the chief administrative judge under the civil committal standard; beyond the maximum sentence, only full civil committal proceedings allow an extension.

entities.name: Alabama

facts.outcome: special NGRI verdict (jury) + probable cause hearing then committal to the Department of Mental Health if mentally ill and dangerous
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: insanity is decided at an ordinary trial and found by a special jury verdict.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Trial suspended; committal to the State hospital until restoration, with no release while the prosecution is pending (§ 15-16-21; Ala. R. Crim. P. 11); if not restorable, civil committal.

entities.excerpt: the defendant, as a result of severe mental disease or defect, was unable to appreciate the nature and quality or wrongfulness of his acts
entities.note: Affirmative defence raised by the accused (special NGRMDD plea), clear and convincing evidence with the burden on the accused; examination may also be ordered by the judge (R. 11; § 15-16-22, capital crimes; texts not read). Unitary trial, special jury verdict (§ 15-16-24); then probable cause hearing and committal if mentally ill and dangerous (§ 15-16-41 et seq.).

entities.name: Arkansas

facts.outcome: Acquittal for lack of criminal responsibility (ALI test) entered by the judge on the expert report without trial or, failing that, by the jury; then detention by the Department of Human Services for examination and a committal hearing (§ 5-2-314), the burden of proof for release resting on the acquitted person
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: After notice of the defence by the accused, the judge may, on the expert report, acquit without trial, with a hearing only if requested (§ 5-2-313); failing that, jury trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Fitness examination ordered by the court of its own motion or on the written motion of any party (§ 5-2-327); proceedings suspended; restoration entrusted to the Department of Human Services (report within 6 months, decision within 8 months); unfit and dangerous: petition for involuntary committal; dismissal on the State's motion at any time, after 5 continuous years of unfitness (without prejudice) or if resuming would be unjust given the time elapsed (§ 5-2-310, as amended by Act 733 of 2025); no examination of the facts.

entities.excerpt: if and only if a defendant charged in circuit court files a notice of intent to raise the affirmative defense of lack of criminal responsibility
entities.note: The expert examination on responsibility is available only if the accused gives notice of the defence (§§ 5-2-304, 5-2-328: “if and only if”); then the judge or the parties appoint the experts. On the report, the judge may acquit without trial (hearing if requested, § 5-2-313), otherwise jury. § 5-2-313(b) (finding of facts if the defence has not been raised): scope not verified. Blue: the accused controls the trigger.

Failing that, jury. Presumed to be the ordinary route in clear cases (practice not verified).

entities.name: Florida

facts.outcome: NGRI verdict (jury or judge) + committal if mentally ill and manifestly dangerous, or outpatient treatment
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No statutory pretrial route identified: the NGRI judgment is rendered by the jury or the judge at trial (Fla. R. Crim. P. 3.217).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Proceedings suspended; committal for restoration (Fla. Stat. § 916.13; R. 3.210-3.215); dismissal without prejudice after 5 years of continuous unfitness, or after only 3 years except for serious offences such as murder (§ 916.145).

entities.excerpt: did not know what he or she was doing or its consequences
entities.note: Statutory M'Naghten test (§ 775.027), clear and convincing evidence with the burden on the accused. The defence must be notified by the accused (R. 3.216), the State's expert examination following that notice; unitary trial, NGRI judgment by the jury or the judge (R. 3.217, to which § 916.15 refers). Text of the rules not read (PDF unreadable); no statutory pretrial route identified.

entities.name: Georgia

facts.outcome: verdict “not guilty by reason of insanity at the time of the crime” + evaluation detention ≤ 30 days, hearing and committal if civil criteria are met
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: insanity is decided at trial by the jury or the judge.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Special plea of incapacity decided by the judge or a special jury; restoration by the DBHDD ≤ 9 months; if not restorable: nolle prosequi or trial solely on civil committal criteria (clear and convincing evidence), committal capped at the maximum sentence (§ 17-7-130, as amended 2024-2025).

entities.excerpt: When notice of an insanity defense is filed, the court shall appoint at least one psychiatrist or licensed psychologist
entities.note: Right/wrong test (§ 16-3-2) or delusional compulsion (§ 16-3-3). Defence notified by the accused; court-ordered expert examination mandatory upon notice (§ 17-7-130.1); unitary trial. After NGRI: evaluation detention ≤ 30 days, hearing, committal if civil criteria are met, continuing jurisdiction of the trial judge. GBMI verdict disregarded.

entities.name: Kentucky

facts.outcome: NGRI verdict (jury) + civil involuntary hospitalisation proceedings ordered by the judge (KRS 202A/202B)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: insanity is decided by the jury at the ordinary trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No trial while the incapacity lasts (KRS 504.090); treatment ≤ 60 days if restoration is likely; otherwise involuntary committal: KRS 202C on the prosecutor's petition for serious felonies, KRS 202A/202B for the others (KRS 504.110, 2024 version).

entities.excerpt: shall file written notice of his or her intention at least ninety (90) days before trial
entities.note: ALI test (KRS 504.020). The accused must give notice 90 days before trial of the intention to raise insanity (KRS 504.070, 2024 version); the examination ordered by the judge falls within this framework; no provision allows the judge or the prosecutor to raise the defence. Unitary trial; after NGRI, involuntary hospitalisation under civil law (KRS 504.030).

entities.name: Louisiana

facts.outcome: NGRI verdict (jury) or NGRI adjudication without trial with the prosecutor's agreement + adversarial hearing and committal if dangerous
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Consensual option: NGRI adjudication without trial if the prosecutor consents and an expert examination establishes a factual basis (art. 558.1).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Proceedings suspended (art. 648); restoration (Feliciana Forensic Facility, prison or outpatient), capped at the maximum sentence; if restoration is unlikely, adversarial hearing then release or civil committal; charges dropped on expiry of the maximum sentence or after 5 years, except for violent felonies (2025 version).

entities.excerpt: When a defendant is tried upon a plea of "not guilty", evidence of insanity or mental defect ... shall not be admissible
entities.note: M'Naghten test (R.S. 14:14). Insanity is admissible only on the accused's plea of “not guilty and not guilty by reason of insanity” (arts. 552, 651); then a sanity commission (art. 650); both defences are tried together. Consensual route without trial (art. 558.1) if the prosecutor consents; the accused can always demand a trial.

entities.name: Mississippi

facts.outcome: Acquittal by reason of insanity (M'Naghten test) returned by the jury, which states whether the accused has recovered and is dangerous; if still insane and dangerous, committal to a State psychiatric hospital, with a presumption of illness and dangerousness rebuttable by clear and convincing evidence (§ 99-13-7)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Ordinary route: jury trial after notice of the defence by the accused (R. 17.4(b)); old routes without trial (justice of the peace § 99-13-3, grand jury § 99-13-5) exist but their use in homicide cases is not attested.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Examination ordered of the court's own motion or on application by any party as soon as there are reasonable grounds (R. 12.2(a); § 99-13-11); fitness hearing (R. 12.5); if unfit, treatment at Mississippi State Hospital for periods of 4 months at most with reports; absent a substantial probability of regaining fitness, civil committal proceedings (§ 41-21-61 et seq.; referral to the chancery court, § 41-21-63, 2019 version), the person remaining in custody until the decision; no examination of the facts provided for.

entities.legal_bases: Miss. Code Ann. §§ 99-13-3, 99-13-5, 99-13-7, 99-13-11, 41-21-63; Miss. R. Crim. P. 12.2, 12.3, 12.5, 17.4(b) (carrying over former URCCC 9.05 to 9.07); case-law M'Naghten test
entities.excerpt: If the defendant has timely raised a defense of insanity pursuant to Rule 17.4(b), […] may order the defendant to submit to a mental examination
entities.note: M'Naghten test. Examination of mental state at the time of the act is possible only if the accused has given notice of insanity (R. 12.2(b), 17.4(b)); defence decided at trial, the jury rules on recovery and dangerousness (§ 99-13-7). Old routes without trial (justice of the peace § 99-13-3; grand jury § 99-13-5): use in homicide cases not verified. Case law on refusal of the defence not read.

entities.name: Tennessee

facts.outcome: NGRI verdict (jury) + evaluation, then judicial hospitalisation or mandatory outpatient treatment
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the affirmative defence of insanity is decided by the jury at trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Evaluation of the court's own motion or on application (§ 33-7-301(a)); if unfit, judicial hospitalisation (jury possible) with six-monthly reports on the probability of restoration; misdemeanour charges withdrawn no later than 2 years after arrest; no verified dismissal rule for felonies.

entities.excerpt: The defendant has the burden of proving the defense of insanity by clear and convincing evidence.
entities.note: Test: inability to appreciate the nature or wrongfulness of the acts (§ 39-11-501), clear and convincing evidence, burden on the accused, who must give notice of the defence (R. 12.2). The judge may order, of their own motion, an evaluation of mental state at the time of the act (§ 33-7-301(a)): mixed triggering, but the defence remains at the accused's initiative. Unitary trial.

facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: insanity is decided by the jury at the ordinary trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Proceedings suspended; restoration if possible within a reasonable time (extendable up to a limit of 2 years or the maximum sentence); otherwise civil committal and dismissal without prejudice, the limitation period being suspended (22 O.S. § 1175.6a, 2025 version).

entities.excerpt: Mentally ill persons, and all persons of unsound mind, including persons temporarily or partially deprived of reason ... incapable of knowing its wrongfulness

entities.name: Texas

facts.outcome: NGRI verdict (jury or judge) or consensual dismissal on grounds of insanity + evaluation, committal or treatment under the judge's jurisdiction

facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Proceedings suspended; restoration in hospital, in prison or on an outpatient basis, cumulative duration capped at the maximum sentence (art. 46B.0095); then civil committal with charges pending or dismissed (arts. 46B.101 et seq., 46B.151); the prosecution may dismiss at any time.

entities.name: Alaska

facts.outcome: “not guilty by reason of insanity” verdict + immediate committal to the commissioner of health, unless there is an opinion that the person is no longer “dangerously mentally ill”; the person must then prove by clear and convincing evidence that they are not dangerous (AS 12.47.090); conditional release possible (12.47.092)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: the defence, notified by the accused within 10 days of the plea (12.47.010(b)), is decided at trial; the judge appoints two experts (12.47.070).

entities.name: California

facts.outcome: “not guilty by reason of insanity” verdict at the end of the responsibility phase (sanity phase) + committal to the Department of State Hospitals or outpatient treatment (CONREP) ordered by the court, for a term not exceeding the maximum sentence, extendable in 2-year periods (PC 1026, 1026.5)

entities.name: Hawaii

facts.outcome: acquittal “on the ground of physical or mental disease, disorder, or defect excluding responsibility” (stated in the verdict and the judgment) then, depending on the danger, committal to the director of health, conditional release or discharge ordered by the court (HRS 704-411)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None since Act 222 of 1980: pretrial acquittal on the accused's motion (Model Penal Code approach) was replaced by submission of the defence to the jury or the trial judge at the single trial.

entities.name: Oregon

facts.outcome: “guilty except for insanity” (GEI) verdict, which is not a conviction: the court finds a qualifying mental disorder and a substantial danger, then commits to a State hospital under the jurisdiction of the Psychiatric Security Review Board (PSRB) or orders conditional release, for a term not exceeding the maximum sentence (ORS 161.327)

entities.name: South Korea

facts.outcome: Ordinary public trial then acquittal for 심신상실 (CP art. 10 para. 1), with placement in 치료감호 (therapeutic confinement) ordered by the same court at the prosecution's request; variant: request for 치료감호 alone without indictment (Act art. 7), also decided at a hearing.

facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Trial suspended for as long as the accused is incapable of discernment or volition, after a physician's opinion (CPP art. 306), unless acquittal, exemption or inadmissibility is manifest; no statutory cap identified; in a request for 치료감호 alone, hearing possible without the person concerned if their illness prevents them from appearing (Act art. 9).

entities.name: India

facts.outcome: Acquittal by reason of insanity (BNSS s. 373) with an express finding as to whether or not the accused committed the act; if so, detention in safe custody (public mental health establishment under State rules made under the Mental Healthcare Act 2017) or delivery to a relative or friend (s. 374); release by the State government after certification (s. 377)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: even if insanity at the time of the offence appears established, the magistrate “shall proceed with the case” and, where appropriate, commits the accused to the Court of Session (BNSS s. 372).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Inquiry by the magistrate (BNSS s. 367) or issue tried first by the court during the trial (s. 368), on the present capacity to make a defence only: civil surgeon, then psychiatrist or clinical psychologist (appeal by the accused to a Medical Board). If the accused is unfit: examination of the prosecution evidence without questioning the accused; no prima facie case: discharge; otherwise adjournment during treatment; intellectual disability: no trial. Release on security, or custody in a place of psychiatric care with a report to the State (s. 369). HC Madras (Kaliyappan, 2020): discharge possible for an unfit accused with an incurable illness by invoking art. 84 IPC.

entities.legal_bases: BNS 2023 s. 22 (formerly IPC s. 84); BNSS 2023 ch. XXVII ss. 367-378 (formerly CrPC 1973 ss. 328-339): 367-369 (fitness, release or custody), 372 (proceeding with the case and committal), 373 (acquittal with finding), 374 (detention or delivery), 377 (release by the State); ss. 370-371, 375-376, 378 not re-read; BSA 2023 s. 108 (burden of proof, not re-read); Mental Healthcare Act 2017 ss. 103 (admission to a mental health establishment on an order made under former ss. 330/335 CrPC), 105 (referral to the Board of contested evidence of mental illness); BNSS s. 1(2) (Nagaland, tribal areas)
entities.excerpt: « shall proceed with the case » (s. 372) ; « the finding shall state specifically whether he committed the act or not » (s. 373)
entities.note: No pretrial filter: if insanity at the time of the offence appears likely, the magistrate proceeds with the case and commits it for trial to the Court of Session (s. 372), which decides after trial. Central Act; no State amendment to ch. XXVII found (TN, AP, MH read; other States not checked individually). Confidence lowered: Nagaland and tribal areas outside the BNSS unless extended by notification (s. 1(2)), none found.

entities.name: Kerala

facts.outcome: acquittal (BNSS s. 373) with a finding on the act + detention in safe custody (s. 374, MHCA s. 103), in practice in a Government Mental Health Centre (Thiruvananthapuram, Thrissur, Kozhikode) until delivery to the family or rehabilitation
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: BNSS s. 372 applies in Kerala without modification; non-responsibility is decided by the trial court after trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: As at national level (BNSS ss. 367-371). The HC requires a genuine inquiry and, if the alleged illness is contested, referral to the Board (MHCA s. 105), whose opinion forms the basis of the decision (Crl.M.C. 428/2023); a mere assertion by counsel is not enough (Crl.M.C. 1058/2023). Unfit persons are kept in mental health centres, not in prison (2010 Act, s. 39(11)), sometimes for years (48 defendants in GMHCs in 2020).

State of Kerala, OP(Crl.) 487/2019 (13.8.2021); Crl.A. 777/2019 (2021); Crl.M.C. 428/2023 (26.6.2023); Crl.M.C. 1058/2023 (Yasin Sunu)

entities.note: Same procedure as India: BNSS ch. XXVII without Kerala amendment, ordinary trial, acquittal (s. 373), detention (s. 374). Specific features: persons of unsound mind held in mental health centres, not in prison (2010 Act, s. 39(11)); the HC requires prompt expert examination by the investigating officer and referral to the Board (MHCA s. 105), and supervises acquitted persons and defendants stuck in the 3 GMHCs (2021-2026). Colour unchanged.

entities.name: Bangladesh

facts.outcome: Acquittal by reason of insanity (CrPC 1898 s. 470) with an express finding as to whether or not the accused committed the act; if so, detention in safe custody ordered by the court, with a report to the government (s. 471); release decided by the government after certification (s. 474) or delivery to a relative (s. 475, text not re-read)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: if the accused, being fit, appears to have been of unsound mind at the time of the offence, the magistrate or court “shall proceed with the case” (s. 469) and the trial court decides, the burden of proof lying on the defence.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Inquiry by the magistrate with examination by the Civil Surgeon (s. 464) or issue tried first by the Court of Session, as part of the trial (s. 465); if the accused is unfit: finding then outright adjournment, with no examination of the charges and no discharge (unlike India, BNSS ss. 367-368); release on security or safe custody with a report to the government (s. 466); resumption as soon as the accused can make a defence (ss. 467-468, 473: headings only read); custody potentially indefinite, without judgment.

entities.name: Mexico

facts.outcome: security measure (treatment in confinement or at liberty) ordered by the tribunal de enjuiciamiento after the juicio oral; acquittal if the act and participation are not proved
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Ordinary procedure with adjustments (CNPP 414-419) up to the juicio oral before the tribunal de enjuiciamiento; abbreviated procedure excluded (art. 418).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Temporary mental disorder arising during the proceedings: suspension of the process by the juez de control (CNPP art. 331 fr. III) until recovery; permanent inimputabilidad: the special procedure continues with adjustments and the trial of the facts takes place.

entities.legal_bases: CNPP arts. 414-419 (procedimiento para personas inimputables), 331 fr. III (suspensión del proceso), 405 fr. III (absolución: la inimputabilidad como causa de inculpabilidad); CPF arts. 15 fr. VII, 67-69; códigos penales estatales concordantes (p. ej. CP CDMX art. 62).
entities.excerpt: Comprobada la existencia del hecho […] y que el inimputable intervino en su comisión […] el Tribunal de enjuiciamiento resolverá el caso
entities.note: National rule: single CNPP, state criminal codes have no bearing (no MX-XXX entry). The juez de control orders expert examinations at a party's request; once inimputabilidad is established, the ordinary procedure continues with adjustments, with no abbreviated procedure, up to the juicio oral: the tribunal de enjuiciamiento establishes the facts, then orders a measure or acquits.

entities.name: Guatemala

facts.outcome: Judgment (CP 86: measure ordered by the courts “en sentencia condenatoria o absolutoria”) at the end of a special juicio for the exclusive application of measures (CPP 484-487); committal to a psychiatric institution (CP 89).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Special juicio for the exclusive application of measures (CPP 484-487) before the trial court, held in camera with the accused absent and represented in the Ríos Montt case; text of the articles not read.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: CPP article not read. In practice (Ríos Montt, 2015) the accused, having become incapable (dementia), was sent to the special juicio for measures: closed hearing, accused absent and represented, judgment of acquittal or imposing a measure, no prison (a dissenting judge wanted the trial halted). CP 67: suspension of the enforcement of the sentence if mental illness arises after sentencing.

entities.legal_bases: CP (Decreto 17-73) arts. 23 inc. 2º (inimputabilidad), 86 (aplicación jurisdiccional), 87-89 (estado peligroso, medidas de seguridad, internamiento especial); CPP (Decreto 51-92) art. 4 (juicio previo), Libro IV Título IV arts. 484-487 (juicio para la aplicación exclusiva de medidas de seguridad y corrección), arts. 328-331 (sobreseimiento) — text of arts. 484-487 and 328 not read.

entities.note: Special juicio for the exclusive application of measures (CPP 484-487); no one is subjected to a measure without a judgment (CPP 4, CP 86). Ríos Montt case (2015-16): closed hearing (in camera) ordered by the court in light of the expert examinations, accused absent and represented, judgment “sobre la absolución o sobre la aplicación de una medida”. Text not read: if a closed hearing and absence were the statutory rule, it would be yellow.

entities.name: Belize

facts.outcome: Special verdict “guilty but insane” at the ordinary trial (jury, or judge alone for murder), then detention in safe custody “until the State's pleasure is known” (IPA 121-122); the Chief Justice orders that the person be dealt with as insane.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No replacement procedure for non-responsibility: special verdict returned at the ordinary trial (IPA 121); only present unfitness goes through a preliminary examination (IPA 119).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: IPA 119: if the accused appears insane before or at arraignment, the court has the accused's mental state tried (jury, or judge alone for murder, IPA 65A); insane and unfit: no verdict on the indictment (IPA 120), detention “until the State's pleasure is known” (IPA 122), without a trial of the facts; medical review every six months, trial upon recovery (King v White, King v Francis, 2024).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Code (Cap. 101) s. 26 (Insanity), s. 27(2); Indictable Procedure Act (Cap. 96) ss. 65A, 119-122 (s. 121 special verdict: heading only read); Unsoundness of Mind Act (Cap. 122) ss. 3-13, 19-28; Constitution s. 5(1)(a),(h).
entities.excerpt: prevented by reason of idiocy, imbecility or any mental derangement or disease affecting the mind, from knowing the nature or consequences of the act
entities.note: No pretrial filter for non-responsibility: at the ordinary trial (jury, or judge alone for murder, IPA 65A), special verdict “guilty but insane” (IPA 121) then detention “until the State's pleasure is known” (IPA 122). The defence raises the issue and bears the burden of proof (Patten v R). Unfit: detention without a trial of the facts (IPA 119-122). Mental Health Act (rev. 2000) not read.

entities.name: Costa Rica

facts.outcome: Judgment of the trial court at the close of the trial hearing in the special procedure: finds that an unlawful act was committed by a non-imputable person and orders a curative security measure (psychiatric committal) instead of a penalty, without a conviction in the strict sense; acquittal not confirmed by the sources read; follow-up by the enforcement judge (CPP art. 478)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Special procedure for the exclusive application of security measures (CPP arts. 388-390), governed “in principle” by the ordinary procedure: trial hearing before the trial court, defence counsel acting as curator, trial possible in the absence of the accused if their condition so requires, neither abbreviated procedure nor suspension of proceedings on probation.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Supervening mental disorder excluding the capacity to understand the procedural acts: suspension until the incapacity ceases, declared by the court after an expert examination, without preventing the investigation (CPP art. 85; art. 90: suspension of the preliminary hearing and of the trial, according to the first pass); but in the special procedure the accused lacking capacity is represented by defence counsel, who acts as curator (art. 389), which allows them to be tried despite their condition.

entities.legal_bases: CP arts. 42 (inimputabilidad), 97-98 (medidas de seguridad sólo para quien haya cometido un hecho punible), 100-102 (medidas curativas: internación en hospital psiquiátrico); CPP (Ley 7594) arts. 1, 85 (incapacidad sobreviniente), 87 (examen mental), 90, 388 (procedencia), 389 (reglas especiales), 390 (procedimiento ordinario), 478 (ejecución de medidas); Sala Tercera voto 2010-00763 (report of the Instituto de Criminología mandatory); Sala Constitucional voto 3679-93

entities.name: Venezuela

facts.outcome: Judgment of acquittal or imposing a security measure: confinement in a psychiatric institution ordered by the court for an act equivalent to a serious offence, with no release without its authorisation (CP art. 62); in practice, sobreseimiento (art. 318.2) without a measure also observed (Táchira 2009)

facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: A serious mental disorder of the accused leads to suspension of the proceedings, the incapacity being declared by the judge after a forensic psychiatric expert examination (COPP art. 130 in the 2019 text, art. 128 in 2005; the 2021 reform does not affect it); where it arises in the intermediate phase or at trial, proceedings are suspended as regards that accused (scholarship cited by the UCAB thesis).

entities.name: Chubut Province

facts.outcome: security and correctional measure alone: opening of the trial hearing under the ordinary rules, judgment of acquittal or ordering a measure (arts. 361-362); parallel route: sobreseimiento requested by the prosecution for “inculpabilidad” (art. 285 inc. 4, art. 287), with referral to the civil courts
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The fiscal requests the opening of the trial hearing solely for the security measure; the trial follows the ordinary rules (representative of the incapacitated person, accused absent if presence is inappropriate) and ends in acquittal or a measure (arts. 361-362).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Art. 84: a mental disorder excluding the capacity to understand procedural acts suspends the proceedings (declared by the judge after an expert examination); if the incapacity is irreversible, the case is archived as regards the person concerned; the investigation and the proceedings against co-accused continue.

entities.name: Córdoba Province

facts.outcome: Sobreseimiento for inimputabilidad (art. 350 inc. 3) requested by the Fiscal de Instrucción (art. 348) and pronounced by the control judge by sentencia (art. 351), with, according to the decisions summarised in the TSJ's BJ n°41, final committal ordered in the same decision (appeal to the Cámara de Acusación; enforcement by the juez de ejecución); security measures also possible in the judgment of acquittal after trial (art. 411)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Sobreseimiento by judgment of the control judge on the application of the Fiscal de Instrucción, committal in the same decision, without a trial hearing; the Cámara de Acusación reviews (partial annulments for lack of reports from the treating team); the accused's right to a trial not established.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Art. 84 (incapacidad sobreviniente): supervening mental illness suspends the accused's statement and the trial, not the investigation or the proceedings against co-accused; committal to a suitable facility with a quarterly report from the director (or handover to the family/curator if there is no danger, six-monthly expert examination); during the investigation the fiscal asks the Juez de Control for suspension and committal. Text silent on permanent incapacity; TSJ “L., F.” (Sent. 220/2016, according to BJ n°41): referral to the civil courts and closure by analogy with art. 350 inc. 3.

BJ n°41 (TSJ): sobreseimiento for inimputabilidad and final committal by the control judge (Cámara de Acusación, Autos 122/2018, 420/2019), without trial. Art. 411: measures also after trial. Text on the measures not read.

entities.name: Corrientes Province

facts.outcome: Sobreseimiento (dismissal) decreed by the fiscal then pronounced by the judge without a hearing; defence counsel represents the accused presumed non-imputable and the civil courts adopt the protective measures (civil committal, Ley 26.657)

facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Art. 83: if a supervening padecimiento mental seriously restricts capacity, the judge sets supports, reasonable accommodations and special time limits, then at the appropriate time suspends the proceedings as regards the person (acts in their absence and proceedings against co-accused possible); civil courts notified.

On a reasoned decree by the fiscal (art. 288 d), notified to the complainant, the judge issues the sobreseimiento without a hearing (arts. 290-291); civil courts for committal (art. 82). Inimputabilidad is not named in art. 288; the complainant may pursue the case alone (art. 290).

entities.name: La Pampa Province

facts.outcome: Sobreseimiento for inimputabilidad pronounced by the control judge on the prosecution's application, or by the court before any trial hearing; security measure by resolution, provisional committal possible.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The fiscal requests the sobreseimiento (art. 282); the control judge pronounces it, with a hearing only in case of objection (art. 283), inimputabilidad being a ground for sobreseimiento (art. 284 inc. 4).

facts.outcome: the judge declares non-imputability (art. 42); on the application of the fiscal or the parties, the judge orders the security measure and transmits the file to the civil courts (art. 221); if the judge finds the accused imputable, ordinary procedure
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: On a simple application (submission by the fiscal with the incriminating evidence), the judge rules on the accusation and orders the security measure, without opening a trial hearing (art. 221).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Art. 42: incapacity to understand procedural acts, declared by the judge, suspends the proceedings until it ends, without preventing the investigation or the proceedings against co-accused; provisional committal if a serious mental impairment is established by expert examination (art. 116).

entities.note: Art. 42: the judge declares non-imputability. entities.name: Salta Province

facts.outcome: sobreseimiento for non-imputability by reasoned order (arts. 428 e, 429), of the court's own motion or on application from the summons to the charging hearing onwards, even without a statement by the accused (art. 426), with the possibility of imposing a security measure (appeal by the accused, art. 430); provisional committal by the judge of guarantees after a hearing (art. 94); final measures supervised by the enforcement judge (art. 42 b)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The sobreseimiento for non-imputability closes the case by reasoned order, without a juicio, even before any statement by the accused (art. 426), and may include a security measure (art. 430).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Art. 95: mental incapacity arising during the proceedings -> suspension of the case; committal ordered by the judge if the person's condition is dangerous (medical opinion, appealable decision); the suspension prevents the accused's statement or the trial hearing depending on the stage; the case resumes upon recovery.

entities.legal_bases: CP art. 34 inc. 1; CPP Salta (Ley 7690 on argentina.gob.ar; same text labelled Ley 6.345 on leyes-ar.com) arts. 42 b), 94, 95, 96 (mandatory mental examination if a security measure is likely), 426-430 (428 e: inimputabilidad; 430: appeal if a security measure is imposed); accusatorial system up and running in early May 2026 (press); Ley 26.657 arts. 20-21, 23-24 (art. 23 excludes committals based on CP art. 34)
entities.excerpt: Media una causa de justificación, inimputabilidad, inculpabilidad o una excusa absolutoria;
entities.note: Sobreseimiento for non-imputability (art. 428 e) by reasoned order, of the court's own motion or on application, even before the accused's statement (art. 426); the accused may appeal if a security measure is imposed (art. 430); provisional committal by the judge of guarantees after a hearing (art. 94). New system up and running in early May 2026 (press). Hearing and special measures procedure not read.

entities.name: San Juan Province

facts.outcome: no dismissal found: art. 356 does not name non-imputability (only “inculpabilidad”) and art. 360 provides for neither a measure nor committal; provisional committal by the judge for the control of guarantees after a hearing (art. 127); according to local press (2025), the case follows the ordinary route (indictment review hearing, then juicio to establish the act and dangerousness) and ends with compulsory committal as a security measure, supervised by the enforcement judge

entities.name: San Luis Province

facts.outcome: two tracks: (1) sobreseimiento if the accused is inimputable (art. 163 d), requested by the fiscal and decided by the judge, in principle without a hearing, with no right of objection provided for the accused (art. 164), with referral to the civil courts (art. 40) and lifting of coercive measures (art. 165); (2) if only a security measure is appropriate, special procedure (arts. 254-255): application by the fiscal meeting the requirements of an accusation, ordinary rules, juicio (accused absent where presence is inappropriate), judgment of acquittal or imposing a security measure, with referral to the civil courts. Classified on the basis of the second (serious case requiring a measure)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Special security-measure procedure governed by the ordinary rules, with juicio followed by a judgment of acquittal or imposing a measure (arts. 254-255); the sobreseimiento track (art. 163 d) exists alongside it.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Art. 41: after an expert examination, the guarantees judge or the court suspends the proceedings by auto, at the fiscal's request; no statement by the accused and no juicio, but the investigation of the act continues; civil judge and defence counsel informed with a view to protective measures.

entities.note: Two tracks: sobreseimiento (art. 163 d), decided by the judge, in principle without a hearing, with no right of objection provided for the accused (art. 164), with referral to the civil courts (art. 40); or, if only a measure is appropriate, special procedure (arts. 254-255): ordinary rules, juicio, judgment of acquittal or imposing a measure. Classified on the basis of the second (serious case); ordinary track uncertain.

entities.name: Santa Fe Province

facts.outcome: The investigation judge may not order the sobreseimiento if it would entail a medida de seguridad: the judge abstains and refers the case to the Tribunal de Juicio (art. 306), whose judgment of acquittal rules on the security measures requested (art. 336)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No replacement procedure when a measure is sought: the IPP judge refers the case to the Tribunal de Juicio (art. 306); no special procedure for security measures among the special procedures (arts. 346-379 bis).

Provisional committal possible (arts. 107, 230, not re-read).
