facts.outcome: improper acquittal (absolvição imprópria) + security measure (committal or outpatient treatment, CP arts. 96-97); in jury cases, pronounced by the judge at the end of the 1st phase or, after committal to the jury, following the jurors' verdict
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No special procedure: in jury cases, if non-responsibility is the sole defence argument, the judge pronounces improper summary acquittal (a judgment open to appeal) after the public, adversarial evidentiary hearing of the 1st phase; otherwise, jury.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Disorder arising after the offence: trial suspended until recovery, committal possible, witnesses reheard on resumption (art. 152 CPP); disorder already present at the time of the acts: the trial continues with a curator (art. 151), even if the accused remains ill.

entities.legal_bases: CP arts. 26, 96-99; CPP arts. 149-154 (incidente de insanidade mental, possível já no inquérito, art. 149 §1º), 319 VII (internação provisória), 386 VI e par. único III, 397 II (absolvição sumária “salvo inimputabilidade”), 411-416 (1ª fase do júri; art. 415 IV e par. único, Lei 11.689/2008), 483, 492 II c; Lei 10.216/2001; Res. CNJ 487/2023 (art. 18); STJ, 39.920/RJ, Rel. Min. Jorge Mussi, 6/2/2014 (Informativo 535)
entities.excerpt: Não se aplica o disposto no inciso IV [...] ao caso de inimputabilidade [...], salvo quando esta for a única tese defensiva.
entities.note: Federal law: national entry. Expert examination ordered by the judge (CPP art. 149); the trial continues with a curator (art. 151). Jury (homicide): after the public, adversarial hearing of the 1st phase, improper summary acquittal + measure if non-responsibility is the sole argument; any other concrete argument sends the case to the jury (STJ, Inf. 535). Non-jury cases: full trial (art. 397 II).

independent_check.reasoning: Read CPP 149 (ex officio expert examination, from the inquérito stage), 151 (trial continued with a curator) and 415 par. único: improper summary acquittal only if inimputability is the sole argument (STJ Inf. 535); any other argument sends the case to the jury: full trial at the accused's request. Purple tenable (planalto blocked, texts read on secondary sites).

entities.merge_decision: Homicide (jury): after the 1st phase (public, adversarial hearing before the judge), improper summary acquittal with a measure is possible only if non-responsibility is the sole defence argument (CPP art. 415, sole para.); otherwise committal to the jury: the accused can obtain the full trial, hence purple. The encoding of the facts (“none”) explains the discrepancy with the inferred colour.

entities.name: Paraguay

facts.outcome: Special procedure for the application of measures (CPP arts. 428-431): accusation, preparatory and intermediate stages, then juicio oral before the trial court; the judgment pronounces acquittal or an improvement measure (committal to a psychiatric hospital, CP art. 73); the ordinary track, concluding that there is no reproachability (CP art. 23) and ordering committal, is also used
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Special procedure (arts. 428-431) conducted through to a juicio oral, but closed hearing and absence of the accused (represented by their legal representative) possible if the accused's condition so requires (art. 429, according to academic works).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: A mental disorder excluding the capacity to understand or to will procedural acts, declared by the judge after a psychiatric expert examination, suspends the proceedings against the accused until the incapacity ceases, without prejudice to the special measures procedure (art. 78); the investigation and the proceedings against co-accused continue; acts of the incapacitated person are invalid; committal for observation of up to 6 weeks (art. 80).

entities.legal_bases: CP (Ley 1160/97) arts. 23 (trastorno mental), 72, 73 (internación en un hospital psiquiátrico); CPP (Ley 1286/98) arts. 78 (incapacidad), 79 (examen mental), 80 (internación para observación) read; arts. 428 (procedencia), 429 (reglas especiales), 430 (rechazo), 431 (transformación) known only through academic works; Instructivo del Ministerio Público N° 7/2013 (not read)
entities.excerpt: provocará la suspensión condicional del procedimiento con relación a él, hasta que desaparezca esa incapacidad; sin perjuicio de la aplicación del procedimiento especial
entities.note: The prosecution must request the special procedure (428; instructivo MP 7/2013): preparatory and intermediate stages and juicio oral before the trial court; judgment of acquittal or imposing a measure (CP 73). Closed hearing and absence of the accused only if the accused's condition so requires (429, cited by two studies; code not read). The ordinary track is also used (2020 case). Purple, low confidence.

history.note: White: text of CPP arts. 428-431 (special measures procedure, referred to in art. 78) not consulted, search quotas exhausted. Mandatory mental expert examination if the act suggests a disorder (art. 79); observation ≤ 6 weeks (art. 80). To be verified (art. 429): publicity and presence of the accused — real trial → purple; closed hearing or no rule → yellow.

entities.name: Uruguay

facts.outcome: final judgment declaring the accused an “autor inimputable” + curative measures (committal) instead of the penalty
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the proceedings follow the ordinary track up to final judgment (CPP art. 67.3).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: If the accused becomes inimputable during the proceedings, provisional committal possible after an expert examination (art. 67.2) and the proceedings continue on the ordinary track up to judgment (art. 67.3); this article provides for no suspension; right not to be tried in absentia (arts. 64 j, 69).

entities.legal_bases: CP arts. 30 (locura) to 33 and 35 (causas de inimputabilidad); CPP (Ley 19.293) arts. 9 (proceso público y contradictorio), 64 j) (no ser juzgado en ausencia), 67 (inimputabilidad), 69 (prohibición del proceso en rebeldía)
entities.excerpt: El proceso continuará el trámite común hasta la sentencia definitiva y de resultar el encausado condenado, se le declarará autor inimputable del delito cometido
entities.note: No pretrial gate: at any stage, on a party's allegation or if it is manifest, provisional committal possible after an expert examination (art. 67.1 CPP). The proceedings follow the ordinary track (accusatorial, oral, public) up to judgment; if the accused is “convicted”, they are declared an inimputable perpetrator and subjected to curative measures instead of the penalty (art. 67.3).

entities.name: Haiti

facts.outcome: Dismissal order (ordonnance de non-lieu) by the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) and release of the charged person (insanity at the time of the act excludes felony and misdemeanour, art. 48 CP); no security measure or judicial confinement provided for in the texts read; failing a dismissal, committal to the criminal court (tribunal criminel) with a jury.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The investigating judge (juge d'instruction) declares that there are no grounds to prosecute when the act constitutes neither felony nor misdemeanour (art. 115 CIC, with art. 48 CP), with no review in chambers (chambre du conseil) or by an indictment chamber (chambre d'accusation) in the articles read.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No provision on unfitness to stand trial in the part of the 1835 CIC read (neither suspension nor fitness procedure); practice undocumented.

entities.legal_bases: CP (1835) art. 48; CIC (1835) arts. 115 (dismissal [non-lieu]), 119-120 (committal to the criminal court [tribunal criminel], custody order [prise de corps]), 121-122 (effect of the dismissal), 180-188 (criminal court, jury). New Code pénal and Code de procédure pénale not in force: entry into force announced for January 2027 (UNDP, 16 Jul. 2026).
entities.excerpt: Il n'y a ni crimes ni délit, lorsque le prévenu était en état de démence au temps de l'action
entities.note: 1835 codes in force on 28 Oct. 2026. Insanity at the time of the act = neither felony nor misdemeanour (art. 48 CP, read): the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) decides that there are no grounds to prosecute (art. 115 CIC, read); otherwise committal to the criminal court (tribunal criminel, art. 119). No confinement provided for in the texts read (first 29 of the CIC's 82 pages); practice undocumented.

history.note: 1835 codes in force. If insanity at the time of the act is established (“ni crime ni délit” (neither felony nor misdemeanour), art. 48 CP), the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) declares that there are no grounds to prosecute and releases the charged person (art. 115 CIC); otherwise committal to the criminal court (tribunal criminel) with a jury (art. 119). No judicial confinement provided for. New codes (2020/2025) postponed on 24 Dec. 2025; entry into force announced for January 2027.

entities.name: Dominican Republic

facts.outcome: Judgment of the trial court in the special procedure for inimputable persons: acquittal, or a security measure (psychiatric committal) whose duration is capped by the penalty incurred; enforcement, supervision and review fall to the sentence-enforcement judge (art. 74 Ley 97-25, according to the Pellerano & Herrera summary).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Procedure for inimputable persons (former CPP arts. 374-376): application by the MP or the private prosecutor in the form of an accusation, followed by trial by the court under the ordinary rules, in camera, the accused being represented by their legal representative.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: A temporary mental disorder excluding the capacity to understand suspends the prosecution until it ceases, and acts of the incapacitated person are void (art. 99 CPP, Ley 97-25, text read); the accused may also be tried in their absence, represented, in the procedure for inimputable persons (health or order, former art. 375.4).

entities.legal_bases: CPP: Ley 97-25 (Ley orgánica establishing the CPP, promulgated on 7 Dec. 2025, in force from 9-10 Dec. 2025; replaces Ley 10-15 and amends Ley 76-02): arts. 3, 74, 99 read; procedure for inimputable persons: former arts. 374-376 (Título V) read, current numbering (1st pass: arts. 381-385) not verified. CP: Ley 74-25, applied since 3 Aug. 2026 (replaces art. 64 of 1884); official text not read, wording quoted by the press (“perturbación psíquica”).
entities.excerpt: El juicio se realiza a puertas cerradas, sin la presencia del imputado, cuando es imposible a causa de su estado de salud […]
entities.note: Measure only after juicio (art. 3 CPP). Special track requested by the MP, the private prosecutor or the accused (former art. 374), tried by the court under the ordinary rules; closed hearing, accused represented, absent on grounds of health or order (former art. 375.4). Ley 97-25 strengthens the curator's role and the content of the measure; its articles not read. Closed hearing = borderline yellow.

history.note: No measure without a trial (art. 3 CPP). The MP or the private prosecutor (the accused may request it) applies for the procedure for inimputable persons in the form of an accusation (art. 381); after the preliminary hearing, the trial court rules under the ordinary rules: acquittal, or a measure if the act and participation are proven (art. 383). Caveats: closed hearing (art. 382.4); dismissal (art. 309.4).

entities.name: Jamaica

facts.outcome: At trial, the judge, magistrate or jury finding that the accused committed the act but was suffering from a mental disorder excluding responsibility returns a special verdict to the effect that the defendant “was guilty of the act or omission charged against him” but was suffering from a mental disorder, on the opinion of at least two doctors; the court then orders the measure (arrangements not read).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the mental disorder at the time of the acts is established in the ordinary trial (CJAA s. 25E), after a finding that the accused committed the act.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Fitness (CJAA s. 25): issue raised by the court, the accused or the prosecution; outside jury trials, the court decides; two doctors required. If unfit: no trial of the facts; the court may order detention, psychiatric hospital, supervision or guardianship (s. 25C(2)); trial possible after recovery (s. 25C(3)). In practice, “administrative” decision by the judge on the medical file and detentions of several decades without trial, recharacterised in 2023-2024 by the Supreme Court as detentions at the Court's pleasure.

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Justice (Administration) Act (CJAA) ss. 25 (fitness), 25C (measures if unfit), 25E(1)-(2) (special verdict; two doctors), ss. 25A-25E inserted by the 2006 Act; Mental Health Act s. 2 (mental disorder) and s. 9 (court-ordered admission, according to R v Williams [2020] JMSC Crim 8)
entities.excerpt: shall return a special verdict to the effect that the defendant was guilty of the act or omission charged against him
entities.note: Ordinary trial: judge, magistrate or jury returns a special verdict (act committed, mental disorder) on the opinion of two doctors (CJAA s. 25E, read via CA 2012). Unfitness: decision by the judge, detention without trial of the facts, sometimes for decades. Measures after special verdict, burden of proof and official text (portal blocked to automated access) not read; no recent reform identified.

entities.name: Bahamas

facts.outcome: At trial on indictment, the jury or the court may find the accused insane at the time of the acts (Penal Code s. 92): special verdict “guilty but insane” (CPC s. 191, text not read); the court then orders the accused's transfer to hospital, where they are held until discharged by order of the Governor-General (s. 192(1), cited by the Court of Appeal in 2021).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: at the preliminary inquiry, the court proceeds and commits the accused for trial even if insanity at the time of the acts is alleged (CPC s. 101).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: If, at the preliminary inquiry or at trial, the court suspects that the accused is insane and incapable of making a defence, it inquires (CPC s. 99) and, if it finds the accused unfit, suspends the proceedings (s. 100): release on bail or report to the Governor-General, who may order detention in hospital; resumption if the accused becomes fit again (s. 102); no trial of the facts. At arraignment: s. 155 (not read).

entities.legal_bases: Penal Code s. 92 (insanity; s. 91 in the 2011 edition cited by the CPC); Criminal Procedure Code Act (Ch. 91) ss. 99-103 (incapacity of the accused), 101 (no gate at the preliminary inquiry), 155 (arraignment), 191 (special verdict “guilty but insane”), 192(1) (the court orders transfer to hospital, custody until discharge by the Governor-General)
entities.excerpt: insane within the meaning of section 91 of the Penal Code, the court shall proceed with the case
entities.note: No pretrial gate: at the preliminary inquiry the court proceeds despite an allegation of insanity (CPC s. 101); Penal Code s. 92: “opinion of the jury or of the court”. Verdict “guilty but insane” (s. 191 not read), custody until discharge by the G.-G. (s. 192(1)). Unfit: proceedings suspended, detention without trial of the facts (ss. 99-102). Mental Health Bill 2022 not verified.

entities.name: Trinidad and Tobago

facts.outcome: At trial, if the jury finds that the accused committed the act but was insane, special verdict “guilty of the act charged against him, but was insane” (CPA ch. 12:02 s. 66); the court orders detention in safe custody at the President's pleasure (s. 67), the President then deciding on care as a mentally ill person (s. 68).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the jury decides insanity in the ordinary trial, after finding that the accused did the act (s. 66).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: On arraignment, the court may have a jury empanelled to determine whether the accused is “insane and unfit to take his trial” (s. 64); during trial, the jury returns an “insane” verdict without ruling on the charge (s. 65); detention at the President's pleasure (ss. 67-68), without trial of the facts; trial remains possible if the accused recovers their sanity (s. 65 para. 2).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Procedure Act, ch. 12:02 (L.R.O. 1/2009) ss. 64 (insanity on arraignment), 65 (during trial), 66 (special verdict), 67 (detention), 68 (report to the President); Miscellaneous Provisions (Trial by Judge Alone) Act 2017 (Act No. 10, in force by proclamation): “Judge” in place of the jury in trials without a jury; Bill No. 1 of 2023 (judge alone, does not amend ss. 64-68)
entities.excerpt: the jury shall return a special verdict to the effect that the accused person was guilty of the act charged against him, but was insane
entities.note: Ordinary trial: the jury returns the special verdict “guilty of the act charged against him, but was insane” (s. 66), followed by detention at the President's pleasure (ss. 67-68). Unfitness: jury on mental state (ss. 64-65), without trial of the facts. entities.name: Barbados

facts.outcome: At trial, if the jury considers that the accused committed the act but was insane, special verdict “not guilty of the act charged against him, by reason of insanity” (CPA Cap. 127 s. 9A); the High Court then orders detention in a psychiatric hospital at Her Majesty's pleasure, with discharge by the Governor-General (MHA Cap. 45 s. 13, L.R.O. 1998 edition read; adaptation to the 2021 republic not verified).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the jury decides insanity in the ordinary trial, after finding that the accused committed the act (CPA s. 9A).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: The CPA as read contains no provision on unfitness. Mental Health Act s. 13(1)(a) provides, for an accused tried before the High Court and declared unfit to plead, for detention in a psychiatric hospital at Her Majesty's pleasure, without trial of the facts; 8-week admission possible for observation (s. 7(1)). entities.name: Saint Lucia

facts.outcome: Special jury verdict of guilty of the act but mentally ill at trial (Criminal Code s. 1019; Mental Hospitals Act s. 32: insane); safe custody ordered by the Court, the judge reporting to the Chief Justice, who has the person treated as insane (s. 1020); pleasure formula (heading of s. 1020; MHA s. 32(2): Her Majesty's pleasure, orders of the Governor General).

entities.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

facts.outcome: Special finding by the trial court (the jury in the High Court) that the accused committed the act but is not guilty by reason of insanity (CPC s. 120); committal to a psychiatric hospital as a criminal person of unsound mind until the Governor General's pleasure is known.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: at the preliminary inquiry, the magistrate proceeds and commits for trial even if insanity at the time of the act is raised (CPC s. 118); it is decided at trial (s. 120).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: CPC s. 115: the court inquires into incapacity of its own motion, the jury deciding in the High Court (s. 115(3)); if the accused cannot defend himself, the proceedings are suspended: observation (max. 1 month), bail or committal to a psychiatric hospital with a report to the Governor General; resumption on medical certificate (ss. 116-117), with no adjudication of the facts in the meantime.

facts.outcome: acquittal “on the ground of mental disease or defect” + committal ordered by the court (§4.08), lifted if there is no danger
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Affirmative defence decided at trial (jury or judge); no acquittal on a mere report (§4.07 “reserved”).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: §4.04: no person may be tried, convicted or punished while unable to understand the proceedings or assist in his defence; fitness is decided by the court (§4.06), which may order a competency examination of its own motion (r. 16(f)(2)(J)); what follows (suspension, placement) not verified.

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Code 2011 §§4.01-4.08; Rules of Criminal Procedure 2005 (rev. 2021) r. 16(e)(1)(E), 16(f)(2)(J), 23; Criminal Procedure Act §156; Public Health and Sanitation Act s. 117
entities.excerpt: Evidence of mental disease or defect excluding responsibility is not admissible unless the defendant … files a written notice
entities.note: Modelled on the Model Penal Code: affirmative defence inadmissible without written notice from the accused (§4.03(2), r. 16(e)(1)(E)); the expert examination requested by the prosecution is tied to that notice (r. 16(f)(2)(J)). Jury or judge acquits, then the judge may order committal (§4.08). Caveat: the former §156 CPA allows the judge to find insanity on medical evidence.

entities.name: Federated States of Micronesia

facts.outcome: judgment of acquittal on the ground of the disorder + committal or conditional release ordered by the court (§302(4))
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The defence is decided at trial; the court enters judgment in favour of the accused and orders the measure (§302(4)).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: §304: no trial while the incapacity lasts; proceedings suspended and placement to restore fitness (or conditional release); resumption upon fitness, or charges dropped if resumption would be unjust, with civil commitment or release.

entities.legal_bases: 11 F.S.M.C. §§107, 302-305; FSM Rules of Criminal Procedure (without Rule 12.2); States: Kosrae State Code §13.104(2), Chuuk State Code (draft) T. 12 §§2002-2004, Yap State Code T. 11 §109
entities.excerpt: When the defendant is acquitted on the grounds of physical or mental disease, disorder, or defect excluding responsibility, the verdict … shall so state
entities.note: National rule: affirmative defence (Runmar v. FSM), proven at trial by the party raising it; the court acquits, retains jurisdiction and orders committal or release (§302(4)). No Rule 12.2 on notice. Homicide falls mainly within State jurisdiction: Kosrae, Chuuk (draft) and Yap follow the same pattern; Pohnpei not verified; no separate State entry.

entities.name: Palau

facts.outcome: acquittal “on the ground of physical or mental disease, disorder, or defect excluding responsibility” pronounced at trial (17 PNC § 503(c)); consequential measures (§§ 510-519) not read
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Even if the expert examination concludes that there is substantial impairment, the defence is submitted to the trier of fact at trial (§ 509; trial without jury under the 2004 rules); no pretrial acquittal.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: §§ 504-508: no trial while unfitness lasts; suspension, custody of the Minister of Health or conditional release; resumption upon fitness; charges may be dropped, with civil commitment (34 PNC ch. 5) if unfitness is lasting.

entities.excerpt: the court shall submit the defense of physical or mental disease, disorder, or defect to the trier of fact
entities.note: White → green: texts read. Ch. 5 modelled on Hawaii: affirmative defence proven by the accused (§ 503(a)); the judge orders an expert examination on notice from the defence or of the judge's own motion if the disorder “will or has become an issue” (§ 505) and submits the defence to the trier of fact (§ 509). Caveat: R. 12.2 (2004) requires notice from the accused, but the later statute allows an examination of the court's own motion. §§ 510-519 not read.

The revised Penal Code, probably inspired by the Model Penal Code, may leave the defence to the accused's initiative (cf. Marshall Islands): to be verified.

entities.name: Cook Islands

facts.outcome: verdict “not guilty on account of insanity” at trial (Crimes Act s. 26), then orders under the New Zealand CP(MIP)A 2003 applied via s. 3 of the CPA; interplay with the Cook Islands Act 1915 (persons “of unsound mind”) not verified
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No mandatory pretrial route; the imported CP(MIP)A 2003 (s. 20) allows a finding of insanity before trial only if the defence raises it and the prosecution accepts it (local use not verified).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: New Zealand CP(MIP)A 2003 applied via s. 3 CPA (R v S.G.C. [2025] CKHC 13): the judge rules before trial on expert reports (balance of probabilities), then a separate hearing on involvement in the acts (s. 10) and orders (ss. 13, 23); no trial on the merits while unfit.

entities.legal_bases: Crimes Act 1969 s. 26(1)-(2); Criminal Procedure Act 1980-81 s. 3; Judicature Act 1980-81 s. 8; Criminal Procedure (Mentally Impaired Persons) Act 2003 (NZ) ss. 8A, 10, 13, 20, 23; Cook Islands Act 1915 (persons of unsound mind, Part XXI)
entities.excerpt: No person shall be convicted of an offence by reason of an act done or omitted by him when labouring under natural imbecility
entities.note: Insanity (Crimes Act s. 26, presumption of sanity) decided at trial. The CPA 1980-81 is silent; via its s. 3, the High Court applies the New Zealand CP(MIP)A 2003 (verified for unfitness: R v S.G.C. [2025] CKHC 13), which also allows a finding of insanity before trial by agreement of the parties. No local decision on insanity found; Part XXI of the Cook Islands Act 1915 not read.

history.note: The Crimes Act excludes the conviction of an insane person (s. 26), a question decided at trial. The Criminal Procedure Act 1980-81 governs neither the verdict nor unfitness; its s. 3 makes the New Zealand procedural law in force applicable (CP(MIP)A 2003, which also allows a finding of insanity before trial by agreement of the parties): application not verified, low confidence.

entities.name: Niue

facts.outcome: acquittal “on ground of insanity” at trial, then detention / medical custody ordered by the High Court (Niue Act 1966 ss. 617-619, according to the headings; operative text not read)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No visible pretrial route: acquittal on the ground of insanity (s. 617) presupposes a trial before the High Court (judge, assessors where applicable, ss. 259-273); text not read.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: s. 616 “Insane persons not to be tried for offences”: an accused who is insane at the time of trial is not tried; medical custody (ss. 602, 619) and possible transfer to New Zealand (ss. 608-611); details not read.

entities.legal_bases: Niue Act 1966 ss. 259-273 (trial, assessors); Part 26 Persons of Unsound Mind ss. 600-620, in particular ss. 616, 617, 618, 619, 620
entities.excerpt: Detention of accused persons acquitted on ground of insanity
entities.note: Colour changed (white → green) according to the official headings of the Niue Act 1966, Part 26: s. 620 insanity defence in prosecutions, s. 617 detention of accused persons acquitted on the ground of insanity, s. 616 insane persons not tried (unfitness). Operative text not read (PacLII and NZ pages truncated, PDF unreadable); the excerpt is the heading of s. 617: low confidence.

history.note: Insufficient data: the Niue Act 1966 (criminal and procedural provisions) could not be consulted (PacLII and New Zealand databases inaccessible, research budget exhausted). An old New Zealand model (acquittal on the ground of insanity at trial, then detention) is probable but unverified.

entities.name: Senegal

facts.outcome: acquittal for lack of criminal responsibility (art. 50 CP) by the criminal chamber after a public trial, with committal to the Thiaroye psychiatric hospital ordered by the chamber itself (Mbour 2026) or judicial committal (Law No. 75-80); dismissal (non-lieu) by the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) conceivable but undocumented
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the criminal chamber, seised (art. 218) by order of the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) or by decision of the indictment chamber (chambre d'accusation), tries the case at a public hearing (art. 253) and acquits for lack of criminal responsibility (art. 295 para. 2).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No specific provision read; in practice, adjournment of the hearing for an expert examination (Tambacounda 2025) or release on health grounds (cf. art. 140 CPP), the case possibly remaining untried (Thiès 2021: insane accused released after 6 years); committal possible by the president of the court in chambers (chambre du conseil; Law 75-80).

entities.legal_bases: CP (Law No. 65-60 of 21 July 1965) art. 50; CPP (Law No. 65-61 of 21 July 1965, as amended notably by Law No. 2016-30 of 2016) arts. 218 (referral to the criminal chamber), 253 (public hearings), 293-295 (acquittal; art. 295 para. 2: non-responsibility within the meaning of art. 50 CP), 299-300 (civil claims), 319 (appeal), 140 (release on health grounds); Law No. 75-80 of 9 July 1975, arts. 1, 8-13 (judicial committal)
entities.excerpt: En cas d'acquittement de l'accusé en raison de son irresponsabilité au sens de l'article 50 du Code pénal, la chambre criminelle peut cependant le condamner
entities.note: Yellow → green: the criminal chamber, seised (CPP art. 218) by the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) or the indictment chamber (chambre d'accusation), tries the case at a public hearing and acquits for lack of criminal responsibility (art. 50 CP; art. 295 para. 2); Mbour 2026: acquittal and committal at Thiaroye. Dismissal (non-lieu) for insanity plausible but neither read nor observed: 4 cases (2013-2026) committed for trial. No CPP reform in 2023-2026.

history.note: The investigating judge (juge d'instruction), who must be seised for felonies, orders the expert examination; if insanity is established, dismissal (non-lieu) (art. 50 CP). Committal is judicial (Law 75-80: prefect seised by the judicial authorities, president of the court in chambers [chambre du conseil] within 15 days). Nuance: if the case is committed for trial, the criminal chamber may acquit on the ground of insanity and order committal (Mbour, 2026).

entities.name: Côte d'Ivoire

facts.outcome: dismissal (non-lieu) by the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) / investigating chamber (chambre d'instruction) + judicial committal to a health facility ordered by the judge on the prosecution's submissions (art. 79 CP)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Dismissal (non-lieu) by the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) on a ground under art. 102 CP, followed where applicable by committal to a health facility, ordered by that same judge.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No title of the 2018 CPP on mental disorder; in practice stay or adjournment and treatment; committal under art. 79 CP presupposes a dismissal (non-lieu) or an acquittal, whether relaxe or acquittement (unverified).

entities.legal_bases: CP (Law No. 2019-574 of 26 June 2019) arts. 40, 79, 94, 102; CPP (Law No. 2018-975 of 27 December 2018) arts. 96 et seq. (investigating judge [juge d'instruction]), 193-204 (expert examination), 209-218 (closing orders), 112 and 121 (dismissal [non-lieu]), 226-261 (investigating chamber [chambre d'instruction])
entities.excerpt: En cas de non-lieu, d'acquittement ou de relaxe pour l'une des causes prévues par l'article 102, le juge ordonne l'internement dans une maison de santé
entities.note: The investigating judge (juge d'instruction) orders the expert examination; if art. 102 CP applies (will abolished), the judge issues a dismissal (non-lieu), then, on the prosecution's submissions and in light of a dangerousness assessment, orders committal to a health facility (art. 79 CP), lifted by the sentence-enforcement judge (JAP). The 2018 CPP contains no title on non-responsibility for mental disorder (tables of contents consulted): no 2008-type reform.

facts.outcome: Unverified: neither the CP nor the CPP of 2016 could be read; hypothesis drawn from the French model (dismissal [non-lieu] by the investigating judge [juge d'instruction], or even a 2008-type non-responsibility procedure, then treatment), with no textual basis found; non-responsibility itself is here merely a default parameter.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Unknown: no article of the 2016 CPP read (copies from the Supreme Court, ecoi.net and the ISFAD library unreadable); default values with no probative value.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Unverified (CPP not read).

entities.legal_bases: CP (Law No. L/2016/059/AN of 26 October 2016) and CPP (Law No. L/2016/060/AN of 26 October 2016): articles on non-responsibility, expert examination, dismissal (non-lieu) and committal not read (no readable copy)

Classification based on the common French model: judicial investigation mandatory for felonies, expert examination ordered by the investigating judge (juge d'instruction), dismissal (non-lieu), or a non-responsibility decision if the 2016 CPP adopted the French 2008 reform (unverified). entities.name: Togo

facts.outcome: dismissal (non-lieu; or discontinuance [classement sans suite], acquittal [acquittement, relaxe]) + committal to a health facility ordered by the judge on the prosecution's application, after a medical expert examination (art. 123 CP)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Dismissal (non-lieu) or discontinuance (classement sans suite) for impairment of mental faculties, then committal to a health facility ordered by “le Juge” (the judge) on the prosecution's application (art. 123 CP).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Unverified (1983 CPP not read): the CP deals only with non-responsibility at the time of the act; no known procedure for a trial of the facts.

entities.legal_bases: CP (Law No. 2015-010 of 24 November 2015, amended by Laws No. 2016-027 [not read] and No. 2022-018) art. 25 (impairment of mental faculties, ground of non-responsibility), art. 26 para. 1 (disorder abolishing discernment), art. 123 (committal to a health facility); CPP (Law No. 83-1 of 2 March 1983) not read
entities.excerpt: […] de non-lieu, d'acquittement ou de relaxe pour l'une des causes prévues par l'article 25 […], le Juge ordonne l'internement dans une maison de santé
entities.note: CP 2015 read (Official Gazette of 24 Nov. 2015, OCR): art. 26 para. 1 (abolished discernment = not responsible); art. 123: after discontinuance (classement sans suite), dismissal (non-lieu) or acquittal (acquittement or relaxe) on a ground under art. 25, “le Juge” (the judge) orders committal on the prosecution's application after an expert examination; release decided by the prosecution. Yellow confirmed; 1983 CPP (which governs the dismissal) not read.

history.note: Togolese CP 2015 and CPP not consulted (web research exhausted). Classification deduced from the French model: the investigating judge (juge d'instruction), who must be seised for felonies, orders the expert examination and issues a dismissal (non-lieu) if discernment was abolished, under review by the indictment chamber (chambre d'accusation); committal outside any trial. A recent CPP reform could not be verified.

entities.name: Benin

facts.outcome: Unverified: article of the 2018 CP on mental disorder not read; in the CPP, mandatory psychiatric examination during the judicial investigation in felony cases (art. 87) and dismissal (non-lieu) by the investigating chamber (chambre de l'instruction) if the facts constitute “ni crime, ni délit, ni contravention” (neither felony, nor misdemeanour, nor petty offence) or for lack of sufficient evidence (new art. 231), with no mention of non-responsibility or committal.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Unknown: Law 2018-14 (new arts. 196, 231, 233, 360) addresses neither non-responsibility nor committal; closing orders and special procedures of the 2012 CPP not read (default values with no probative value).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Unverified: no provision found in arts. 1-136 of the CPP or in Law 2018-14.

entities.legal_bases: CPP (Law No. 2012-15 of 18 March 2013) art. 87 (mandatory psychiatric examination in felony cases); Law No. 2018-14 amending the CPP, new arts. 196 and 233 (indictment by the investigating judge [juge d'instruction] or the investigating chamber [chambre de l'instruction]), 201, new art. 231 (dismissal [non-lieu]: neither felony, nor misdemeanour, nor petty offence, or insufficient evidence), new art. 360 (accused found not guilty); CP (Law No. 2018-16 of 28 December 2018): article on mental disorder not read; Law No. 2020-23 not read
entities.excerpt: En matière criminelle, il doit prescrire un examen médical ou médico-psychologique et psychiatrique
entities.note: White (yellow → white): no text read says what becomes of an insane charged person. Law 2018-14 read: dismissal (non-lieu) by the investigating chamber (chambre de l'instruction) if neither felony nor misdemeanour nor petty offence, or for lack of evidence (art. 231), without mentioning non-responsibility. 2018 CP and remainder of the 2012 CPP unreadable (binary PDF; text cut off at art. 136). Hypothesis: yellow (mandatory examination, art. 87).

history.note: In felony cases, the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) must order a psychiatric examination (art. 87 CPP). If discernment was abolished, the judge issues a dismissal (non-lieu) (appeal to the investigating chamber [chambre de l'instruction]); otherwise committal for trial before the court sitting in felony matters. Unverified: the 2018 CP article, the existence of a 2008-type procedure (the colour would remain yellow) and the treatment regime.

Read: 2012 CPP up to art. 136 (mandatory psychiatric examination in felony cases, art. 87) and Law 2018-14 (felonies: investigating judge [juge d'instruction], then investigating chamber [chambre de l'instruction], which indicts or rules that there are no grounds to proceed). Not read: the 2018 CP article on mental disorder, the closing orders, the treatment regime. Yellow inferred from the French model, unverified.

entities.name: Cameroon

facts.outcome: acquittal on the ground of insanity pronounced by the court seised + committal to a special health facility if the liberty of the person concerned is found dangerous to public order (felony or misdemeanour punishable by at least two years); only that court can end it, after medical opinion (CP art. 43)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No replacement procedure read: the CP provides for committal only after an acquittal on the ground of insanity by the court seised (art. 43) and mentions neither dismissal (non-lieu) nor investigating courts; grounds for dismissal in the CPP not read.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Art. 68 para. 3 b CPP (read in the first pass) lists insanity arising after the offence among the factual obstacles suspending the limitation period, which implies that prosecution awaits recovery; detailed regime (examination, treatment, resumption) not read.

entities.legal_bases: CP (Law No. 2016/007 of 12 July 2016) arts. 78 (insanity: no responsibility if the will is abolished), 79, 43 (acquittal on the ground of insanity: committal ordered by the court seised, which alone can end it), 44, 20 and 52 (committal, security measure of immediate application); CPP (Law No. 2005/007 of 27 July 2005) art. 68 para. 3 b; orders closing the judicial investigation (art. 257 et seq.) not read
entities.excerpt: En cas d'acquittement pour démence de l'auteur d'un crime ou d'un délit […] celle-ci ordonne son internement dans une maison spéciale de santé.
entities.note: Green maintained, low confidence. CP art. 43 read verbatim: committal follows an “acquittement pour démence” (acquittal on the ground of insanity) pronounced by the court seised, which alone can end it; the CP makes no provision for dismissal (non-lieu) or investigating courts. Not read: grounds for dismissal in the CPP (copies cut off around art. 172 or unreadable), expert examination. If in practice the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) closes the case for insanity: yellow.

history.note: The 2005 CPP is unified and also applies to the North-West and South-West, of common-law tradition: a single national entry. Judicial investigation mandatory for felonies; the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) may issue a dismissal (non-lieu) for insanity (art. 78 CP). Texts not consulted (research exhausted); any special CPP rules on insanity remain to be verified.

Colour changed (yellow → green, low confidence): in the 2016 CP (French text, arts. 43 and 78), only “la juridiction” (the court) orders committal after an acquittal on the ground of insanity and only it can end it; no dismissal (non-lieu) with committal read. 2005 CPP: closing of the judicial investigation (non-lieu) unreadable after art. 172. If the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) can close the case for non-responsibility: yellow.

entities.name: Gabon

facts.outcome: dismissal (non-lieu) by the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) or the indictment chamber (chambre d'accusation), or decision of the trial court + placement in a specialised institution ordered by “la juridiction d'instruction ou de jugement” (the investigating or trial court) (art. 50 CP)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Dismissal (non-lieu) by the investigating judge (juge d'instruction, art. 163 CPP) or by the indictment chamber (chambre d'accusation) seised of felonies (art. 166), the investigating court being able to order placement (art. 50 CP).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Unverified: no provision read (CPP read only up to art. 177) on insanity arising after the events; no known procedure for a trial of the facts.

entities.legal_bases: CP (Law No. 042/2018 of 5 July 2019, amended by Law No. 006/2020) art. 50 (read via the press, not in the code); CPP (Law No. 043/2018 of 5 July 2019) arts. 95, 147 para. 3, 151, 163, 166 (read); arts. 178 et seq. not read; CPP revision under consultation in April 2026, not adopted to our knowledge
entities.excerpt: n'est pas pénalement responsable la personne qui était atteinte, au moment des faits, d'un trouble psychique ou neuropsychique ayant aboli son discernement […]
entities.note: Art. 50 CP (read via the press): not responsible if discernment abolished; “la juridiction d'instruction ou de jugement” (the investigating or trial court) may order placement (text quoted in 2015), release by the local court (2021). 2019 CPP read up to art. 177: dismissal (non-lieu) by the investigating judge (juge d'instruction, art. 163), felonies referred to the indictment chamber (chambre d'accusation, art. 166), art. 147 para. 3 refers to non-responsibility. Remainder not read.

entities.name: Madagascar

facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The investigating judge (juge d'instruction) declares that there are no grounds to prosecute if the facts constitute neither felony nor misdemeanour (CPP art. 286); the indictment chamber (chambre d'accusation), seised for felonies, rules likewise in chambers (chambre du conseil; arts. 303, 307).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No specific provision found in the CPP as read.

entities.legal_bases: Penal Code art. 64 (insanity: “ni crime ni délit”, neither felony nor misdemeanour); CPP (Ordinance No. 62-052 of 20 September 1962, as amended) arts. 280-284 (expert examination), 285-286 (closing of the judicial investigation, dismissal [non-lieu]), 290-291 (felonies), 303 and 307 (indictment chamber [chambre d'accusation], in chambers [chambre du conseil], dismissal); Law No. 2016-017 (no effect on these articles).

entities.note: Combined reading: the CP (art. 64) states that there is “ni crime ni délit” (neither felony nor misdemeanour) in case of insanity; the CPP then requires the investigating judge (juge d'instruction, art. 286) or the indictment chamber (chambre d'accusation), sitting in chambers (chambre du conseil; arts. 303, 307), to declare that there are no grounds to prosecute. The CPP provides for neither a trial nor criminal-law committal: treatment outside the proceedings (case reported in 2026). Law 2016-017 does not affect these articles.

entities.name: Seychelles

facts.outcome: Ordinary trial, then special finding by the trial court (act committed but accused insane at the time of the offence: CP s.13, CPC s.138); detention as a “criminal lunatic” on the President's order (psychiatric hospital, prison or other safe place); admission to a mental health establishment and monitoring by the Tribunal (MHCA 2020 s.34), discharge on the order of the court or the President.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: at the preliminary inquiry the court proceeds even if insanity at the time of the offence is alleged (CPC s.137); the special finding is made only at trial (s.138).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: CPC s.136: if the court has reason to believe the accused is insane and incapable of making his defence, it holds an inquiry and may order one month's observation in a psychiatric hospital; if incapacity is found, the proceedings are adjourned and the accused is released on bail or detained on the President's order; resumption on a certificate of fitness (ss.139-140). No trial of the facts while he remains unfit. S.141: accused not insane but not understanding the proceedings: the court may proceed (referral to the Supreme Court if committal or conviction).

entities.name: Ghana

facts.outcome: At trial on indictment, the jury (or the court) returns a special verdict: act committed but accused insane (“guilty but insane”); the court orders custody as a “criminal lunatic” until the President's decision; the Minister may release, absolutely or conditionally, by warrant.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: insanity is a defence decided at trial on indictment (Act 30 s. 137); the 2012 Mental Health Act (s. 76) provides for assessment and treatment but presupposes a judicial finding of non-responsibility (s. 76(7)).

entities.name: Sierra Leone

facts.outcome: At trial, the Court finds that the accused committed the act but was insane and makes a “special finding” of non-guilt on grounds of insanity (not guilty by reason of insanity); it orders custody as a “criminal lunatic” and refers the matter to the Minister, who may order committal to a psychiatric hospital; annual report, review at least every 3 years, absolute or conditional discharge by the Minister.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: at the committal stage the court proceeds and commits the accused for trial even if insanity at the time of the offence is alleged (s. 69); the issue is decided at trial (s. 70).

entities.name: Liberia

facts.outcome: Criminal non-responsibility for mental disease or defect (Penal Law § 4.3), argued at the ordinary trial (Sheriff v. RL, 1981: conviction quashed in particular because the mental examination had not been carried out by a psychiatrist; the State bears the burden of proving sanity); the exact effect of the acquittal (committal, release) could not be read in the CPL.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None found: chapter 6 of the CPL deals only with present fitness to stand trial, and the chapters read (preliminary examination, grand jury, indictment, pleas) do not allow the case to be closed before trial for non-responsibility.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: CPL §§ 6.1-6.4: no one may be tried, convicted or punished while unable to understand the proceedings or to assist in his own defence; the court appoints at least one physician (observation in an institution for up to 5 days) and decides (hearing if the finding is contested); if unfit, the proceedings are suspended and the accused is committed to a psychiatric institution for as long as the incapacity lasts; resumption on application; discontinuance possible if resumption would be unjust; legal objections to the prosecution may be decided before trial (§ 6.4).

entities.legal_bases: Penal Law (Title 26 LCLR) § 4.3 “Mental disease or defect” (not § 4.1, which deals with immaturity); Criminal Procedure Law (Title 2 LCLR) ch. 6, §§ 6.1-6.4 (fitness to stand trial) and § 2.5(3)(b); Supreme Court, Sheriff v. RL, 29 LLR 103 (1981)

facts.outcome: Under the 1933 CPC: insanity defence decided at trial, special verdict “guilty but insane”, then committal to Tanka Tanka psychiatric hospital until the President's decision (Special Criminal Court, Anna Jatta case, 2013). The regime of the Criminal Procedure Act 2025 (Act No. 6 of 2025; art. 188 cited by the criminal statute) could not be read.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None according to the 1933 CPC and practice (special verdict after a full trial, with evidence and witnesses); the text of the Criminal Procedure Act 2025 has not been verified.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: CPC 1933 ss. 132-134 and 140 (headings only): accused apparently insane and incapable of making his defence, then procedure after certification of his capacity and resumption of the trial; content and regime of the 2025 act not verified.

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Procedure Act 2025 (Act No. 6 of 2025), art. 188 (not read); Criminal Offences Act (Criminal Offences Bill 2020, passed on 28 March 2025, stage “Assented” on the Assembly's website) ss. 9-10: presumption of sanity and non-responsibility of a person “of unsound mind”, s. 11(3) referring to art. 188 of the CPA; former Criminal Procedure Code 1933 (Act No. 26 of 1933), ss. 132-140 (headings only)
entities.excerpt: 135. Defence of lunacy. 136. Special verdict.
entities.note: Former regime verified: full trial, then special verdict “guilty but insane” and committal to Tanka Tanka until the President's decision (Jatta case, 2013). The Criminal Procedure Act 2025 (Act No. 6 of 2025), adopted in March 2025, probably replaces the CPC; its art. 188 could not be read. “Green” maintained, low confidence.

entities.name: Kenya

facts.outcome: special finding “guilty of the act … but insane” (s. 166(1) CPC) made by the High Court at the end of the trial; detention “at the President's pleasure” having been held unconstitutional, the court orders psychiatric committal and its review
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the High Court (judge sitting alone) rules on insanity at the end of the ordinary trial, after both parties' evidence.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: s. 162 CPC (routine mental assessment before plea in murder cases): if the accused is unfit, the proceedings are adjourned, with custody or treatment, then resume as soon as he is fit (ss. 163-164); s. 162(4)-(5) (presidential order) held unconstitutional; the 2026 bill provides for committal ordered by the court.

entities.legal_bases: Penal Code (Cap. 63) ss. 11-12; Criminal Procedure Code (Cap. 75) ss. 162-167 (s. 166 special finding; s. 167); Mental Health Act (Cap. 248); Constitution 2010 arts. 29, 50, 160; HCK: Republic v SOM [2018] eKLR; petition Isaac Ndegwa Kimaru & 4 others (Mrima J); Bor v DPP [2024] KEHC 4588 (KLR); Criminal Procedure Code (Amendment) Bill 2026 (NA Bill No. 11 of 2026)
entities.excerpt: the court shall make a special finding to the effect that the accused was guilty of the act or omission charged but was insane
entities.note: No pretrial gate: insanity, argued at trial, results in a special finding by the High Court. Ss. 166(2)-(7) and 167 (detention “at the President's pleasure”) have been held unconstitutional (SOM 2018; Mrima J; Bor 2024): the court itself orders committal and its review. The CPC 2026 bill (capped court-ordered committal) is at 1st reading.

entities.name: Uganda

facts.outcome: special finding “not guilty by reason of insanity” (s. 48 TIA) at the end of the trial, then custody on the minister's order; case law now entrusts the court with fixed-term detention for treatment, which it reviews and lifts
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the High Court rules on insanity at the end of the trial on indictment, by a special finding.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: s. 45 TIA: inquiry and adjournment; designation as a “criminal lunatic” by ministerial order (s. 45(5)) has been held unconstitutional; the courts order treatment under the Mental Health Act 2018 and resume the trial as soon as the accused is fit (s. 47); proceedings are permanently stayed only in cases of lasting unfitness (Omaka 2018).

entities.legal_bases: Penal Code Act s. 11; Trial on Indictments Act (Cap. 23) ss. 45-48 (s. 48 special finding) and s. 82(6) as modified by the Constitutional Court; Magistrates Courts Act; Mental Health Act 2018; Constitution arts. 28, 126, 274; CEHURD v AG (Const. Pet. No. 64 of 2011); Bushoborozi v Uganda (HC 2015); Uganda v Kachope (HC 2024)
entities.excerpt: Special finding of not guilty by reason of insanity
entities.note: No pretrial gate: the High Court decides insanity at trial by a special finding (s. 48 TIA). The ministerial decision on detention has been called into question: Bushoborozi (2015) and the Constitutional Court (CEHURD) entrust the court with fixed-term detention for treatment, reviewed periodically; practice remains uneven.

entities.name: Tanzania

facts.outcome: Special finding by the trial court: the accused committed the act but, by reason of his insanity, is not guilty (CPA s. 219(2)); mandatory detention as a “criminal lunatic” for violent offences punishable by death or at least 7 years (s. 219(3)), then reports to the minister (after 3 years, then every 2 years) and release on his decision (s. 219(4)-(6)).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the defence is announced at plea (s. 219(1)) or the court orders the examination during the trial (s. 220), then the trial continues until the special finding (Madaha procedure, according to the 1st pass).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: s. 216 CPA: if the accused appears insane, the prosecution first presents its evidence; if the charge is made out, inquiry into his mental state; if unfit to make his defence, finding, proceedings suspended and detention as a “criminal lunatic”; resumption of the trial on recovery (ss. 217-218). No full trial while he remains unfit.

entities.legal_bases: Penal Code (Cap. 16) s. 13 (three limbs: understanding, knowledge that the act is prohibited, control of the act); Criminal Procedure Act (Cap. 20) ss. 216-220 (s. 219: defence at plea, special finding, detention, release by the minister; s. 220: examination ordered during trial); Mental Health Act 2008; CAT: Miburo Mussa v R (2024); Republic v Madaha (procedure)
entities.excerpt: by reason of his insanity, is not guilty of the offence
entities.note: No pretrial gate: defence raised at plea (s. 219(1)) or examination ordered by the court (s. 220), then full trial and “special finding” by the trial court; a premature finding is quashed (Miburo Mussa, CAT 2024, according to the 1st pass). Text reviewed via CJAD (2008 ed.); TanzLII blocked to automated access, revised 2022 ed. not reopened. Zanzibar: see TZ-ZAN.

history.note: The insanity defence must be announced at plea (s. 219(1)); the court orders the examination (s. 220), then the parties produce their evidence and the High Court makes a special finding; a premature finding is quashed (Miburo Mussa, CAT 2024). Zanzibar (Penal Act and CPA 2018) not verified: no TZ-ZAN entry. Searches in Kiswahili not carried out.

entities.name: South Sudan

facts.outcome: Non-responsibility recognised by the Penal Code Act 2008, s. 34 (“unsoundness of mind”, permanent or temporary insanity); the procedural outcome (acquittal or special finding, custody) could not be verified for lack of access to the Code of Criminal Procedure Act 2008.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Not verified: the Code of Criminal Procedure Act 2008 (Act No. 5 of 2008) could not be read (unreadable PDF, Ministry of Justice portal blocked to automated access); default values with no probative value.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Not verified.

entities.legal_bases: Penal Code Act 2008 (Act No. 9 of 2008) s. 34; Code of Criminal Procedure Act 2008 (Act No. 5 of 2008), insanity provisions not read
entities.excerpt: appreciate the nature of his or her acts, or of controlling them by reason of permanent or temporary insanity or mental infirmity
entities.note: Only the Penal Code Act 2008 s. 34 was read: an act is not an offence when done by a person who could not appreciate or control their acts (permanent or temporary insanity). The Code of Criminal Procedure Act 2008 (who decides, at what stage, what hearing, what custody) remained unreadable (binary PDF; mojca.gov.ss blocked to automated access): classification impossible, white.

entities.name: South Africa

facts.outcome: verdict “not guilty by reason of mental illness or intellectual disability” (CPA s. 78(6)) + measure chosen by the judge: psychiatric hospitalisation (state patient), temporary detention in a prison health facility for lack of a bed, admission as an involuntary user (MHCA s. 37), conditional or unconditional release
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: only the trial court returns the verdict, after finding that the accused committed the act, if necessary by setting aside a conviction before sentence.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Expert examination under s. 79 ordered of the court's own motion or upon allegation (s. 77(1)); if the accused is unfit, the court competent to try the case may, in the accused's interest, receive the available evidence to determine whether they committed the act, then orders at its discretion (since De Vos, CC 2015, and Act 4/2017) hospitalisation, temporary detention, involuntary admission or release; trial possible if the accused becomes fit again (s. 77(7)).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Procedure Act 51 of 1977 (CPA) ss. 77, 78(1), (1A), (1B), (2)-(6), (8), 79; Criminal Matters Amendment Act 68 of 1998; Criminal Procedure Amendment Act 4 of 2017; Mental Health Care Act 17 of 2002 ss. 37, 41-47; De Vos NO v Minister of Justice and Constitutional Development (CC, 2015)
entities.excerpt: « If the court finds that the accused committed the act in question … the court shall find the accused not guilty » (CPA s. 78(6))
entities.note: No pretrial gate: if non-responsibility is alleged (by the prosecution or the defence) or appears to the court, the court must order the s. 79 expert examination; the trial court then finds that the accused committed the act and returns the verdict (s. 78(6)), on an uncontested report (s. 78(3)) or after adversarial evidence (s. 78(4)). Since Act 4/2017, the measure is chosen by the judge.

No gate: green.

entities.name: Namibia

facts.outcome: verdict “not guilty by reason of mental illness or mental defect” (CPA s. 78(6)) + mandatory detention in a psychiatric hospital or in prison “pending the signification of the decision of the President” (state patient, Mental Health Act 18 of 1973)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the trial court hears the evidence, finds that the accused committed the act, then returns the verdict (e.g. S v Hamutenya, 2021).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Expert examination under s. 79 (s. 77(1)); if the accused is unfit, mandatory detention in a psychiatric hospital or in prison pending the President's decision (s. 77(6), 1977 text not reformed as in South Africa), without examination of the facts; the accused cannot demand acquittal or conviction and may be tried if they become fit again (s. 77(7)).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Procedure Act 51 of 1977 (Namibian version) ss. 77, 78(1), (2), (6), 79; Mental Health Act 18 of 1973 (state patients); Criminal Procedure Act Repeal Act 14 of 2018 (repeals the Criminal Procedure Act 25 of 2004, never brought into force); Mental Health Bill (passed by the National Assembly on 9 June 2026)
entities.excerpt: « If the court finds that the accused committed the act in question … not guilty by reason of mental illness or mental defect » (CPA s. 78(6))
entities.note: Pre-1998 South African text: examination (ss. 77(1), 78(2), s. 79 panel) at the request of the prosecution or the defence, or of the court's own motion; the trial court hears the evidence, finds that the accused committed the act and returns the verdict (s. 78(6)); mandatory detention pending the President's decision. CPA 2004 repealed (2018). Mental Health Bill passed by the National Assembly on 9/6/2026, promulgation not verified.

entities.name: Botswana

facts.outcome: “Special finding” that the accused is “guilty of the act or omission charged” but was insane, returned by the trial court (CPEA s. 160(1)); custody as a “criminal lunatic” at the place fixed by the court (s. 160(2)), annual reports (s. 169), release by the President (s. 170).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the special finding is returned by the trial court at the end of the trial (CPEA s. 160); the defence is raised under a plea of not guilty (State v Mogampana, cited in legal scholarship).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: CPEA s. 158(1): the magistrate or judge who believes the accused to be insane and incapable of making a defence inquires into that condition; under the former text, deemed identical, proceedings stayed, bail or detention, referral to the High Court (s. 158(5)) and confinement “during his pleasure” by the President; no trial of the facts noted (s. 158(2)-(4) not read).

entities.legal_bases: Penal Code (Cap. 08:01) ss. 10-11; Criminal Procedure and Evidence Act (Cap. 08:02) ss. 158, 160, 169-170 (read only in a scholarly article, not in the official text); Act 13 of 2022 (amends only ss. 2-3 of the CPEA)
entities.excerpt: the court shall return a special finding to the effect that the accused was guilty of the act or omission charged
entities.note: No pretrial gate: the trial court returns the “special finding” (CPEA s. 160, worded “guilty of the act… but insane”), then orders custody; release by the President. Texts seen only via an article in the UB Law Journal (official text out of reach); Act No. 13 of 2022 amends only ss. 2-3 of the CPEA; who orders the expert examination not verified.

entities.name: Lesotho

facts.outcome: Insanity verdict (“verdict of insanity”) returned by the trial court if the accused proves their mental disorder (Penal Code Act 2010, s. 19(2)-(3)); detention under s. 172(3) CPEA 1981, “in some prison pending the signification of King's pleasure”, release left to the King on medical advice; periodic medical review required by the Constitutional Court (2014).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: full trial before the judge and assessors; the expert examination, ordered during the trial at the defence's request (Rex v Ralee, 2022), is ruled on in the judgment.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: CPEA s. 172 (“Trial of insane person”): if the accused cannot understand the proceedings, the court inquires into their insanity; in LSCA 1990/43, without a plea, evidence heard on the commission of the acts, then detention “pending the signification of His Majesty's pleasure”; text of s. 172 not read (judicial paraphrase).

entities.legal_bases: Penal Code Act 2010 (Act No. 6 of 2012) s. 19(1)-(3); Criminal Procedure and Evidence Act 1981 (Act No. 7 of 1981) ss. 166 (heading), 172(1)-(3); Constitutional Court, [2014] LSHC 1 (periodic review of detention)
entities.excerpt: Where proof of mental disorder is established, the court shall return a verdict of insanity and order the detention of the person
entities.note: The accused proves the disorder (balance of probabilities, PC s. 19(2)); the judge and assessors return the insanity verdict at the end of a full trial (Ralee 2022: expert examination ordered during the trial; 2006 special verdict under s. 172(3), cf. [2014] LSHC 1). Actual text of s. 172 CPEA not read (heading, cross-references and judicial paraphrases); who can compel the expert examination not verified.

entities.name: Eswatini

facts.outcome: Special finding that the accused “did the act charged but was insane”, returned by the High Court at the end of the trial (CPEA s. 165(1)); custody as a “criminal lunatic” ordered by the court, report to the Attorney-General for His Majesty (s. 165(2)); the King may order confinement “during His pleasure” (s. 165(3)).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the Crown proves the facts beyond reasonable doubt, the accused proves insanity (balance of probabilities); in 2013, s. 165 was applied on admitted facts and uncontested psychiatric reports.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Probably CPEA s. 163 (accused insane in the course of proceedings): detention “pending the signification of His Majesty's pleasure” (cross-reference in s. 86(3)); text not read; in Rex v Dlamini [2013] SZHC 46, reports from 2000 (unfit) and then 2010 (fit) precede a special finding in 2013.

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Procedure and Evidence Act 67 of 1938 ss. 163 (not read), 165(1)-(5), 86(3); case law: King v Chibi (SZHC 1989), King v Mngometulu (SZHC 1998), Mavimbela v Rex (SZSC 2012)
entities.excerpt: return a special finding to the effect that the accused did the act charged but was insane as aforesaid when he did it
entities.note: The High Court first tries the facts, then insanity, and returns the “special finding” (s. 165(1)); custody as a “criminal lunatic” with no margin of discretion (Chibi 1989; Mngometulu 1998). Supreme Court (Mavimbela 2012): the judge, not the expert, decides; s. 165 requires a finding of insanity. Only s. 165 (as cited in case law) was seen; s. 163 and recent reforms not verified.

entities.name: Zimbabwe

facts.outcome: special verdict “not guilty because of insanity” (MHA s. 29(2)) + return to prison for transfer to an institution (or special institution) for examination and treatment, treatment order, or release; oversight by a special board and the Mental Health Review Tribunal (ss. 29(4)-(6), 35)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the special verdict requires the judge or magistrate presiding at the trial to be satisfied, on the evidence produced at trial, that the accused committed the act.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Examination ordered before or during the trial (MHA ss. 26-28); if the accused can neither understand the proceedings nor make a defence, the judge so finds and orders placement in an institution (a special institution if dangerous) or, for minor offences, suspends the proceedings with treatment; no examination of the facts; prosecution possible after recovery (ss. 28(7), 28(11), 31(2)).

entities.legal_bases: Mental Health Act [Chapter 15:12] (Act 15 of 1996) ss. 26-29, 31, 35; Criminal Law (Codification and Reform) Act [Chapter 9:23] s. 18(4) and ch. XIV (mental disorder, s. 226 ff.)
entities.excerpt: « If a judge or magistrate presiding over a criminal trial is satisfied … return a special verdict … not guilty because of insanity » (MHA s. 29(2))
entities.note: No pretrial gate: a psychiatric examination may be ordered from the first appearance (MHA s. 26), but only the trial court returns the special verdict, on the evidence (including medical evidence) produced at trial and after finding that the accused committed the act. The verdict counts as an acquittal except for purposes of appeal (s. 29(10)). Burden of proving the disorder on the accused (CLC s. 18(4)).

entities.name: Zambia

facts.outcome: “Special finding” (CPC s. 167(1): not guilty by reason of insanity) returned by the trial court, then detention “during the President's pleasure” in a psychiatric hospital, prison or other suitable place (regime of ss. 163-164: reports at least every six months, release by the President; application to the special finding not re-verified).
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the special finding is returned at the end of the trial (CPC s. 167); the psychiatric examination is ordered by the court, when alerted or at the defence's request (People v Mwanza, 2002 referral; Kalonga 2018: examination refused at trial, conviction quashed, retrial).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: CPC s. 160: question decided as soon as it arises; if the accused is unfit, a plea of not guilty is entered and evidence heard (s. 161): acquittal if the evidence justifies neither conviction nor a special finding, otherwise detention “during the President's pleasure”, confirmed by the High Court (s. 162); trial de novo if the accused becomes fit again (s. 165). Mbaye (1975): no special finding for an accused found unfit.

entities.name: Malawi

facts.outcome: special finding “not guilty by reason of insanity” (CPEC s. 135(1)) + order for admission to a psychiatric hospital (reception order), with a possible prohibition on discharge without the Minister's consent (s. 135(2))
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: if the accused appears to be of sound mind at the preliminary inquiry, the inquiry continues despite the allegation of insanity (s. 134); the special finding is a matter for the trial court.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: If the court has reason to believe the accused incapable of making a defence: adjournment (1 month max.), observation and medical report, hearing on the report; if the accused is unfit, adjournment sine die and bail or admission to a psychiatric hospital (s. 133); resumption as soon as a doctor certifies them fit (ss. 133(6), 136); no examination of the facts.

entities.name: Philippines

facts.outcome: acquittal / exemption from criminal liability on grounds of insanity (art. 12(1) RPC) + confinement ordered by the trial court (NCMH), discharge with the permission of the same court; civil liability maintained (art. 101 RPC)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: the motion to quash (Rule 117 §3(h)) presupposes that the information itself alleges the excuse; insanity is decided at trial (reverse order possible, Rule 119 §11(e)).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Rule 116 §11(a): on motion of the party concerned, the arraignment is suspended, the court orders a mental examination and, if necessary, confinement (NCMH); trial resumed once the accused is fit (Bacolot 2018); if the incapacity persists, case archived (Admin. Circ. 7-A-92), with no trial of the facts; insanity after final conviction: execution suspended (art. 79 RPC).

entities.legal_bases: Revised Penal Code (Act No. 3815) arts. 12(1), 79, 101; Revised Rules of Criminal Procedure (2000) Rule 116 sec. 11(a), Rule 117 sec. 3(h), Rule 119 sec. 11(e), Rule 120 sec. 2; SC Administrative Circular No. 7-A-92 (archiving); People v. Paña, G.R. No. 214444 (17 Nov. 2020, En Banc); Verdadero v. People, G.R. No. 216021 (2 March 2016); People v. Bacolot, G.R. No. 233193 (10 Oct. 2018)
entities.excerpt: The burden of proving the affirmative allegation of insanity rests on the defense.
entities.note: No pretrial gate: insanity (art. 12(1) RPC) is a defence (confession and avoidance) that only the accused invokes and proves (clear and convincing evidence, Paña 2020); the RTC rules in its judgment after an ordinary trial and orders confinement. Caveat: the judge may order a mental examination (mainly for fitness); revision of the criminal procedure rules proposed, not adopted.

entities.name: Jordan

facts.outcome: judgment finding that the acts were committed (“إدانة”) and declaring criminal non-responsibility (إعلان عدم المسؤولية الجزائية) + committal to a psychiatric hospital until recovery is certified by a medical board (CP art. 92 para. 2)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the prosecution cannot close the case on grounds of insanity; non-responsibility is declared by the trial court at trial, after the facts have been established.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Art. 233 §3 CPP: unfit accused (does not understand the proceedings) → interlocutory decision keeping them in a psychiatric hospital, trial adjourned for them alone and resumed as soon as they are fit; if the illness is incurable, placement in a psychiatric hospital. Mental disability (§5): tried in the presence of the guardian or a court-appointed lawyer.

entities.legal_bases: CP (قانون العقوبات رقم 16 لسنة 1960) arts. 91-92; CPP (قانون أصول المحاكمات الجزائية رقم 9 لسنة 1961) art. 233 §1-5; Cass. (تمييز جزاء) 122/1972, 493/1996, 68/1999 (هيئة عامة), 436/2022; CP amending law No. 12/2025 (no bearing on art. 92)
entities.excerpt: فتقرر إعلان عدم مسؤوليته جزائياً وأعمال المادة (92) من قانون العقوبات بحقه
entities.note: No pretrial gate: the prosecutor places the suspect under medical supervision without halting the investigation (233 §1) and cannot issue a منع المحاكمة on grounds of insanity (Cass. 122/1972, 2026 scholarship). The trial court has the accused examined by 3 public-sector psychiatrists, finds that they committed the acts, then declares non-responsibility and orders committal (CP 92). Official text not consulted.

entities.name: Indonesia

facts.outcome: Putusan “lepas dari segala tuntutan hukum” (exemption from punishment) + tindakan, notably perawatan di rumah sakit jiwa, ordered by the court and executed by the prosecution
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No ground for SP3 or for dropping the prosecution on account of mental disorder; the penetapan under art. 146 KUHAP 2025 (public hearing) awaits a PP, not found.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No special procedure found: proceedings are deferred; art. 107(1)(a) KUHAP 2025 allows detention to be extended (2 × 30 days, then release as of right) if the suspect or accused cannot be examined owing to serious mental disorder; neither trial of the facts nor closure of the case is provided for.

entities.legal_bases: KUHP (UU 1/2023, in force 2.1.2026) Pasal 38, 39, 103 ayat (2)-(3), 110, 132; KUHAP (UU 20/2025, in force 2.1.2026) Pasal 24 ayat (2), 71 ayat (2), 107 ayat (1) huruf a, 146; transitional regime (cases opened before 2026): KUHP lama Pasal 44 and KUHAP UU 8/1981; Putusan MA No. 1115 K/Pid/2026
entities.excerpt: Tindakan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) ditetapkan dengan penetapan Hakim dalam sidang terbuka untuk umum.
entities.note: The court tries the merits, then pronounces “lepas” (KUHP art. 39) and orders the RSJ tindakan, executed by the prosecution (MA 1115 K/Pid/2026, murder, transitional KUHAP 1981); KUHP arts. 103(3), 110 tie the measure to the judgment. No ground for SP3 or for dropping the prosecution on account of mental disorder (KUHAP 2025 arts. 24, 71). Caveat: art. 146 KUHAP 2025, penetapan by the judge in a public hearing, details left to a PP.

entities.name: Mauritania

facts.outcome: Dismissal (non-lieu) by order of the investigating judge (juge d'instruction), the act committed in a state of insanity being “ni crime ni délit” (neither felony nor misdemeanour); no trial or judicial committal appears in the texts read.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: After the prosecutor's submissions, the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) declares by order that there are no grounds to prosecute if the facts constitute neither a felony nor a misdemeanour (CPP art. 177); the order is notified to the charged person (art. 183).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No specific provision found in the texts read.

entities.legal_bases: CP (Ordinance No. 83-162 of 9 July 1983) art. 58 (insanity: “ni crime ni délit” (neither felony nor misdemeanour)); CPP (Ordinance No. 83-163 revised by Ordinance No. 2007-036, JO No. 1143 of 15 May 2007; Codes usuels de Mauritanie, vol. 3) arts. 177 (dismissal (non-lieu): neither felony, nor misdemeanour, nor petty offence, or insufficient evidence), 183 (notification of dismissal orders), 206.
entities.excerpt: les faits ne constituent ni crime, ni délit, ni contravention [...] il déclare, par une ordonnance, qu'il n'y a pas lieu à poursuivre
entities.note: Combined reading: the CP states that there is “ni crime ni délit” (neither felony nor misdemeanour) in case of insanity (art. 58); the CPP then requires the investigating judge (juge d'instruction) to declare by order that there are no grounds to prosecute (art. 177), the order being notified to the charged person (art. 183). Neither a special trial nor judicial committal in the texts read. CPP read via Legal Data Hunter (official SGG compilation).

entities.name: Thailand

facts.outcome: Judgment after trial: the offender committed the act but is not subject to punishment (ป.อ. art. 65 para. 1, ground of exemption from punishment); dismissal of the charge if there is a legal ground for exemption (ป.วิ.อ. art. 185); the court may order custody in a care facility if release would be dangerous, an order revocable at any time (ป.อ. art. 48)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the trial court rules on art. 65 after hearing the facts and the psychiatric expert; a discontinuance (คำสั่งไม่ฟ้อง) by the prosecutor remains possible but excludes any art. 48 measure, which can be ordered only by the court.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: ป.วิ.อ. art. 14: the investigating officer or the court has the person examined by a doctor; if the person is insane and unable to make a defence, the investigation, preliminary examination or trial is suspended until recovery; possible referral to a psychiatric hospital or handover to a guardian; the court may provisionally strike out the case (จำหน่ายคดีชั่วคราว). No examination of the facts; custody potentially long.

entities.legal_bases: ประมวลกฎหมายอาญา (ป.อ.) ม. 65 para. 1 (exemption from punishment), ม. 48 (custody in a care facility, revocable court order); ประมวลกฎหมายวิธีพิจารณาความอาญา (ป.วิ.อ.) ม. 14 (unfitness: suspension, hospital, provisional striking out), ม. 185 (dismissal of the charge if there is a legal ground for exemption from punishment); พ.ร.บ.สุขภาพจิต พ.ศ. 2551 ม. 37-38 (report to the court every 180 days, lifting; cited in scholarship, text and 2562 amendment not read)
entities.excerpt: « ถ้าศาลเห็นว่า การปล่อยตัวผู้มีจิตบกพร่อง โรคจิตหรือจิตฟั่นเฟือน ซึ่งไม่ต้องรับโทษ » ; « ศาลจะสั่งให้ส่งไปคุมตัวไว้ในสถานพยาบาลก็ได้ » (ป.อ. ม. 48)
entities.note: No statutory pretrial gate: the trial court, after hearing the facts and the expert, exempts from punishment (ป.อ. 65) or dismisses the charge (ป.วิ.อ. 185) and may order hospital custody (ป.อ. 48). The prosecutor may discontinue the case (2015 scholarship), but without any art. 48 measure: in serious cases, the ordinary route is trial. Texts read via scholarship; no adopted reform identified (2025).
