entities.name: Malaysia

facts.outcome: Acquittal on grounds of insanity (Penal Code s. 84) pronounced by the trial court, which finds that the accused committed the act; safe custody ordered by the court, in a psychiatric hospital (Hospital Bahagia), “at the pleasure of” the Ruler (CPC s. 348); release at the Ruler's discretion, with no fixed duration
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: even when the psychiatric observation report concludes that the accused was insane at the time of the acts, the case is tried; the High Court may acquit at the close of the prosecution evidence (Federal Court, Pang Kar Foong, 26.8.2026).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: From the first appearance, the court orders one month's psychiatric observation at Hospital Bahagia (CPC s. 342, applied in 2025, at the prosecution's request); an accused found fit is then tried. Regime for persistent unfitness (adjournment, custody with report to the Ruler, resumption of trial; ss. 342-346) not read in the text.

entities.legal_bases: Penal Code (Act 574) / Kanun Keseksaan s. 84; Criminal Procedure Code (Act 593) / Kanun Tatacara Jenayah ch. XXXIII: s. 342 (psychiatric observation), s. 347 (special finding, text not read), s. 348 (custody at the Ruler's pleasure, applied by the Federal Court on 26.8.2026); federal laws, nationwide rule; Mental Health Act 2001 (Act 615) not examined
entities.excerpt: « the accused in this case is to be kept in safe custody at the pleasure of the Sultan » (Cour fédérale, 2026)
entities.note: No pretrial gate: despite an observation report (CPC s. 342) concluding that the accused was insane at the time of the acts, the case is tried; the trial court acquits (PC s. 84), here at the close of the prosecution case, and orders custody at the Ruler's pleasure (s. 348): Federal Court, Pang Kar Foong, 26.8.2026. CPC text not read (press only), hence medium confidence.

entities.name: Pakistan

facts.outcome: Acquittal on grounds of insanity (CrPC s. 470) with an express finding as to whether or not the accused committed the act; if they did, safe custody ordered by the trial judge with a report to the provincial government (s. 471), carried out in a secure psychiatric facility (provincial Mental Health Acts)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: if the accused, being fit, appears to have been insane at the time of the acts, “the Magistrate or Court shall proceed with the case” (s. 469, 1972 wording) and the Sessions Court decides the art. 84 question after the trial, the burden of proof lying on the accused.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: The magistrate (s. 464) or the Sessions Court (s. 465, question tried first, as part of the trial) rules on the present capacity to make a defence; medical examination mandatory (Fauqual Bashar 1997; medical boards required by Safia Bano 2021); if unfit: finding and outright postponement, without examination of the facts; release on security or safe custody with report to the government (s. 466); resumption when the accused becomes fit again (ss. 467-468, 473); custody potentially indefinite.

entities.legal_bases: PPC 1860 s. 84; CrPC 1898 ch. XXXIV ss. 464-475 (464-466 fitness and custody; 469 substituted by the Law Reforms Ordinance 1972; 470 acquittal with finding; 471 safe custody); Sindh Mental Health Act 2013 ss. 2(o), 54-55 and KP Mental Health Act 2017 ss. 2(o), 48-49 (refer to ss. 466 and 471, without affecting responsibility); Pakistan Prison Rules r. 440-444; Safia Bano, PLD 2021 SC 488
entities.excerpt: the Magistrate or Court shall proceed with the case. […] the finding shall state specifically whether he committed the act or not.
entities.note: No pretrial gate: if insanity at the time of the acts appears probable, the judge proceeds with the case (s. 469); the Sessions Court acquits after an ordinary trial, makes a finding on the act (s. 470) and orders safe custody (s. 471). Concurrent competence (art. 142): Mental Health Acts Sindh 2013 and KP 2017 without effect; Punjab, Balochistan not read. Senate bill (terminology): adoption not verified.

entities.name: Nepal

facts.outcome: Exemption from criminal responsibility (“आरोपित कसुरबाट उन्मुक्ति”) declared by the trial judge after trial (Penal Code 2074 art. 14); no criminal committal measure found in the texts read (the Supreme Court merely states that a mentally ill person must be treated, not punished)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the indictment filed by the prosecutor (सरकारी वकिल) brings the case before the district court, which decides the insanity defence in its judgment on the merits, subject to review by the High Court and the Supreme Court.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Criminal Procedure Code 2074 art. 128: examination and treatment by a doctor on the court's order; if the accused cannot defend themselves, adjournment by order; handover to a guardian under an undertaking, or special care in prison; trial resumed after a medical certificate of recovery; co-accused may be tried; no examination of the facts during the adjournment.

entities.legal_bases: मुलुकी अपराध संहिता, २०७४ (Penal Code) दफा १४; मुलुकी फौजदारी कार्यविधि संहिता, २०७४ (Criminal Procedure Code) ch. 13, दफा १२७-१२९ (order of evidence, insane accused, public hearing); former मुलुकी ऐन, दण्ड सजायको महल १ नं.; Supreme Court: NKP 2065 dec. no. 7988, NKP 2073 dec. no. 9672, NKP 2079 dec. no. 10931
entities.excerpt: कुनै काम गर्दाका बखत मानसिक अस्वस्थताको कारणले त्यस्तो कामको प्रकृति, गुण, दोष वा परिणाम बुझ्न नसक्ने गरी
entities.note: No pretrial gate: the prosecutor brings the case before the district court, which rules on insanity (art. 14) in its judgment after an ordinary trial, on the basis of a court-ordered expert examination; proof “beyond doubt” borne by the defence. Decisions read mostly under the former Muluki Ain; full text of art. 14 not read (PDFs unreadable); no criminal committal measure found.

entities.name: Bhutan

facts.outcome: Exoneration for mental disorder (PC ss. 118-119); if the accused is found “clinically insane”, civil commitment to a hospital or psychiatric institution ordered by the court instead of imprisonment (s. 25), if it promotes rehabilitation without threatening public safety (s. 27), with possible civil compensation (s. 26)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the preliminary hearing (CCPC s. 190) only checks that there is sufficient cause to prosecute; the defence under art. 119 is examined at trial and decided in the judgment (s. 96).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No specific procedure found in the CCPC 2001: only a general adjournment of up to 60 days for a “mentally unsound” party on a medical certificate (s. 76.1(g)) and verification of mental competence before a guilty plea or a plea bargain (ss. 195, 197.3); 2011 and 2021 amendments not read.

entities.legal_bases: Penal Code of Bhutan 2004 (amended 2011) ss. 25-27 (civil commitment instead of imprisonment), 118 (permanent mental incapacity), 119 (mental disorder defence); Civil and Criminal Procedure Code of Bhutan 2001 ss. 76.1(g), 96, 190, 195, 197.3; CCPC (Amendment) Acts 2011 and 2021 not read
entities.excerpt: If a defendant is found to be clinically insane […] a Court shall, in lieu of imprisonment, order the civil commitment of the defendant
entities.note: No pretrial gate: the preliminary hearing (CCPC s. 190) checks only for “sufficient cause”; the mental disorder defence (PC s. 119) is decided by the district court in its judgment after trial (Lekden D. Dorji case, 2025, upheld in 2026); if the accused is found insane, the court orders civil commitment instead of prison (s. 25). CCPC Amendment 2021 not read.

entities.name: Taiwan

facts.outcome: Discontinuance (不起訴) because the act is not punishable (CP §19 I), then a court order (裁定), on the prosecutor's application, imposing 監護 (CP §87: placement or appropriate care); concurrent route for homicides: trial, acquittal (無罪) and 監護 imposed in the judgment.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: After the 不起訴, the court rules by order on the measure alone: summons, court-appointed lawyer in case of disability, views of the parties (CPP §481-3 to §481-5, applicable via §481-7 since 2022).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Not verified (official portal blocked, from memory): CPP §294, trial suspended until the recovery of an accused unable to understand the proceedings, judgment possible in the accused's absence if acquittal is clearly warranted; provisional placement (暫行安置, CPP §121-1 ff., 2022) possible.

entities.excerpt: 檢察官依刑法…第十九條第一項而為不起訴之處分者，如認有宣告保安處分之必要，得聲請法院裁定之。
entities.note: The prosecutor orders an expert examination; on finding abolished discernment (CP §19 I), the prosecutor discontinues the case (不起訴) and may ask the court to impose 監護 by order (CPP §481 II); since 2022: hearing, court-appointed lawyer in case of disability (§481-3, §481-5, §481-7). Serious homicide cases are nevertheless tried and end in acquittal with 監護 (police officer killed in Chiayi, 2020). No statistics found on the dominant route; official portals blocked.

entities.name: Hong Kong

facts.outcome: Special verdict “not guilty by reason of insanity” returned by the jury at trial (CPO s. 74), then court order (s. 76): committal (Siu Lam Psychiatric Centre or psychiatric hospital), guardianship order, supervision and treatment order or absolute discharge.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: no pretrial gate; insanity is decided by the jury at the ordinary trial before the Court of First Instance.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Question raised by the defence or otherwise, decided by a jury as soon as it arises, postponement possible (CPO s. 75); if unfit, the same jury determines only whether the accused did the act (s. 75A, trial of facts), otherwise acquittal; then an order under s. 76 (e.g. committal to Siu Lam, Ng Mei Lan 2009).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap. 221) ss. 74, 75, 75A, 76 and Schedule 4; Mental Health Ordinance (Cap. 136) Parts IIIA and IIIB (guardianship, supervision and treatment); M'Naghten Rules (common law)
entities.excerpt: the jury shall return a special verdict
entities.note: No pretrial gate: in homicide cases, jury trial (Court of First Instance); the jury returns the special verdict (s. 74), the accused proving insanity (M'Naghten) on the balance of probabilities; the court chooses the measure (s. 76). Power of the prosecution or the judge to raise insanity not verified (otherwise “blue”). Official portals blocked; recent reforms not verified.

entities.name: Macao

facts.outcome: Judgment of the court (collegiate bench) declaring the arguido non-imputable (不可歸責, CP art. 19.º n.º 1) and ordering their committal (收容) to a care, treatment or security establishment (CP art. 83.º), for at least 3 years for a crime against the person or of common danger punishable by more than 5 years.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: None: the prosecution (Ministério Público) indicts, applying for the security measure, and the court rules after the trial hearing (TSI 338/2008).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No specific rule identified; a mental anomaly that comes to light after judgment falls to the sentence-enforcement judge (CP arts. 96.º-97.º, TSI 49/2018); the trial judge may have the mental state examined at the hearing (CPP art. 332.º, cited by TSI 1015/2009, not re-read).

entities.legal_bases: CP de Macau (刑法典) arts. 19.º n.º 1, 83.º, 96.º, 97.º; CPP de Macau (刑事訴訟法典) arts. 332.º (cited, not re-read), 400.º
entities.excerpt: 法院須命令將之收容於康復場所、治療場所或保安處分場所。
entities.note: The prosecution (Ministério Público) investigates and indicts, applying for committal; the collegiate court holds the trial hearing in the presence of the accused, hears the psychiatrist, declares non-imputability (CP art. 19) and orders 收容 (art. 83): TSI 338/2008 (arson). Discontinuance for non-imputability not verified; BO portal blocked, CPP not re-read, 2024-2026 reforms not verified.

entities.name: Guam

facts.outcome: acquittal on the ground of mental illness, disease or defect (jury verdict or judge's finding), then release, conditional release or committal ordered by the court
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: the affirmative defence pleaded or notified by the accused is decided at the ordinary unitary trial (jury or judge alone), without a bifurcated trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Raised by a party or by the court of its own motion; the judge rules without a jury on the basis of an expert examination; proceedings suspended and treatment (six-monthly reports) if fitness may be restored; otherwise charges dropped and release or civil commitment (10 GCA ch. 82).

entities.legal_bases: 9 GCA §§ 7.16 (test), 7.22 (affirmative defence, plea or notice by the accused), 7.25 (expert examination), 7.31 (reasoned verdict), 7.34 (measure); 9 GCA §§ 7.37, 7.40, 7.43 (unfitness); 10 GCA ch. 82
entities.excerpt: The defendant shall plead not guilty by reason of mental illness, disease or defect, or shall give notice
entities.note: Affirmative defence (ALI test, § 7.16) proved by the accused (preponderance). Only the accused pleads it or gives notice of it within 10 days after arraignment, which triggers the court-ordered expert examination (§§ 7.22, 7.25). Decided at a unitary trial (jury or judge); the verdict states the ground, then the court rules on committal (§ 7.34). Texts unchanged: P.L. 38-094 (2026) concerns only § 7.58.

entities.name: Northern Mariana Islands

facts.outcome: judgment “not guilty by reason of mental illness, disease or defect”, release as for any acquitted person, civil commitment possible in separate proceedings
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: the affirmative defence, raised by the NGRI plea or the defence's notice, is decided at trial, which ends in a reasoned judgment of acquittal.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Motion by a party or of the court's own motion; proceedings suspended, expert examination, decision by the judge without a jury; committal for 30-day periods if fitness may be restored; otherwise unconditional release and charges dropped (6 CMC §§ 6603, 6606-6607).

entities.legal_bases: 6 CMC § 252 (affirmative defence); 6 CMC § 6602 (test); § 6604 (expert examination on NGRI plea or notice); § 6605 (release after NGRI judgment, civil commitment); §§ 6603, 6606-6607 (unfitness); Com. R. Crim. P. (notice)
entities.excerpt: Mental illness, disease or defect, precluding responsibility, is an affirmative defense.
entities.note: 1993 Act (PL 8-37): affirmative defence (§ 252; ALI test, § 6602) raised by an NGRI plea or by notice from the accused, which triggers the court-ordered expert examination (§ 6604). Decided at trial; after acquittal, release as for any acquitted person, civil commitment possible (§ 6605). Caveat: every expert report, even on fitness, addresses the mental state at the time of the offence. Notice rule not read.

facts.outcome: verdict “not guilty by reason of insanity” at trial, then committal ordered and supervised by the court (if necessary outside the territory, e.g. at the Hawaii State Hospital)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route identified: the defence notified by the accused is decided at trial (NGRI verdict), but §§ 46.1307-46.1310 could not be read.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Expert examination ordered of the court's own motion or on motion, then decision by the judge; the unfit accused is held at the correctional facility for up to 120 days (A.S.C.A. § 46.1305; Taylor, 1990); beyond that, civil commitment possible; outcome of the prosecution not verified.

entities.name: Tokelau

facts.outcome: acquittal (prohibition on convicting an insane person); no committal measure provided for by the 2003 Rules
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: after the Commissioner's preliminary hearing, insanity is decided at trial by the High Court judge sitting alone.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No provision in the 2003 Rules (only refusal to plead is dealt with, r. 131(3)); the judge would rule case by case under the residual rule of Part 4, with New Zealand practice able to supplement the procedure.

entities.legal_bases: Crimes, Procedure and Evidence Rules 2003 (Tokelau): r. 116(1) (insanity, presumption of sanity), r. 112(9) (exclusive jurisdiction of the High Court), r. 129 (committal for trial), r. 131(3), r. 135 (trial before a judge alone), r. 153, residual rule of Part 4; Tokelau Amendment Act 1986 (jurisdiction of the High Court, cited by McGovern)
entities.excerpt: No person shall be convicted of an offence if at the time of the commission of the offence that person was insane
entities.note: Murder: exclusive jurisdiction of the High Court (r. 112(9)) after a preliminary hearing (r. 129); trial before a judge alone (r. 135), who may not convict an insane person, presumed sane until the contrary is proved (r. 116). Nothing on expert examination, special verdict, committal or unfitness; New Zealand practice may fill the gaps. 2005 consolidation: later amendments not verified.

entities.name: Pitcairn Islands

facts.outcome: special verdict “not guilty by reason of insanity” returned by the judge alone (English law applied), then English-law measures (hospital order, supervision order, absolute discharge) subject to local adaptation
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No pretrial route: the question would be decided at trial by the Supreme Court judge sitting alone, under the applicable English law.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: No local text: English law (CP(I)A 1964 ss. 4-4A: judge's decision on fitness, then examination of the facts) would apply without a jury; the Judicature Ordinance mentions “inquiries into fitness to stand trial” (s. 2). No known practice.

entities.legal_bases: Constitution of Pitcairn 2010, s. 42 (English law); Judicature (Courts) Ordinance (Cap. 2), ss. 2, 9(1), 17(3); Justice (Persons of Unsound Mind) Amendment Ordinance 2025 (repealing Justice Ordinance ss. 5(1)(a)(v) and 75); via s. 42: Trial of Lunatics Act 1883 s. 2, Criminal Procedure (Insanity) Act 1964
entities.excerpt: the jury shall return a special verdict that the accused is not guilty by reason of insanity
entities.note: No ordinance on insanity: the Constitution (s. 42) applies the common law and English statutes of general application so far as local circumstances permit. The Supreme Court tries cases without a jury (s. 9(1)) following English practice (s. 17(3)): the 1883 special verdict would be returned by the judge at trial. The 2025 Ordinance repeals s. 75 (civil commitment). No case law.

entities.name: Norfolk Island

facts.outcome: acquittal for mental impairment (verdict of the jury or the judge), then detention pending a decision of the Mental Health Tribunal or a treatment order (serious offence)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No mandatory pretrial route; sole consensual exception: plea of not guilty on the ground of mental impairment, which the Supreme Court accepts with the prosecution's consent (s. 30).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Raised by a party or the judge: expert examination, then decision of the Mental Health Tribunal (s. 18); if fitness cannot be restored within 12 months, special hearing conducted like an ordinary trial (jury, or judge alone) on whether the act is proved beyond reasonable doubt (ss. 23-25), then detention or a treatment order (ss. 26-27).

entities.legal_bases: Criminal Procedure Act 2007 (NI), compilation no. 5 of 10 July 2021, ch. 2: ss. 8, 16, 18-28 (unfitness, special hearing), 29 (acquittal for mental impairment), 30 (plea accepted with the prosecution's consent), 31-33 (verdicts, orders); Mental Health Act 1996 (NI); Norfolk Island Continued Laws Ordinance 2015
entities.excerpt: entitled to be acquitted of an indictable offence on the grounds of mental impairment
entities.note: NSW lead ruled out: the Criminal Procedure Act 2007 (NI), a law continued in force after 2016 (2021 compilation), governs the matter. Acquittal for mental impairment at trial, by jury or judge (ss. 29, 31); the prosecution may raise it only with leave (s. 29(4)). Consensual route: plea accepted if the prosecution consents (s. 30). Then detention pending a decision of the Mental Health Tribunal (s. 33).

entities.name: Kazakhstan

facts.outcome: court order (постановление) releasing from criminal responsibility + compulsory medical measure (forced treatment in a psychiatric hospital)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: After a mandatory preliminary investigation, the prosecutor refers the case to the district court (single judge), which hears it under the general rules of the Code, in a public and adversarial hearing, and rules by order.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Mental illness arising after the act: same procedure under chapter 54 (release from responsibility or from punishment + medical measure); on recovery, the court lifts the measure and returns the case to the prosecutor for prosecution under the general procedure (art. 524 УПК).

entities.excerpt: По поступлении в суд дела о применении принудительных мер медицинского характера судья назначает его к рассмотрению в судебном заседании по правилам, предусмотренным настоящим Кодексом.
entities.note: Investigator, then prosecutor, send the case to the district court (single judge, art. 519). Hearing under the general rules of the Code, in public (art. 29), defence counsel and legal representative mandatory; the person takes part in the evidence and arguments unless the expert examination rules this out. The judge verifies the act, the perpetrator and non-responsibility (“признав доказанным”), and rules by постановление. Practice not verified.

entities.name: Mongolia

facts.outcome: judgment of the first-instance criminal court closing the case (хэрэгсэхгүй болгох) without penalty + compulsory medical measure (forensic psychiatric clinic)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No replacement procedure: indictment and trial under the ordinary procedure, with chapter 19 of the procedure law only adding special rules (19.1.1).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Mental illness arising after the act also falls under chapter 19 (19.1.1): the court may try the case without the defendant, represented by a legal representative and defence counsel (34.9.4), and order a medical measure; suspension and resumption after recovery not verified.

entities.excerpt: Шүүх хуралдаанаар шүүгдэгч гэмт хэрэг үйлдсэнийг нотолж байгаа, эсхүл үгүйсгэж байгаа нотлох баримтыг шалгаж, түүний сэтгэцийн өвчний талаар гаргасан шинжээчийн дүгнэлтийг сонсож…

facts.replacement_procedure_detail: After the discontinuance, the preliminary-chamber judge rules on the measure in chambers (prosecutor present, person heard with counsel, expert examination), by an încheiere open to challenge.

No trial: art. 18 covers non-imputability, but art. 319 only opens a different discontinuance to the suspect. If established at trial: acquittal (not read).

entities.name: Albania

facts.outcome: Proceedings cannot begin and must cease at any stage if the person is not criminally responsible: discontinuance (pushim) by the prosecutor during the investigation, or a pushim decision by the court; only a court can impose the compulsory medical measure.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The prosecutor decides the pushim of the case where the person is not criminally responsible (KPP arts. 290, 1, b, and 328) and asks the court for compulsory medical treatment (KP art. 46), without a trial on the merits (Fier case, 2021).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: If a supervening mental illness prevents participation, the proceedings are suspended (pezullim, KPP arts. 43-46), with medical measures possible.

entities.legal_bases: KP arts. 17 (papërgjegjshmëria) and 46 (mjekimi i detyruar, decided by the court); KPP (ligji no. 7905 of 21/03/1995, text indexed on qbz.gov.al) art. 290, 1, b (proceedings cannot begin and must cease at any stage if the person is not criminally responsible), art. 328 (pushimi i çështjes by the prosecutor), art. 387 (the court's vendimi i pushimit), arts. 43-46.

entities.note: The KPP prohibits initiating or continuing proceedings against a person who is not criminally responsible, at any stage (art. 290, 1, b): the prosecutor discontinues the case (pushim, art. 328) and asks the court for the medical measure, which only a court can impose (KP art. 46). facts.outcome: Court aktvendim finding that the act was committed in a state of paaftësi mendore and imposing the masa e trajtimit të detyrueshëm psikiatrik (me ndalim in a health institution or në liri), without penalty.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: Instead of an aktakuzë, the prosecutor files a propozim for a measure; the court panel holds a shqyrtim gjyqësor (witnesses, expert, accused and defence counsel present), then delivers an aktvendim pronounced publicly and open to appeal.

entities.name: Sri Lanka

facts.outcome: acquittal on grounds of insanity (verdict specifying whether the act was committed) + safe custody ordered by the trial court, then committal on the Minister's order (in practice the forensic unit of the NIMH, Angoda)
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: No replacement procedure: criminal non-responsibility is decided by the verdict of the jury or the High Court judge at the end of the ordinary trial.
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: If the accused appears, by reason of their disorder, incapable of making a defence, the jury or the High Court judge first decides that issue (s. 375(1) CCPA; s. 374 for the Magistrate) and the trial is adjourned; custody or committal to a psychiatric hospital on the Minister's order (s. 376(2), referred to in the Mental Diseases Ordinance s. 33(c)); trial resumes once the accused is fit, with no determination of the facts in the meantime (ss. 374 and 376-377 not read in full).

entities.legal_bases: Penal Code (Ord. No. 2 of 1883) s. 77; Code of Criminal Procedure Act No. 15 of 1979 (CCPA), chapter “accused persons of unsound mind”, ss. 374-381 (s. 375(1) unfitness to stand trial; s. 376(2) committal on ministerial order; s. 380 acquittal verdict; s. 381(1)-(2) safe custody and orders of the Minister); Evidence Ordinance s. 105; Mental Diseases Ordinance (1873) ss. 9-10, 33(c)
entities.excerpt: Whenever any person is acquitted … by reason of unsoundness of mind … the verdict shall state specifically whether he committed the act or not.
entities.note: No pretrial filter: insanity (s. 77 PC) is pleaded at the ordinary trial before the High Court (jury or judge), burden of proof on the accused (s. 105 EO); the acquittal verdict states whether the act was committed (s. 380 CCPA), followed by safe custody and orders of the Minister (s. 381). Mental illness arising after the offence and precluding punishment: same ch. 39 procedure with medical measures; after recovery, closure and ordinary procedure, punishment becomes possible again (art. 19 ч. 3 КК, art. 513 ч. 5 КПК).

entities.excerpt: Судовий розгляд здійснюється одноособово суддею в судовому засіданні за участю прокурора, […] обов’язковою участю фізичної особи, стосовно якої вирішується питання про застосування примусових заходів
entities.note: Territory under Kyiv's control. Expert examination imposed by the investigator/prosecutor (art. 509); application to the court instead of an indictment; the court holds a судовий розгляд under the general rules (single judge, mandatory presence, counsel), establishes the act and its perpetrator (art. 513), and rules by ухвала. Nuances: no panel and no jury; texts read on mirror sites; no martial-law reform found.

entities.name: Moldova

facts.outcome: sentinţă of the first-instance court absolving from criminal responsibility (art. 23 CP) + coercive measure of a medical nature (psychiatric committal, e.g. under strict supervision); if no danger: termination of the trial without a measure
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: On the prosecutor's committal order (art. 495 CPP), the first-instance court tries the case at a hearing under the general trial rules (art. 497), verifies the evidence and rules by sentinţă (art. 499).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: Mental illness arising after the offence (art. 23 para. 2 CP, art. 488 ff. CPP): same special procedure, medical measure without a penalty being set; after recovery, revocation and referral back to the prosecutor for the prosecution to resume, time in hospital credited against the sentence; hearing without the person concerned if the illness prevents attendance (art. 496).

entities.legal_bases: CP RM art. 23 (iresponsabilitatea), arts. 99-100, 102 (măsuri de constrângere cu caracter medical); CPP RM (Legea nr. 122/2003) arts. 488-503, in particular art. 495 alin. (1) pct. 2 (ordonanța procurorului de trimitere în judecată), art. 496 (judecare în absență dacă boala împiedică prezentarea), art. 497 alin. (1)-(2), art. 498, art. 499 alin. (1) (sentinţă de absolvire); Hotărârea Plenului CSJ nr. 23/2005 (amended 2018).
entities.excerpt: judecarea cauzelor trimise instanței în baza art.495 […] se face în ședință de judecată, potrivit dispozițiilor din Partea specială titlul II cap. I şi III
entities.note: After an expert examination during the urmărire penală, the prosecutor sends the case by ordonanţă (art. 495 CPP) to the 1st-instance court, which tries it under the general trial rules (art. 497: defence counsel mandatory, evidence verified) and, if it holds proven that the act was committed in a state of non-responsibility, absolves by sentinţă + medical measure (art. 499). Nuance: hearing without the person concerned if their illness prevents attendance (art. 496).

entities.name: United Arab Emirates

facts.outcome: Dismissal by the prosecution after investigation (“dismissal with prejudice”) based on insanity or a serious mental disorder, or acquittal by the court; in both cases, placement in a care facility ordered by the prosecution or the court until a discharge decision.
facts.replacement_procedure_detail: The prosecution closes the case by a dismissal (art. 118; in felony matters, by an advocate general with the approval of the Attorney General) and itself orders placement in a care facility (art. 188).
facts.unfitness_to_stand_trial: If the accused cannot defend themselves (insanity, mental disorder, weakness), the investigation or trial is suspended until the cause ceases, with placement on the order of the prosecution or the court (art. 186); duration credited against the sentence (art. 187).

entities.legal_bases: Federal Decree-Law No. 31 of 2021 (Crimes and Penalties Law) arts. 62 (no criminal responsibility in case of loss of perception or will due to insanity or mental deficiency), 134, 138, 140 and 142 (placement in a therapeutic facility, six-monthly reports, release by the court); Federal Decree-Law No. 38 of 2022 (criminal procedure, in force from 1/3/2023) arts. 118, 120, 185-188.
entities.excerpt: If a dismissal with prejudice order is issued or a judgment of acquittal is rendered in favor of the Defendant on grounds of insanity
entities.note: After the investigation, the prosecution may issue a dismissal (“dismissal with prejudice”, art. 118; in felony matters, an advocate general with the approval of the Attorney General). If it rests on insanity or a serious mental disorder, the prosecution itself orders placement in a care facility until a discharge decision (art. 188); same rule for acquittal.
